  41: const MACOS_PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE: &str = "rustynet.wg_passphrase";
  42: const MAX_PASSPHRASE_BYTES: usize = 4096;
  43: const WG_BINARY_PATH_ENV: &str = "RUSTYNET_WG_BINARY_PATH";
  44: #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
  45: const IP_BINARY_PATH_ENV: &str = "RUSTYNET_IP_BINARY_PATH";
  46: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
  47: const IFCONFIG_BINARY_PATH_ENV: &str = "RUSTYNET_IFCONFIG_BINARY_PATH";
  48: #[cfg(not(windows))]
  49: const DEFAULT_WG_BINARY_PATH: &str = "/usr/bin/wg";
  50: #[cfg(windows)]
  51: const DEFAULT_WG_BINARY_PATH: &str = r"C:\Program Files\WireGuard\wg.exe";
  52: #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
  53: const DEFAULT_IP_BINARY_PATH: &str = "/usr/sbin/ip";
  54: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
  55: const DEFAULT_IFCONFIG_BINARY_PATH: &str = "/sbin/ifconfig";
  56: #[cfg(windows)]
  57: const WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b"RNYDPAPI";
  58: #[cfg(windows)]
  59: const WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_VERSION: u8 = 1;
  60: #[cfg(windows)]
  61: const WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_DESCRIPTION: &str = "RustyNet WireGuard passphrase";
  62: 
  63: pub fn read_passphrase_file(path: &Path) -> Result<Zeroizing<String>, String> {
  64:     #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
  65:     if let Some(account) = resolve_macos_keychain_account_from_env()? {
  66:         return read_passphrase_from_macos_keychain(&account);
  67:     }
  68:     #[cfg(windows)]
  69:     {
  70:         return read_windows_runtime_passphrase_source(path);
  71:     }
  72:     #[cfg(not(windows))]
  73:     {
  74:         let source_path = resolve_passphrase_source(path)?;
  75:         read_passphrase_from_source(&source_path)
  76:     }
  77: }
  78: 
  79: pub fn read_passphrase_file_explicit(path: &Path) -> Result<Zeroizing<String>, String> {
  80:     #[cfg(windows)]
  81:     {
  82:         read_windows_explicit_passphrase_source(path)
  83:     }
  84:     #[cfg(not(windows))]
  85:     {
  86:         read_passphrase_from_source(path)
  87:     }
  88: }
  89: 
  90: pub fn store_passphrase_in_os_secure_store(
  91:     passphrase_path: &Path,
  92:     keychain_account: Option<&str>,
  93: ) -> Result<(), String> {
  94:     #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
  95:     {
  96:         let account = match keychain_account {
  97:             Some(value) => normalize_macos_keychain_account(value)?,
  98:             None => resolve_macos_keychain_account_from_env()?.ok_or_else(|| {
  99:                 format!(
 100:                     "missing {PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT_ENV}; configure a macOS keychain account for passphrase custody"
 101:                 )
 102:             })?,
 103:         };
 104:         let passphrase = read_passphrase_file_explicit(passphrase_path)?;
 105:         store_macos_generic_password(
 106:             MACOS_PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE,
 107:             account.as_str(),
 108:             passphrase.as_bytes(),
 109:         )
 110:         .map_err(|err| format!("store macOS keychain passphrase failed: {err}"))?;
 111:         Ok(())
 112:     }
 113:     #[cfg(windows)]
 114:     {
 115:         if keychain_account.is_some() {
 116:             return Err(
 117:                 "Windows passphrase secure-store provisioning does not accept --keychain-account"
 118:                     .to_string(),
 119:             );
 120:         }
 121:         let passphrase = read_passphrase_file_explicit(passphrase_path)?;
 122:         store_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(passphrase_path, passphrase.as_bytes())
 123:     }
 124:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
 125:     #[cfg(not(windows))]
 126:     {
 127:         let _ = (passphrase_path, keychain_account);
 128:         Err("passphrase secure-store provisioning is only supported on macOS".to_string())
 129:     }
 130: }
 131: 
 132: #[cfg(not(windows))]
 133: fn read_passphrase_from_source(source_path: &Path) -> Result<Zeroizing<String>, String> {
 134:     let allow_root_owner = is_systemd_credential_path(source_path);
 135:     validate_secret_file_security(source_path, "passphrase file", allow_root_owner)?;
 136: 
 137:     let raw = fs::read(source_path).map_err(|err| format!("read passphrase file failed: {err}"))?;
 138:     parse_passphrase_bytes(raw, "passphrase file")
 139: }
 140: 
 141: fn parse_passphrase_bytes(
 142:     mut raw: Vec<u8>,
 143:     source_label: &str,
 144: ) -> Result<Zeroizing<String>, String> {
 145:     if raw.len() > MAX_PASSPHRASE_BYTES {
 146:         raw.zeroize();
 147:         return Err("passphrase exceeds maximum allowed size".to_string());
 148:     }
 149:     let decoded = match std::str::from_utf8(&raw) {
 150:         Ok(value) => value,
 151:         Err(_) => {
 152:             raw.zeroize();
 153:             return Err(format!("{source_label} contains non-utf8 bytes"));
 154:         }
 155:     };
 156:     let trimmed = decoded.trim();
 157:     if trimmed.len() < 16 {
 158:         raw.zeroize();
 159:         return Err("passphrase must be at least 16 characters".to_string());
 160:     }
 161:     let value = Zeroizing::new(trimmed.to_string());
 162:     raw.zeroize();
 163:     Ok(value)
 164: }
 165: 
 166: #[cfg(windows)]
 167: fn read_windows_runtime_passphrase_source(path: &Path) -> Result<Zeroizing<String>, String> {
 168:     validate_windows_secret_blob_path(path, "passphrase file")?;
 169:     validate_secret_file_security(path, "passphrase file", false)?;
 170:     // Use local-secret ACL here: the blob may be created by an SSH bootstrap session
 171:     // (admin user, not SYSTEM), so the file owner is the SSH user's SID rather than
 172:     // BA/SY. Security is provided by DPAPI LocalMachine encryption + NTFS DACL
 173:     // (SY/BA/service only); file-owner identity is not a meaningful invariant.
 174:     validate_windows_local_secret_acl(path, "passphrase file")?;
 175:     let raw = fs::read(path).map_err(|err| format!("read passphrase file failed: {err}"))?;
 176:     decode_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(raw, "passphrase file")
 177: }
 178: 
 179: #[cfg(windows)]
 180: fn read_windows_explicit_passphrase_source(path: &Path) -> Result<Zeroizing<String>, String> {
 181:     validate_windows_local_secret_input_path(path, "passphrase file")?;
 182:     validate_secret_file_security(path, "passphrase file", false)?;
 183:     let raw = fs::read(path).map_err(|err| format!("read passphrase file failed: {err}"))?;
 184:     if looks_like_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(raw.as_slice()) {
 185:         decode_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(raw, "passphrase file")
 186:     } else {
 187:         parse_passphrase_bytes(raw, "passphrase file")
 188:     }
 189: }
 190: 
 191: #[cfg(windows)]
 192: fn store_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(path: &Path, plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
 193:     use std::fs::OpenOptions;
 194: 
 195:     validate_windows_secret_blob_path(path, "passphrase file")?;
 196:     let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
 197:         format!(
 198:             "passphrase file path must include a parent directory: {}",
 199:             path.display()
 200:         )
 201:     })?;
 202:     validate_windows_runtime_file_path(parent, "passphrase file parent directory")?;
 203:     validate_windows_runtime_acl(parent, "passphrase file parent directory")?;
 204:     if path.exists() {
 205:         validate_secret_file_security(path, "passphrase file", false)?;
 206:     }
 207: 
 208:     let mut protected = dpapi_protect(
 209:         plaintext,
 210:         // LocalMachine scope allows the service account (NT SERVICE\RustyNet) to
 211:         // decrypt a passphrase blob provisioned by the Administrator bootstrap
 212:         // session via SSH. NTFS ACLs on C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\secrets\ restrict
 213:         // which local identities can read the file at all; DPAPI provides an
 214:         // additional layer that ties the blob to this machine.
 215:         WindowsDpapiScope::LocalMachine,
 216:         WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_DESCRIPTION,
 217:     )
 218:     .map_err(|err| format!("protect Windows DPAPI passphrase blob failed: {err}"))?;
 219:     let mut blob = encode_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(protected.as_slice())?;
 220:     protected.zeroize();
 221: 
 222:     let candidate = parent.join(format!(
 223:         ".{}.{}.tmp",
 224:         path.file_name()
 225:             .and_then(|value| value.to_str())
 226:             .unwrap_or("passphrase"),
 227:         std::process::id()
 228:     ));
 229:     if candidate.exists() {
 230:         remove_file_if_present(candidate.as_path())?;
 231:     }
 232: 
 233:     let write_result = (|| -> Result<(), String> {
 234:         let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
 235:             .write(true)
 236:             .create_new(true)
 237:             .open(candidate.as_path())
 238:             .map_err(|err| {
 239:                 format!(
 240:                     "create Windows DPAPI passphrase blob failed ({}): {err}",
 241:                     candidate.display()
 242:                 )
 243:             })?;
 244:         file.write_all(blob.as_slice()).map_err(|err| {
 245:             format!(
 246:                 "write Windows DPAPI passphrase blob failed ({}): {err}",
 247:                 candidate.display()
 248:             )
 249:         })?;
 250:         file.flush().map_err(|err| {
 251:             format!(
 252:                 "flush Windows DPAPI passphrase blob failed ({}): {err}",
 253:                 candidate.display()
 254:             )
 255:         })?;
 256:         if path.exists() {
 257:             remove_file_if_present(path)?;
 258:         }
 259:         fs::rename(candidate.as_path(), path).map_err(|err| {
 260:             format!(
 261:                 "persist Windows DPAPI passphrase blob failed ({} -> {}): {err}",
 262:                 candidate.display(),
 263:                 path.display()
 264:             )
 265:         })?;
 266:         validate_secret_file_security(path, "passphrase file", false)?;
 267:         // Use local-secret ACL (not runtime ACL) for the post-write check: the blob
 268:         // may be created during SSH bootstrap where the creating process runs under
 269:         // the admin user's SSH token (not SYSTEM), so the file owner is the SSH user
 270:         // rather than BA/SY. DPAPI LocalMachine encryption + NTFS DACL are the
 271:         // enforced security guarantees; owner identity is checked at startup
 272:         // by validate_windows_runtime_startup_acls on the containing directories.
 273:         validate_windows_local_secret_acl(path, "passphrase file")
 274:     })();
 275:     if write_result.is_err() {
 276:         let _ = remove_file_if_present(candidate.as_path());
 277:     }
 278:     blob.zeroize();
 279:     write_result
 280: }
 281: 
 282: #[cfg(windows)]
 283: fn encode_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(protected: &[u8]) -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, String> {
 284:     let blob_len = u32::try_from(protected.len())
 285:         .map_err(|_| "Windows DPAPI passphrase blob exceeds u32".to_string())?;
 286:     let mut encoded = Zeroizing::new(Vec::with_capacity(
 287:         WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_MAGIC.len() + 1 + 1 + 4 + protected.len(),
 288:     ));
 289:     encoded.extend_from_slice(WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_MAGIC);
 290:     encoded.push(WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_VERSION);
 291:     encoded.push(0);
 292:     encoded.extend_from_slice(&blob_len.to_be_bytes());
 293:     encoded.extend_from_slice(protected);
 294:     Ok(encoded)
 295: }
 296: 
 297: #[cfg(windows)]
 298: fn decode_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(
 299:     mut blob: Vec<u8>,
 300:     source_label: &str,
 301: ) -> Result<Zeroizing<String>, String> {
 302:     if !looks_like_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(blob.as_slice()) {
 303:         blob.zeroize();
 304:         return Err(format!(
 305:             "{source_label} is not a reviewed Windows DPAPI passphrase blob",
 306:         ));
 307:     }
 308:     let version = blob[WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_MAGIC.len()];
 309:     if version != WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_VERSION {
 310:         blob.zeroize();
 311:         return Err(format!(
 312:             "{source_label} uses unsupported Windows DPAPI blob version {version}",
 313:         ));
 314:     }
 315:     let length_offset = WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_MAGIC.len() + 2;
 316:     let protected_len = u32::from_be_bytes([
 317:         blob[length_offset],
 318:         blob[length_offset + 1],
 319:         blob[length_offset + 2],
 320:         blob[length_offset + 3],
 321:     ]) as usize;
 322:     let data_offset = length_offset + 4;
 323:     let actual_len = blob
 324:         .len()
 325:         .checked_sub(data_offset)
 326:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("truncated {source_label} Windows DPAPI blob"))?;
 327:     if actual_len != protected_len {
 328:         blob.zeroize();
 329:         return Err(format!(
 330:             "{source_label} Windows DPAPI blob length mismatch (declared {protected_len}, actual {})",
 331:             actual_len
 332:         ));
 333:     }
 334:     let mut protected = Zeroizing::new(blob.split_off(data_offset));
 335:     blob.zeroize();
 336:     let mut plaintext = dpapi_unprotect(protected.as_slice())
 337:         .map_err(|err| format!("unprotect Windows DPAPI passphrase blob failed: {err}"))?;
 338:     let result = parse_passphrase_bytes(std::mem::take(&mut plaintext), source_label);
 339:     plaintext.zeroize();
 340:     result
 341: }
 342: 
 343: #[cfg(windows)]
 344: fn looks_like_windows_dpapi_passphrase_blob(blob: &[u8]) -> bool {
 345:     let header_len = WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_MAGIC.len() + 1 + 1 + 4;
 346:     blob.len() >= header_len && blob.starts_with(WINDOWS_DPAPI_PASSPHRASE_BLOB_MAGIC)
 347: }
 348: 
 349: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 350: fn read_passphrase_from_macos_keychain(account: &str) -> Result<Zeroizing<String>, String> {
 351:     let value =
 352:         load_macos_generic_password(MACOS_PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE, account).map_err(|err| {
 353:             format!(
 354:                 "load macOS keychain passphrase failed for service '{MACOS_PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE}' account '{account}': {err}",
 355:             )
 356:         })?;
 357:     parse_passphrase_bytes(value, "macOS keychain passphrase")
 358: }
 359: 
 360: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 361: fn resolve_macos_keychain_account_from_env() -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
 362:     let account = match std::env::var(PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT_ENV) {
 363:         Ok(value) => value,
 364:         Err(std::env::VarError::NotPresent) => return Ok(None),
 365:         Err(std::env::VarError::NotUnicode(_)) => {
 366:             return Err(format!(
 367:                 "{PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT_ENV} must be valid utf-8",
 368:             ));
 369:         }
 370:     };
 371:     Ok(Some(normalize_macos_keychain_account(&account)?))
 372: }
 373: 
 374: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 375: fn normalize_macos_keychain_account(raw: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
 376:     let account = raw.trim();
 377:     if account.is_empty() {
 378:         return Err(format!(
 379:             "{PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT_ENV} must not be empty",
 380:         ));
 381:     }
 382:     if account.len() > 128 {
 383:         return Err(format!(
 384:             "{PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT_ENV} exceeds max length (128)",
 385:         ));
 386:     }
 387:     if !account
 388:         .chars()
 389:         .all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '-' || ch == '_' || ch == '.')
 390:     {
 391:         return Err(format!(
 392:             "{PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT_ENV} contains invalid characters; allowed: [A-Za-z0-9._-]",
 393:         ));
 394:     }
 395:     Ok(account.to_string())
 396: }
 397: 
 398: pub fn decrypt_private_key(
 399:     encrypted_key_path: &Path,
 400:     passphrase_path: &Path,
 401: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
 402:     let passphrase = read_passphrase_file(passphrase_path)?;
 403:     let manager = key_custody_manager(encrypted_key_path, passphrase)?;
 404:     let key_id = key_custody_key_id(encrypted_key_path);
 405:     let mut key = manager
 406:         .load_private_key(&key_id)
 407:         .map_err(|err| format!("decrypt encrypted key failed: {err}"))?;
 408:     if key.is_empty() {
 409:         return Err("decrypted key is empty".to_string());
 410:     }
 411:     if !key.ends_with(b"\n") {
 412:         key.push(b'\n');
 413:     }
 414:     Ok(key)
 415: }
 416: 
 417: pub fn encrypt_private_key(
 418:     private_key: &[u8],
 419:     encrypted_key_path: &Path,
 420:     passphrase_path: &Path,
 421: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 422:     encrypt_private_key_with_passphrase(private_key, encrypted_key_path, passphrase_path, None)
 423: }
 424: 
 425: pub fn encrypt_private_key_with_passphrase(
 426:     private_key: &[u8],
 427:     encrypted_key_path: &Path,
 428:     passphrase_path: &Path,
 429:     explicit_passphrase_path: Option<&Path>,
 430: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 431:     let passphrase = match explicit_passphrase_path {
 432:         Some(path) => read_passphrase_file_explicit(path)?,
 433:         None => read_passphrase_file(passphrase_path)?,
 434:     };
 435:     let manager = key_custody_manager(encrypted_key_path, passphrase.clone())?;
 436:     let key_id = key_custody_key_id(encrypted_key_path);
 437:     let _backend = manager
 438:         .store_private_key(&key_id, private_key)
 439:         .map_err(|err| format!("encrypt key failed: {err}"))?;
 440:     let parent = encrypted_key_path
 441:         .parent()
 442:         .ok_or_else(|| "encrypted key path must include parent directory".to_string())?;
 443:     // Keep the configured encrypted-key path materialized on disk for service prechecks and
 444:     // deterministic bootstrap across hosts, even when the custody backend also stores by key-id.
 445:     write_encrypted_key_file(
 446:         parent,
 447:         encrypted_key_path,
 448:         private_key,
 449:         &passphrase,
 450:         KeyCustodyPermissionPolicy::default(),
 451:     )
 452:     .map_err(|err| format!("encrypt key backup failed: {err}"))?;
 453:     Ok(())
 454: }
 455: 
 456: fn key_custody_manager(
 457:     encrypted_key_path: &Path,
 458:     passphrase: Zeroizing<String>,
 459: ) -> Result<KeyCustodyManager<PlatformOsSecureStore>, String> {
 460:     let parent = encrypted_key_path
 461:         .parent()
 462:         .ok_or_else(|| "encrypted key path must include parent directory".to_string())?;
 463:     let manager = KeyCustodyManager::new_zeroizing(
 464:         PlatformOsSecureStore,
 465:         parent.to_path_buf(),
 466:         passphrase,
 467:         KeyCustodyPermissionPolicy::default(),
 468:     );
 469:     #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 470:     let manager = manager.with_fallback_policy(OsStoreFallbackPolicy::RequireOsSecureStore);
 471:     #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
 472:     let manager = manager.with_fallback_policy(OsStoreFallbackPolicy::RequireOsSecureStore);
 473:     Ok(manager)
 474: }
 475: 
 476: fn validate_secret_file_security(
 477:     path: &Path,
 478:     label: &str,
 479:     allow_root_owner: bool,
 480: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 481:     #[cfg(unix)]
 482:     {
 483:         let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(path)
 484:             .map_err(|err| format!("{label} metadata read failed: {err}"))?;
 485:         if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() {
 486:             return Err(format!("{label} must not be a symlink"));
 487:         }
 488:         if !metadata.file_type().is_file() {
 489:             return Err(format!("{label} must be a regular file"));
 490:         }
 491:         let mode = metadata.mode() & 0o777;
 492:         let disallowed_mode_mask = if allow_root_owner { 0o037 } else { 0o077 };
 493:         if mode & disallowed_mode_mask != 0 {
 494:             let expected = if allow_root_owner {
 495:                 "owner-only or root-owned credential with group-read only"
 496:             } else {
 497:                 "owner-only"
 498:             };
 499:             return Err(format!(
 500:                 "{label} permissions are too broad: expected {expected}, found {mode:03o}",
 501:             ));
 502:         }
 503:         let owner_uid = metadata.uid();
 504:         let expected_uid = Uid::effective().as_raw();
 505:         if owner_uid != expected_uid && !(allow_root_owner && owner_uid == 0) {
 506:             return Err(format!(
 507:                 "{label} owner uid mismatch: expected {expected_uid}, found {owner_uid}"
 508:             ));
 509:         }
 510:     }
 511:     #[cfg(not(unix))]
 512:     {
 513:         #[cfg(windows)]
 514:         {
 515:             validate_windows_local_secret_input_path(path, label)?;
 516:             let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(path)
 517:                 .map_err(|err| format!("{label} metadata read failed: {err}"))?;
 518:             if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() {
 519:                 return Err(format!("{label} must not be a symlink"));
 520:             }
 521:             if !metadata.file_type().is_file() {
 522:                 return Err(format!("{label} must be a regular file"));
 523:             }
 524:             validate_windows_local_secret_acl(path, label)?;
 525:             fs::File::open(path)
 526:                 .map_err(|err| format!("{label} is not readable by the current identity: {err}"))?;
 527:             return Ok(());
 528:         }
 529: 
 530:         #[cfg(not(windows))]
 531:         {
 532:             let metadata =
 533:                 fs::metadata(path).map_err(|err| format!("{label} metadata read failed: {err}"))?;
 534:             if !metadata.is_file() {
 535:                 return Err(format!("{label} must be a regular file"));
 536:             }
 537:         }
 538:     }
 539:     Ok(())
 540: }
 541: 
 542: fn resolve_passphrase_source(configured_path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
 543:     #[cfg(windows)]
 544:     {
 545:         validate_windows_secret_blob_path(configured_path, "passphrase file")?;
 546:         if configured_path.exists() {
 547:             return Ok(configured_path.to_path_buf());
 548:         }
 549:         return Err(format!(
 550:             "Windows passphrase source must be a reviewed DPAPI blob at {}",
 551:             configured_path.display()
 552:         ));
 553:     }
 554:     let explicit = std::env::var(PASSPHRASE_CREDENTIAL_PATH_ENV).ok();
 555:     let directory = std::env::var(SYSTEMD_CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY_ENV).ok();
 556:     resolve_passphrase_source_from_env(configured_path, explicit.as_deref(), directory.as_deref())
 557: }
 558: 
 559: fn resolve_passphrase_source_from_env(
 560:     configured_path: &Path,
 561:     explicit_credential_path: Option<&str>,
 562:     credentials_directory: Option<&str>,
 563: ) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
 564:     #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 565:     {
 566:         let _ = (
 567:             configured_path,
 568:             explicit_credential_path,
 569:             credentials_directory,
 570:         );
 571:         Err(format!(
 572:             "macOS passphrase file custody is disabled; set {PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT_ENV} and provision the passphrase in keychain",
 573:         ))
 574:     }
 575:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
 576:     {
 577:         if let Some(explicit) = explicit_credential_path {
 578:             let explicit_path = PathBuf::from(explicit);
 579:             if explicit_path.exists() {
 580:                 return Ok(explicit_path);
 581:             }
 582:             return Err(format!(
 583:                 "passphrase credential path not found ({}={})",
 584:                 PASSPHRASE_CREDENTIAL_PATH_ENV,
 585:                 explicit_path.display()
 586:             ));
 587:         }
 588: 
 589:         if let Some(directory) = credentials_directory {
 590:             let candidate = Path::new(directory).join(DEFAULT_PASSPHRASE_CREDENTIAL_NAME);
 591:             if candidate.exists() {
 592:                 return Ok(candidate);
 593:             }
 594:             return Err(format!(
 595:                 "passphrase credential not found in {} (expected {})",
 596:                 SYSTEMD_CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY_ENV,
 597:                 candidate.display()
 598:             ));
 599:         }
 600: 
 601:         if configured_path.exists() {
 602:             return Err(format!(
 603:                 "passphrase credential source must be explicitly configured via {} or {}; direct fallback to {} is disallowed",
 604:                 PASSPHRASE_CREDENTIAL_PATH_ENV,
 605:                 SYSTEMD_CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY_ENV,
 606:                 configured_path.display()
 607:             ));
 608:         }
 609: 
 610:         Err(format!(
 611:             "passphrase credential source is not configured; set {PASSPHRASE_CREDENTIAL_PATH_ENV} or {SYSTEMD_CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY_ENV}",
 612:         ))
 613:     }
 614: }
 615: 
 616: fn is_systemd_credential_path(path: &Path) -> bool {
 617:     path.starts_with("/run/credentials/")
 618: }
 619: 
 620: fn key_custody_key_id(encrypted_key_path: &Path) -> String {
 621:     let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
 622:     hasher.update(encrypted_key_path.to_string_lossy().as_bytes());
 623:     let digest = hasher.finalize();
 624:     let mut suffix = String::with_capacity(16);
 625:     for byte in digest.iter().take(8) {
 626:         suffix.push_str(&format!("{byte:02x}"));
 627:     }
 628:     format!("wg-private-{suffix}")
 629: }
 630: 
 631: pub fn write_runtime_private_key(path: &Path, private_key: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
 632:     if private_key.is_empty() {
 633:         return Err("private key must not be empty".to_string());
 634:     }
 635:     write_atomic(path, private_key, 0o600)
 636: }
 637: 
 638: pub fn write_public_key(path: &Path, public_key: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
 639:     if public_key.trim().is_empty() {
 640:         return Err("public key must not be empty".to_string());
 641:     }
 642:     let value = format!("{}\n", public_key.trim());
 643:     write_atomic(path, value.as_bytes(), 0o644)
 644: }
 645: 
 646: pub fn generate_wireguard_keypair() -> Result<(Vec<u8>, String), String> {
 647:     let wg_binary = resolve_wireguard_binary_path()?;
 648:     let private = Command::new(&wg_binary)
 649:         .arg("genkey")
 650:         .output()
 651:         .map_err(|err| format!("wg genkey spawn failed ({}): {err}", wg_binary.display()))?;
 652:     if !private.status.success() {
 653:         return Err(format!("wg genkey failed: {}", private.status));
 654:     }
 655:     let mut private_key = private.stdout;
 656:     if private_key.is_empty() {
 657:         return Err("wg genkey produced empty key".to_string());
 658:     }
 659:     if !private_key.ends_with(b"\n") {
 660:         private_key.push(b'\n');
 661:     }
 662: 
 663:     let public_key = match derive_public_key_from_private_key(&private_key) {
 664:         Ok(value) => value,
 665:         Err(err) => {
 666:             private_key.fill(0);
 667:             return Err(err);
 668:         }
 669:     };
 670:     Ok((private_key, public_key))
 671: }

 673: pub fn apply_interface_private_key(
 674:     interface_name: &str,
 675:     runtime_key_path: &Path,
 676: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 677:     validate_interface_name(interface_name)?;
 678:     let wg_binary = resolve_wireguard_binary_path()?;
 679:     let status = Command::new(&wg_binary)
 680:         .arg("set")
 681:         .arg(interface_name)
 682:         .arg("private-key")
 683:         .arg(runtime_key_path)
 684:         .status()
 685:         .map_err(|err| {
 686:             format!(
 687:                 "wg set private-key spawn failed ({}): {err}",
 688:                 wg_binary.display()
 689:             )
 690:         })?;
 691:     if status.success() {
 692:         return Ok(());
 693:     }
 694:     Err(format!(
 695:         "wg set private-key failed for {interface_name}: {status}",
 696:     ))
 697: }

 699: pub fn set_interface_down(interface_name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
 700:     validate_interface_name(interface_name)?;
 701:     #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 702:     let status = {
 703:         let ifconfig_binary = resolve_ifconfig_binary_path()?;
 704:         Command::new(&ifconfig_binary)
 705:             .arg(interface_name)
 706:             .arg("down")
 707:             .status()
 708:             .map_err(|err| {
 709:                 format!(
 710:                     "ifconfig down spawn failed ({}): {err}",
 711:                     ifconfig_binary.display()
 712:                 )
 713:             })?
 714:     };
 715:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
 716:     let status = {
 717:         let ip_binary = resolve_ip_binary_path()?;
 718:         Command::new(&ip_binary)
 719:             .arg("link")
 720:             .arg("set")
 721:             .arg("down")
 722:             .arg("dev")
 723:             .arg(interface_name)
 724:             .status()
 725:             .map_err(|err| {
 726:                 format!(
 727:                     "ip link set down spawn failed ({}): {err}",
 728:                     ip_binary.display()
 729:                 )
 730:             })?
 731:     };
 732:     if status.success() {
 733:         return Ok(());
 734:     }
 735:     #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 736:     return Err(format!(
 737:         "ifconfig down failed for {interface_name}: {status}",
 738:     ));
 739:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
 740:     Err(format!(
 741:         "ip link set down failed for {interface_name}: {status}"
 742:     ))
 743: }

 745: pub fn remove_file_if_present(path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
 746:     let metadata = match fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 747:         Ok(metadata) => metadata,
 748:         Err(err) if err.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),
 749:         Err(err) => return Err(format!("inspect {} failed: {err}", path.display())),
 750:     };
 751:     if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() {
 752:         return fs::remove_file(path)
 753:             .map_err(|err| format!("remove symlink {} failed: {err}", path.display()));
 754:     }
 755:     if !metadata.file_type().is_file() {
 756:         return Err(format!(
 757:             "secure remove requires a regular file: {}",
 758:             path.display()
 759:         ));
 760:     }
 761:     scrub_file_contents(path)?;
 762:     fs::remove_file(path).map_err(|err| format!("remove {} failed: {err}", path.display()))
 763: }
 764: 
 765: fn scrub_file_contents(path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
 766:     let metadata = fs::metadata(path)
 767:         .map_err(|err| format!("inspect file {} failed: {err}", path.display()))?;
 768:     let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
 769:         .write(true)
 770:         .open(path)
 771:         .map_err(|err| format!("open {} failed: {err}", path.display()))?;
 772:     let mut remaining = metadata.len();
 773:     let zero_block = [0u8; 8192];
 774:     while remaining > 0 {
 775:         let chunk_len = std::cmp::min(remaining, zero_block.len() as u64) as usize;
 776:         file.write_all(&zero_block[..chunk_len])
 777:             .map_err(|err| format!("scrub write {} failed: {err}", path.display()))?;
 778:         remaining -= chunk_len as u64;
 779:     }
 780:     file.sync_all()
 781:         .map_err(|err| format!("sync {} failed: {err}", path.display()))?;
 782:     file.set_len(0)
 783:         .map_err(|err| format!("truncate {} failed: {err}", path.display()))?;
 784:     file.sync_all()
 785:         .map_err(|err| format!("sync {} after truncate failed: {err}", path.display()))?;
 786:     Ok(())
 787: }
 788: 
 789: pub fn initialize_encrypted_key_material(
 790:     runtime_private_key_path: &Path,
 791:     encrypted_key_path: &Path,
 792:     public_key_path: &Path,
 793:     passphrase_path: &Path,
 794:     explicit_passphrase_path: Option<&Path>,
 795:     force: bool,
 796: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 797:     if !force
 798:         && (runtime_private_key_path.exists()
 799:             || encrypted_key_path.exists()
 800:             || public_key_path.exists())
 801:     {
 802:         return Err(
 803:             "key material already exists; use --force to overwrite existing files".to_string(),
 804:         );
 805:     }
 806: 
 807:     let (mut private_key, public_key) = generate_wireguard_keypair()?;
 808:     let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
 809:         encrypt_private_key_with_passphrase(
 810:             &private_key,
 811:             encrypted_key_path,
 812:             passphrase_path,
 813:             explicit_passphrase_path,
 814:         )?;
 815:         if let Err(err) = write_runtime_private_key(runtime_private_key_path, &private_key) {
 816:             let _ = remove_file_if_present(runtime_private_key_path);
 817:             return Err(err);
 818:         }
 819:         if let Err(err) = write_public_key(public_key_path, &public_key) {
 820:             let _ = remove_file_if_present(public_key_path);
 821:             return Err(err);
 822:         }
 823:         Ok(public_key.clone())
 824:     })();
 825:     private_key.fill(0);
 826:     result
 827: }
 828: 
 829: pub fn migrate_existing_private_key_material(
 830:     existing_private_key_path: &Path,
 831:     runtime_private_key_path: &Path,
 832:     encrypted_key_path: &Path,
 833:     public_key_path: &Path,
 834:     passphrase_path: &Path,
 835:     explicit_passphrase_path: Option<&Path>,
 836:     force: bool,
 837: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 838:     if !existing_private_key_path.exists() {
 839:         return Err(format!(
 840:             "existing private key file not found: {}",
 841:             existing_private_key_path.display()
 842:         ));
 843:     }
 844:     if !force && (encrypted_key_path.exists() || public_key_path.exists()) {
 845:         return Err(
 846:             "target key material already exists; use --force to overwrite existing files"
 847:                 .to_string(),
 848:         );
 849:     }
 850: 
 851:     let mut private_key = fs::read(existing_private_key_path).map_err(|err| {
 852:         format!(
 853:             "read existing private key {} failed: {err}",
 854:             existing_private_key_path.display()
 855:         )
 856:     })?;
 857:     if private_key.is_empty() {
 858:         return Err("existing private key is empty".to_string());
 859:     }
 860:     if !private_key.ends_with(b"\n") {
 861:         private_key.push(b'\n');
 862:     }
 863: 
 864:     let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
 865:         let public_key = derive_public_key_from_private_key(&private_key)?;
 866:         encrypt_private_key_with_passphrase(
 867:             &private_key,
 868:             encrypted_key_path,
 869:             passphrase_path,
 870:             explicit_passphrase_path,
 871:         )?;
 872:         if let Err(err) = write_runtime_private_key(runtime_private_key_path, &private_key) {
 873:             let _ = remove_file_if_present(runtime_private_key_path);
 874:             return Err(err);
 875:         }
 876:         if let Err(err) = write_public_key(public_key_path, &public_key) {
 877:             let _ = remove_file_if_present(public_key_path);
 878:             return Err(err);
 879:         }
 880:         Ok(public_key)
 881:     })();
 882:     private_key.fill(0);
 883:     result
 884: }
 885: 
 886: fn write_atomic(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8], mode: u32) -> Result<(), String> {
 887:     let parent = path
 888:         .parent()
 889:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("path {} has no parent", path.display()))?;
 890:     if parent.exists() {
 891:         let parent_meta = fs::symlink_metadata(parent).map_err(|err| {
 892:             format!(
 893:                 "inspect parent directory {} failed: {err}",
 894:                 parent.display()
 895:             )
 896:         })?;
 897:         if parent_meta.file_type().is_symlink() || !parent_meta.file_type().is_dir() {
 898:             return Err(format!(
 899:                 "parent path {} must be a real directory, not a symlink",
 900:                 parent.display()
 901:             ));
 902:         }
 903:     }
 904:     fs::create_dir_all(parent)
 905:         .map_err(|err| format!("create parent directory {} failed: {err}", parent.display()))?;
 906: 
 907:     #[cfg(unix)]
 908:     {
 909:         use std::os::unix::fs::{MetadataExt, PermissionsExt};
 910:         match fs::set_permissions(parent, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700)) {
 911:             Ok(()) => {}
 912:             Err(err) if err.kind() == ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => {
 913:                 let metadata = fs::metadata(parent).map_err(|meta_err| {
 914:                     format!(
 915:                         "inspect parent permissions {} failed after chmod denial: {meta_err}",
 916:                         parent.display()
 917:                     )
 918:                 })?;
 919:                 let mode = metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o777;
 920:                 let owner_uid = metadata.uid();
 921:                 let expected_uid = Uid::effective().as_raw();
 922:                 // Privilege-separated deployments keep /run/rustynet root-owned and group-writable
 923:                 // for helper + daemon cooperation; accept that hardened shared parent shape.
 924:                 let root_managed_shared_runtime = owner_uid == 0 && mode == 0o770;
 925:                 if !root_managed_shared_runtime {
 926:                     return Err(format!(
 927:                         "set parent permissions {} failed: {err}",
 928:                         parent.display()
 929:                     ));
 930:                 }
 931:                 if owner_uid == expected_uid {
 932:                     return Err(format!(
 933:                         "set parent permissions {} failed despite owner match: {err}",
 934:                         parent.display()
 935:                     ));
 936:                 }
 937:             }
 938:             Err(err) => {
 939:                 return Err(format!(
 940:                     "set parent permissions {} failed: {err}",
 941:                     parent.display()
 942:                 ));
 943:             }
 944:         }
 945:     }
 946: 
 947:     let temp = temp_path_for(path);
 948:     if path.exists() {
 949:         let target_meta = fs::symlink_metadata(path)
 950:             .map_err(|err| format!("inspect target {} failed: {err}", path.display()))?;
 951:         if target_meta.file_type().is_symlink() {
 952:             return Err(format!("target {} must not be a symlink", path.display()));
 953:         }
 954:         if !target_meta.file_type().is_file() {
 955:             return Err(format!("target {} must be a regular file", path.display()));
 956:         }
 957:     }
 958:     let mut options = OpenOptions::new();
 959:     options.write(true).create_new(true);
 960:     #[cfg(unix)]
 961:     {
 962:         options.mode(mode);
 963:     }
 964:     let mut file = options
 965:         .open(&temp)
 966:         .map_err(|err| format!("create temp key file {} failed: {err}", temp.display()))?;
 967:     if let Err(err) = file.write_all(bytes) {
 968:         let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp);
 969:         return Err(format!(
 970:             "write temp key file {} failed: {err}",
 971:             temp.display()
 972:         ));
 973:     }
 974:     if let Err(err) = file.sync_all() {
 975:         let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp);
 976:         return Err(format!(
 977:             "sync temp key file {} failed: {err}",
 978:             temp.display()
 979:         ));
 980:     }
 981:     if let Err(err) = fs::rename(&temp, path) {
 982:         let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp);
 983:         return Err(format!(
 984:             "rename temp key file {} to {} failed: {err}",
 985:             temp.display(),
 986:             path.display()
 987:         ));
 988:     }
 989:     // Directory fsync is a no-op on Windows: FlushFileBuffers on a directory
 990:     // handle requires special access that read-open does not provide.
 991:     #[cfg(unix)]
 992:     {
 993:         let parent_dir = fs::File::open(parent)
 994:             .map_err(|err| format!("open parent directory {} failed: {err}", parent.display()))?;
 995:         parent_dir
 996:             .sync_all()
 997:             .map_err(|err| format!("sync parent directory {} failed: {err}", parent.display()))?;
 998:     }
 999:     Ok(())
1000: }
1001: 
1002: fn temp_path_for(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
1003:     let mut out = path.as_os_str().to_os_string();
1004:     let stamp = SystemTime::now()
1005:         .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
1006:         .map(|duration| duration.as_nanos())
1007:         .unwrap_or(0);
1008:     out.push(format!(".tmp.{}.{}", std::process::id(), stamp));
1009:     PathBuf::from(out)
1010: }

1012: fn validate_interface_name(value: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
1013:     if value.is_empty() {
1014:         return Err("interface name must not be empty".to_string());
1015:     }
1016:     if value.len() > 15 {
1017:         return Err("interface name must be <= 15 characters".to_string());
1018:     }
1019:     if value
1020:         .chars()
1021:         .all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '-' || ch == '_' || ch == '.')
1022:     {
1023:         return Ok(());
1024:     }
1025:     Err("interface name contains invalid characters".to_string())
1026: }

1046: fn resolve_binary_path(env_var: &str, default_path: &str, label: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
1047:     let configured = std::env::var(env_var).ok();
1048:     let candidate = configured
1049:         .as_deref()
1050:         .map(str::trim)
1051:         .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
1052:         .unwrap_or(default_path);
1053:     validate_binary_path(candidate, label)?;
1054:     Ok(PathBuf::from(candidate))
1055: }
1056: 
1057: fn validate_binary_path(raw_path: &str, label: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
1058:     let path = Path::new(raw_path);
1059:     if !path.is_absolute() {
1060:         return Err(format!("{label} binary path must be absolute: {raw_path}"));
1061:     }
1062:     let canonical = fs::canonicalize(path).map_err(|err| {
1063:         format!(
1064:             "{label} binary canonicalization failed for {}: {err}",
1065:             path.display()
1066:         )
1067:     })?;
1068:     let metadata =
1069:         fs::metadata(&canonical).map_err(|err| format!("{label} binary metadata failed: {err}"))?;
1070:     if !metadata.file_type().is_file() {
1071:         return Err(format!(
1072:             "{label} binary path must be a regular file: {}",
1073:             canonical.display()
1074:         ));
1075:     }
1076:     #[cfg(unix)]
1077:     {
1078:         let mode = metadata.mode() & 0o777;
1079:         if mode & 0o111 == 0 {
1080:             return Err(format!(
1081:                 "{label} binary is not executable: {} ({:03o})",
1082:                 canonical.display(),
1083:                 mode
1084:             ));
1085:         }
1086:         if mode & 0o022 != 0 {
1087:             return Err(format!(
1088:                 "{label} binary must not be group/other writable: {} ({:03o})",
1089:                 canonical.display(),
1090:                 mode
1091:             ));
1092:         }
1093:         let owner_uid = metadata.uid();
1094:         if owner_uid != 0 {
1095:             return Err(format!(
1096:                 "{label} binary must be root-owned: {} (uid={owner_uid})",
1097:                 canonical.display()
1098:             ));
1099:         }
1100:     }
1101:     Ok(())
1102: }
1103: 
1104: fn derive_public_key_from_private_key(private_key: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {
1105:     let wg_binary = resolve_wireguard_binary_path()?;
1106:     let mut child = Command::new(&wg_binary)
1107:         .arg("pubkey")
1108:         .stdin(Stdio::piped())
1109:         .stdout(Stdio::piped())
1110:         .spawn()
1111:         .map_err(|err| format!("wg pubkey spawn failed ({}): {err}", wg_binary.display()))?;
1112:     {
1113:         let stdin = child
1114:             .stdin
1115:             .as_mut()
1116:             .ok_or_else(|| "wg pubkey stdin unavailable".to_string())?;
1117:         stdin
1118:             .write_all(private_key)
1119:             .map_err(|err| format!("wg pubkey stdin write failed: {err}"))?;
1120:     }
1121:     let output = child
1122:         .wait_with_output()
1123:         .map_err(|err| format!("wg pubkey wait failed: {err}"))?;
1124:     if !output.status.success() {
1125:         return Err(format!("wg pubkey failed: {}", output.status));
1126:     }
1127:     let public_key = String::from_utf8(output.stdout)
1128:         .map_err(|err| format!("wg pubkey produced non-utf8 output: {err}"))?
1129:         .trim()
1130:         .to_string();
1131:     if public_key.is_empty() {
1132:         return Err("wg pubkey produced empty key".to_string());
1133:     }
1134:     Ok(public_key)
1135: }

1138: mod tests {
1139:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
1140:     use super::DEFAULT_PASSPHRASE_CREDENTIAL_NAME;

1143:     fn unique_test_dir(prefix: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
1144:         let stamp = std::time::SystemTime::now()
1145:             .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
1146:             .expect("time should be monotonic")
1147:             .as_nanos();

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/linux_authenticode.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Linux authenticode-equivalent stub.
   4: //!
   5: //! Authenticode is a Windows-specific binary signature mechanism
   6: //! (`WinVerifyTrust` + the WINTRUST_ACTION_GENERIC_VERIFY_V2 chain).
   7: //! Linux does not enforce binary signatures at runtime — package
   8: //! signature verification happens at install time via dpkg / rpm /
   9: //! apt-secure / dnf-gpgcheck, not as a runtime binary attestation.
  10: //!
  11: //! Rather than reject the `Authenticode` op on Linux, the daemon
  12: //! exposes a `linux-authenticode-check` subcommand that always emits
  13: //! a typed `applicable: false` report. This keeps the
  14: //! `LinuxDaemonProbe::build_argv` shape uniform — every op resolves
  15: //! to argv — and gives the orchestrator a consistent JSON structure
  16: //! to consume regardless of platform. The `applicable` field signals
  17: //! the orchestrator that the runtime did not enforce a binary
  18: //! signature on this host; a future Linux slice could swap this stub
  19: //! for an actual dpkg/rpm signature lookup, at which point the
  20: //! report's `applicable` would flip to `true` and the existing
  21: //! Windows-style `valid` field would carry the verdict.
  22: 
  23: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  24: 
  25: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  26: pub struct LinuxAuthenticodeReport {
  27:     pub schema_version: u32,
  28:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  29:     /// Always `false` on Linux today: there is no runtime binary
  30:     /// signature attestation equivalent to Windows `WinVerifyTrust`.
  31:     /// Reserved for a future slice that wires dpkg/rpm signature
  32:     /// verification.
  33:     pub applicable: bool,
  34:     pub reason: String,
  35: }
  36: 
  37: pub fn collect_linux_authenticode_report() -> LinuxAuthenticodeReport {
  38:     LinuxAuthenticodeReport {
  39:         schema_version: 1,
  40:         // overall_ok=true because the verifier did not find drift;
  41:         // it found the op is not applicable on this platform. The
  42:         // orchestrator threads this differently from Windows where
  43:         // `valid: false` is a hard fail.
  44:         overall_ok: true,
  45:         applicable: false,
  46:         reason: "Linux does not enforce binary signatures at runtime; package \
  47:              signature verification happens at install time via dpkg/rpm. \
  48:              A runtime authenticode-equivalent is not part of the reviewed \
  49:              Linux posture today."
  50:             .to_string(),
  51:     }
  52: }
  53: 
  54: #[cfg(test)]
  55: mod tests {
  56:     use super::*;
  57: 
  58:     #[test]
  59:     fn report_marks_overall_ok_with_applicable_false() {
  60:         let report = collect_linux_authenticode_report();
  61:         assert!(report.overall_ok);
  62:         assert!(!report.applicable);
  63:         assert!(
  64:             report.reason.contains("dpkg/rpm"),
  65:             "reason must cite the install-time mechanism: {}",
  66:             report.reason
  67:         );
  68:     }
  69: 
  70:     #[test]
  71:     fn report_serde_round_trips() {
  72:         let report = collect_linux_authenticode_report();
  73:         let json = serde_json::to_string(&report).expect("serialize");
  74:         let parsed: LinuxAuthenticodeReport = serde_json::from_str(&json).expect("deserialize");
  75:         assert_eq!(parsed, report);
  76:     }
  77: 
  78:     #[test]
  79:     fn report_schema_pins_version_one() {
  80:         let report = collect_linux_authenticode_report();
  81:         assert_eq!(report.schema_version, 1);
  82:     }
  83: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/linux_dns_failclosed.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Linux DNS fail-closed verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! Linux parity for `windows_dns_failclosed`. Confirms the host's
   6: //! resolver is bound to loopback only — no external DNS server is
   7: //! configured to receive queries that should stay inside the mesh.
   8: //! When the resolver path on the host points anywhere off-loopback,
   9: //! a queries-to-mesh-names side-channel exists and the verifier
  10: //! reports drift.
  11: //!
  12: //! On Linux there are several resolver stacks (systemd-resolved,
  13: //! resolvconf, dnsmasq, plain `/etc/resolv.conf`). This verifier
  14: //! reads `/etc/resolv.conf` directly because that's the lowest-
  15: //! common-denominator file every libc-using process consults. A
  16: //! future slice can extend the verifier to query
  17: //! `resolvectl status` for systemd-resolved-managed hosts; the
  18: //! resolv.conf check stays as the floor.
  19: //!
  20: //! The pure evaluator takes a parsed list of nameserver addresses
  21: //! and confirms every one is loopback (127.0.0.0/8 for IPv4, ::1/128
  22: //! for IPv6). Off-loopback nameservers count as drift.
  23: //!
  24: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd linux-dns-failclosed-check`.
  25: //! The orchestrator's `LinuxDaemonProbe` adapter dispatches the
  26: //! `DnsFailclosed` op to this subcommand.
  27: 
  28: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  29: use std::net::IpAddr;
  30: 
  31: pub const REVIEWED_RESOLV_CONF_PATH: &str = "/etc/resolv.conf";
  32: 
  33: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  34: pub struct LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
  35:     pub resolv_conf_path: String,
  36:     pub resolv_conf_present: bool,
  37:     /// Raw nameserver lines from `/etc/resolv.conf`, in source order.
  38:     pub nameservers: Vec<String>,
  39:     /// Optional capture of `search` / `domain` lines for forensic
  40:     /// completeness; not evaluated for drift today.
  41:     pub search_domains: Vec<String>,
  42:     /// Whether the daemon's loopback resolver is bound — currently
  43:     /// inferred from the `RUSTYNET_DNS_RESOLVER_BIND_ADDR=127.0.0.1:…`
  44:     /// env-var contract; this snapshot field is a placeholder for a
  45:     /// future probe of the actual listening socket.
  46:     pub loopback_resolver_advertised: bool,
  47: }
  48: 
  49: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  50: pub struct LinuxDnsFailclosedReport {
  51:     pub schema_version: u32,
  52:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  53:     pub snapshot: LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot,
  54:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  55: }
  56: 
  57: /// Pure evaluator: walks the nameserver list and confirms every
  58: /// entry is a loopback address. Returns every drift reason in one
  59: /// pass. The collector does the file-IO / parsing; the evaluator
  60: /// stays platform-agnostic and unit-testable.
  61: pub fn evaluate_linux_dns_failclosed_snapshot(
  62:     snapshot: &LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot,
  63: ) -> Vec<String> {
  64:     let mut reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  65:     if !snapshot.resolv_conf_present {
  66:         reasons.push(format!(
  67:             "resolv.conf not readable at {}: cannot confirm DNS fail-closed posture",
  68:             snapshot.resolv_conf_path
  69:         ));
  70:         return reasons;
  71:     }
  72:     if snapshot.nameservers.is_empty() {
  73:         reasons.push(format!(
  74:             "{} contains no nameserver entries; cannot confirm fail-closed posture",
  75:             snapshot.resolv_conf_path
  76:         ));
  77:         return reasons;
  78:     }
  79:     for raw in &snapshot.nameservers {
  80:         match raw.parse::<IpAddr>() {
  81:             Ok(addr) if is_loopback_address(&addr) => {}
  82:             Ok(addr) => {
  83:                 reasons.push(format!(
  84:                     "nameserver {addr} is non-loopback; mesh DNS queries leak off-host"
  85:                 ));
  86:             }
  87:             Err(err) => {
  88:                 reasons.push(format!(
  89:                     "nameserver entry {raw:?} is not a parseable IP address: {err}"
  90:                 ));
  91:             }
  92:         }
  93:     }
  94:     reasons
  95: }
  96: 
  97: fn is_loopback_address(addr: &IpAddr) -> bool {
  98:     match addr {
  99:         IpAddr::V4(v4) => v4.is_loopback(),
 100:         IpAddr::V6(v6) => v6.is_loopback(),
 101:     }
 102: }
 103: 
 104: pub fn build_linux_dns_failclosed_report(
 105:     snapshot: LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot,
 106: ) -> LinuxDnsFailclosedReport {
 107:     let drift_reasons = evaluate_linux_dns_failclosed_snapshot(&snapshot);
 108:     let overall_ok = drift_reasons.is_empty();
 109:     LinuxDnsFailclosedReport {
 110:         schema_version: 1,
 111:         overall_ok,
 112:         snapshot,
 113:         drift_reasons,
 114:     }
 115: }
 116: 
 117: /// Parse `/etc/resolv.conf`-style content. Strips comments (`#` /
 118: /// `;`), extracts each `nameserver <addr>` and `search <domain ...>`
 119: /// line. Tolerant of leading whitespace + blank lines so the parser
 120: /// matches what glibc accepts.
 121: pub fn parse_resolv_conf(body: &str) -> (Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
 122:     let mut nameservers: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
 123:     let mut search_domains: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
 124:     for line in body.lines() {
 125:         let trimmed = line.trim();
 126:         if trimmed.is_empty() {
 127:             continue;
 128:         }
 129:         if trimmed.starts_with('#') || trimmed.starts_with(';') {
 130:             continue;
 131:         }
 132:         if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_prefix("nameserver") {
 133:             let value = rest.trim();
 134:             if !value.is_empty() {
 135:                 nameservers.push(value.to_string());
 136:             }
 137:             continue;
 138:         }
 139:         if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_prefix("search") {
 140:             for token in rest.split_ascii_whitespace() {
 141:                 search_domains.push(token.to_string());
 142:             }
 143:             continue;
 144:         }
 145:         if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_prefix("domain") {
 146:             let value = rest.trim();
 147:             if !value.is_empty() {
 148:                 search_domains.push(value.to_string());
 149:             }
 150:         }
 151:     }
 152:     (nameservers, search_domains)
 153: }
 154: 
 155: /// Cross-platform collector. On Linux reads `/etc/resolv.conf` and
 156: /// parses it; off-Linux emits a snapshot with `resolv_conf_present =
 157: /// false` and a clear blocker reason.
 158: pub fn collect_linux_dns_failclosed_snapshot() -> LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
 159:     collect_linux_dns_failclosed_snapshot_inner()
 160: }
 161: 
 162: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
 163: fn collect_linux_dns_failclosed_snapshot_inner() -> LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
 164:     let body = match std::fs::read_to_string(REVIEWED_RESOLV_CONF_PATH) {
 165:         Ok(b) => b,
 166:         Err(_) => {
 167:             return LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
 168:                 resolv_conf_path: REVIEWED_RESOLV_CONF_PATH.to_string(),
 169:                 resolv_conf_present: false,
 170:                 nameservers: Vec::new(),
 171:                 search_domains: Vec::new(),
 172:                 // Off-host loopback advertise: assume the daemon's
 173:                 // RUSTYNET_DNS_RESOLVER_BIND_ADDR env var advertises
 174:                 // 127.0.0.1; the snapshot field stays a contract
 175:                 // marker until a future slice probes the live socket.
 176:                 loopback_resolver_advertised: true,
 177:             };
 178:         }
 179:     };
 180:     let (nameservers, search_domains) = parse_resolv_conf(body.as_str());
 181:     LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
 182:         resolv_conf_path: REVIEWED_RESOLV_CONF_PATH.to_string(),
 183:         resolv_conf_present: true,
 184:         nameservers,
 185:         search_domains,
 186:         loopback_resolver_advertised: true,
 187:     }
 188: }
 189: 
 190: #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
 191: fn collect_linux_dns_failclosed_snapshot_inner() -> LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
 192:     LinuxDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
 193:         resolv_conf_path: REVIEWED_RESOLV_CONF_PATH.to_string(),
 194:         resolv_conf_present: false,
 195:         nameservers: Vec::new(),
 196:         search_domains: Vec::new(),
 197:         loopback_resolver_advertised: false,
 198:     }
 199: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/linux_key_custody.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Linux key-custody verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! Linux parity for `windows_key_custody`. Validates that the on-disk
   6: //! key material on a Linux runtime host matches the reviewed custody
   7: //! contract:
   8: //!
   9: //! * the encrypted WireGuard private key exists at
  10: //!   `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.key.enc`, owned by
  11: //!   `rustynetd:rustynetd`, mode `0600`;
  12: //! * the WireGuard public key exists at
  13: //!   `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.pub`, owned by
  14: //!   `rustynetd:rustynetd`, mode `0640` or `0600`;
  15: //! * the keys directory `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/` is a real directory
  16: //!   owned by `rustynetd:rustynetd`, mode `0700`;
  17: //! * the plaintext WireGuard private key (the legacy unencrypted path)
  18: //!   is absent at rest — Phase E migrated runtime key custody to
  19: //!   encrypted-at-rest.
  20: //!
  21: //! These come from the systemd unit's `RUSTYNET_WG_*` env vars + the
  22: //! e2e bootstrap install commands. Wired through the CLI as
  23: //! `rustynetd linux-key-custody-check`. The orchestrator's
  24: //! `LinuxDaemonProbe` adapter dispatches the `KeyCustody` op to this
  25: //! subcommand.
  26: 
  27: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  28: 
  29: pub const LINUX_WG_KEYS_DIR: &str = "/var/lib/rustynet/keys";
  30: pub const LINUX_WG_ENCRYPTED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH: &str = "/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.key.enc";
  31: pub const LINUX_WG_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH: &str = "/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.pub";
  32: /// Legacy plaintext private key path. Must NOT exist at rest after the
  33: /// Phase E migration to encrypted-at-rest custody.
  34: pub const LINUX_WG_PLAINTEXT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH: &str = "/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.key";
  35: 
  36: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  37: #[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
  38: pub enum LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus {
  39:     /// Required artifact present, valid, with reviewed mode + owner.
  40:     Ok { mode: u32, uid: u32, gid: u32 },
  41:     /// Required artifact missing.
  42:     Missing { reason: String },
  43:     /// Required artifact present but mode / owner / type drifted.
  44:     Invalid {
  45:         reason: String,
  46:         mode: u32,
  47:         uid: u32,
  48:         gid: u32,
  49:     },
  50:     /// Forbidden artifact present (e.g. plaintext private key file).
  51:     Forbidden { reason: String },
  52:     /// Forbidden artifact correctly absent.
  53:     AbsentAsExpected,
  54: }
  55: 
  56: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  57: pub struct LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
  58:     pub label: String,
  59:     pub path: String,
  60:     /// `"present"` or `"absent"` — drives how the status is interpreted.
  61:     pub requirement: String,
  62:     #[serde(flatten)]
  63:     pub status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus,
  64: }
  65: 
  66: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  67: pub struct LinuxKeyCustodyReport {
  68:     pub schema_version: u32,
  69:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  70:     pub entries: Vec<LinuxKeyCustodyEntry>,
  71:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  72: }
  73: 
  74: const REQUIREMENT_PRESENT: &str = "present";
  75: const REQUIREMENT_ABSENT: &str = "absent";
  76: 
  77: /// Pure evaluator: walks the entries and re-derives drift reasons from
  78: /// per-entry statuses. Returns `Ok(())` when every entry's status is
  79: /// consistent with its requirement, otherwise the aggregated reasons.
  80: pub fn evaluate_linux_key_custody(entries: &[LinuxKeyCustodyEntry]) -> Result<(), Vec<String>> {
  81:     let mut reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  82:     if entries.is_empty() {
  83:         reasons.push("key custody report contains no entries".to_string());
  84:         return Err(reasons);
  85:     }
  86:     for entry in entries {
  87:         match (entry.requirement.as_str(), &entry.status) {
  88:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok { .. }) => {}
  89:             (REQUIREMENT_ABSENT, LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected) => {}
  90:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing { reason }) => {
  91:                 reasons.push(format!("{} missing: {reason}", entry.label));
  92:             }
  93:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid { reason, .. }) => {
  94:                 reasons.push(format!("{} invalid: {reason}", entry.label));
  95:             }
  96:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected) => {
  97:                 reasons.push(format!(
  98:                     "{} required but reported absent (collector bug or missing artifact)",
  99:                     entry.label
 100:                 ));
 101:             }
 102:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Forbidden { reason }) => {
 103:                 reasons.push(format!(
 104:                     "{} marked forbidden but requirement is present: {reason}",
 105:                     entry.label
 106:                 ));
 107:             }
 108:             (REQUIREMENT_ABSENT, LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Forbidden { reason }) => {
 109:                 reasons.push(format!(
 110:                     "{} forbidden but present at rest: {reason}",
 111:                     entry.label
 112:                 ));
 113:             }
 114:             (REQUIREMENT_ABSENT, other) => {
 115:                 reasons.push(format!(
 116:                     "{} requirement is absent but status is {other:?}",
 117:                     entry.label
 118:                 ));
 119:             }
 120:             (other, _) => {
 121:                 reasons.push(format!(
 122:                     "{} has unknown requirement {other}; expected `present` or `absent`",
 123:                     entry.label
 124:                 ));
 125:             }
 126:         }
 127:     }
 128:     if reasons.is_empty() {
 129:         Ok(())
 130:     } else {
 131:         Err(reasons)
 132:     }
 133: }
 134: 
 135: pub fn build_linux_key_custody_report(entries: Vec<LinuxKeyCustodyEntry>) -> LinuxKeyCustodyReport {
 136:     let drift_reasons = match evaluate_linux_key_custody(&entries) {
 137:         Ok(()) => Vec::new(),
 138:         Err(reasons) => reasons,
 139:     };
 140:     let overall_ok = drift_reasons.is_empty();
 141:     LinuxKeyCustodyReport {
 142:         schema_version: 1,
 143:         overall_ok,
 144:         entries,
 145:         drift_reasons,
 146:     }
 147: }
 148: 
 149: /// Cross-platform collector. On Linux walks the canonical key custody
 150: /// paths via `std::fs::symlink_metadata` + ownership / mode checks.
 151: /// Off-Linux every entry is reported `Missing` with an explicit
 152: /// "requires a Linux runtime host" reason — same off-platform
 153: /// discipline as the runtime-acls verifier.
 154: pub fn collect_linux_key_custody_report() -> LinuxKeyCustodyReport {
 155:     let entries = vec![
 156:         probe_present_directory(
 157:             "keys directory",
 158:             LINUX_WG_KEYS_DIR,
 159:             0o700,
 160:             "rustynetd",
 161:             "rustynetd",
 162:         ),
 163:         probe_present_file(
 164:             "encrypted WireGuard private key",
 165:             LINUX_WG_ENCRYPTED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH,
 166:             0o600,
 167:             "rustynetd",
 168:             "rustynetd",
 169:         ),
 170:         probe_present_file(
 171:             "WireGuard public key",
 172:             LINUX_WG_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH,
 173:             0o640,
 174:             "rustynetd",
 175:             "rustynetd",
 176:         ),
 177:         probe_forbidden_path(
 178:             "plaintext WireGuard private key (legacy)",
 179:             LINUX_WG_PLAINTEXT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH,
 180:         ),
 181:     ];
 182:     build_linux_key_custody_report(entries)
 183: }
 184: 
 185: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
 186: fn probe_present_directory(
 187:     label: &str,
 188:     path: &str,
 189:     expected_mode: u32,
 190:     expected_owner: &str,
 191:     expected_group: &str,
 192: ) -> LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 193:     use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
 194:     let p = std::path::Path::new(path);
 195:     let metadata = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(p) {
 196:         Ok(m) => m,
 197:         Err(err) => {
 198:             return LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 199:                 label: label.to_string(),
 200:                 path: path.to_string(),
 201:                 requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 202:                 status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 203:                     reason: format!("{path}: {err}"),
 204:                 },
 205:             };
 206:         }
 207:     };
 208:     if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() || !metadata.is_dir() {
 209:         return LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 210:             label: label.to_string(),
 211:             path: path.to_string(),
 212:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 213:             status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 214:                 reason: format!("{label} must be a real directory at {path}"),
 215:                 mode: metadata.mode(),
 216:                 uid: metadata.uid(),
 217:                 gid: metadata.gid(),
 218:             },
 219:         };
 220:     }
 221:     let (uid, gid) = (metadata.uid(), metadata.gid());
 222:     let mode = metadata.mode();
 223:     if let Err(reason) = check_owner_and_mode(
 224:         label,
 225:         mode,
 226:         uid,
 227:         gid,
 228:         expected_mode,
 229:         expected_owner,
 230:         expected_group,
 231:     ) {
 232:         return LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 233:             label: label.to_string(),
 234:             path: path.to_string(),
 235:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 236:             status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 237:                 reason,
 238:                 mode,
 239:                 uid,
 240:                 gid,
 241:             },
 242:         };
 243:     }
 244:     LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 245:         label: label.to_string(),
 246:         path: path.to_string(),
 247:         requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 248:         status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok { mode, uid, gid },
 249:     }
 250: }
 251:

 253: fn probe_present_file(
 254:     label: &str,
 255:     path: &str,
 256:     expected_mode: u32,
 257:     expected_owner: &str,
 258:     expected_group: &str,
 259: ) -> LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 260:     use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
 261:     let p = std::path::Path::new(path);
 262:     let metadata = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(p) {
 263:         Ok(m) => m,
 264:         Err(err) => {
 265:             return LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 266:                 label: label.to_string(),
 267:                 path: path.to_string(),
 268:                 requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 269:                 status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 270:                     reason: format!("{path}: {err}"),
 271:                 },
 272:             };
 273:         }
 274:     };
 275:     if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() || !metadata.is_file() {
 276:         return LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 277:             label: label.to_string(),
 278:             path: path.to_string(),
 279:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 280:             status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 281:                 reason: format!("{label} must be a regular file at {path}"),
 282:                 mode: metadata.mode(),
 283:                 uid: metadata.uid(),
 284:                 gid: metadata.gid(),
 285:             },
 286:         };
 287:     }
 288:     let (uid, gid) = (metadata.uid(), metadata.gid());
 289:     let mode = metadata.mode();
 290:     if let Err(reason) = check_owner_and_mode(
 291:         label,
 292:         mode,
 293:         uid,
 294:         gid,
 295:         expected_mode,
 296:         expected_owner,
 297:         expected_group,
 298:     ) {
 299:         return LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 300:             label: label.to_string(),
 301:             path: path.to_string(),
 302:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 303:             status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 304:                 reason,
 305:                 mode,
 306:                 uid,
 307:                 gid,
 308:             },
 309:         };
 310:     }
 311:     LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 312:         label: label.to_string(),
 313:         path: path.to_string(),
 314:         requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 315:         status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok { mode, uid, gid },
 316:     }
 317: }

 319: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
 320: fn probe_forbidden_path(label: &str, path: &str) -> LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 321:     let p = std::path::Path::new(path);
 322:     if std::fs::symlink_metadata(p).is_ok() {
 323:         return LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 324:             label: label.to_string(),
 325:             path: path.to_string(),
 326:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_ABSENT.to_string(),
 327:             status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Forbidden {
 328:                 reason: format!(
 329:                     "{label} must not exist at rest after Phase E migration; found {path}"
 330:                 ),
 331:             },
 332:         };
 333:     }
 334:     LinuxKeyCustodyEntry {
 335:         label: label.to_string(),
 336:         path: path.to_string(),
 337:         requirement: REQUIREMENT_ABSENT.to_string(),
 338:         status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected,
 339:     }
 340: }
 341: 
 342: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
 343: fn check_owner_and_mode(
 344:     label: &str,
 345:     actual_mode: u32,
 346:     actual_uid: u32,
 347:     actual_gid: u32,
 348:     expected_mode: u32,
 349:     expected_owner: &str,
 350:     expected_group: &str,
 351: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 352:     let perms = actual_mode & 0o7777;
 353:     if perms != expected_mode {
 354:         return Err(format!(
 355:             "{label} mode is 0o{perms:o}, expected 0o{expected_mode:o}"
 356:         ));
 357:     }
 358:     let expected_uid = nix::unistd::User::from_name(expected_owner)
 359:         .ok()
 360:         .flatten()
 361:         .map(|u| u.uid.as_raw())
 362:         .ok_or_else(|| {
 363:             format!("{label} reviewed owner {expected_owner:?} not present on this host")
 364:         })?;
 365:     if actual_uid != expected_uid {
 366:         return Err(format!(
 367:             "{label} owner uid is {actual_uid}, expected {expected_uid} ({expected_owner})"
 368:         ));
 369:     }
 370:     let expected_gid = nix::unistd::Group::from_name(expected_group)
 371:         .ok()
 372:         .flatten()
 373:         .map(|g| g.gid.as_raw())
 374:         .ok_or_else(|| {
 375:             format!("{label} reviewed group {expected_group:?} not present on this host")
 376:         })?;
 377:     if actual_gid != expected_gid {
 378:         return Err(format!(
 379:             "{label} group gid is {actual_gid}, expected {expected_gid} ({expected_group})"
 380:         ));
 381:     }
 382:     Ok(())
 383: }

 402:         },

 548:                 path: LINUX_WG_PLAINTEXT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH.to_string(),
 549:                 requirement: REQUIREMENT_ABSENT.to_string(),
 550:                 status: LinuxKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected,
 551:             },
 552:         ];
 553:         let report = build_linux_key_custody_report(entries);
 554:         assert!(report.overall_ok);
 555:         assert!(report.drift_reasons.is_empty());
 556:         assert_eq!(report.entries.len(), 4);
 557:     }
 558: 
 559:     #[test]
 560:     fn report_serde_round_trips() {
 561:         let report =
 562:             build_linux_key_custody_report(vec![ok_entry("keys directory", LINUX_WG_KEYS_DIR)]);
 563:         let json = serde_json::to_string(&report).expect("serialize");
 564:         let parsed: LinuxKeyCustodyReport = serde_json::from_str(&json).expect("deserialize");
 565:         assert_eq!(parsed, report);
 566:     }
 567: 
 568:     #[test]
 569:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
 570:     fn collector_off_linux_marks_required_entries_missing() {
 571:         let report = collect_linux_key_custody_report();
 572:         assert!(!report.overall_ok);
 573:         // Required (present) entries should report Missing with the
 574:         // off-Linux blocker reason. The forbidden plaintext-key entry
 575:         // is correctly absent off-Linux too.
 576:         assert_eq!(report.entries.len(), 4);
 577:     }
 578: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/linux_mesh_status.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Linux mesh-status verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! Linux parity for `windows_mesh_status`. Reads the daemon's persisted
   6: //! session snapshot at the canonical Linux state path
   7: //! (`/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.state`, mirroring the systemd unit's
   8: //! `RUSTYNET_STATE` env var) and emits a typed JSON report the
   9: //! orchestrator can parse to confirm the Linux peer joined the mesh
  10: //! and observes the expected peers.
  11: //!
  12: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd linux-mesh-status-check`. The
  13: //! orchestrator's `LinuxDaemonProbe` adapter dispatches the
  14: //! `MeshStatus` op to this subcommand.
  15: //!
  16: //! Re-uses `windows_mesh_status::evaluate_windows_mesh_status` as the
  17: //! pure evaluator — the snapshot-load enum + drift-rules are
  18: //! platform-neutral. Only the default state path differs.
  19: 
  20: use crate::resilience::{ResilienceError, load_session_snapshot};
  21: use crate::windows_mesh_status::{WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad, evaluate_windows_mesh_status};
  22: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  23: use std::path::PathBuf;
  24: use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
  25: 
  26: pub const DEFAULT_LINUX_STATE_PATH: &str = "/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.state";
  27: 
  28: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  29: pub struct LinuxMeshStatusReport {
  30:     pub schema_version: u32,
  31:     pub state_path: String,
  32:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  33:     pub snapshot: WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad,
  34:     pub expected_peer_ids: Vec<String>,
  35:     pub max_age_seconds: Option<i64>,
  36:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  37: }
  38: 
  39: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
  40: pub struct LinuxMeshStatusOptions {
  41:     pub state_path: Option<PathBuf>,
  42:     pub expected_peer_ids: Vec<String>,
  43:     pub max_age_seconds: Option<i64>,
  44: }
  45: 
  46: pub fn collect_linux_mesh_status_report(options: &LinuxMeshStatusOptions) -> LinuxMeshStatusReport {
  47:     let state_path: PathBuf = options
  48:         .state_path
  49:         .clone()
  50:         .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(DEFAULT_LINUX_STATE_PATH));
  51:     let state_path_str = state_path.display().to_string();
  52:     let now_unix = current_unix_seconds();
  53:     let snapshot = match load_session_snapshot(state_path.as_path()) {
  54:         Ok(snap) => {
  55:             let age = now_unix.saturating_sub(snap.timestamp_unix as i64);
  56:             WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Ok {
  57:                 timestamp_unix: snap.timestamp_unix,
  58:                 age_seconds: age,
  59:                 peer_ids: snap.peer_ids,
  60:                 selected_exit_node: snap.selected_exit_node,
  61:                 lan_access_enabled: snap.lan_access_enabled,
  62:             }
  63:         }
  64:         Err(ResilienceError::Io) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Missing {
  65:             reason: format!("runtime state path is unreadable on this host: {state_path_str}"),
  66:         },
  67:         Err(ResilienceError::IntegrityMismatch) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::IntegrityMismatch {
  68:             reason: format!("runtime state file failed integrity verification: {state_path_str}"),
  69:         },
  70:         Err(ResilienceError::InvalidFormat) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::InvalidFormat {
  71:             reason: format!(
  72:                 "runtime state file does not match the expected on-disk format: {state_path_str}"
  73:             ),
  74:         },
  75:     };
  76:     let drift_reasons = evaluate_windows_mesh_status(
  77:         &snapshot,
  78:         options.expected_peer_ids.as_slice(),
  79:         options.max_age_seconds,
  80:     );
  81:     let overall_ok = drift_reasons.is_empty();
  82:     LinuxMeshStatusReport {
  83:         schema_version: 1,
  84:         state_path: state_path_str,
  85:         overall_ok,
  86:         snapshot,
  87:         expected_peer_ids: options.expected_peer_ids.clone(),
  88:         max_age_seconds: options.max_age_seconds,
  89:         drift_reasons,
  90:     }
  91: }
  92: 
  93: fn current_unix_seconds() -> i64 {
  94:     SystemTime::now()
  95:         .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
  96:         .map(|d| d.as_secs() as i64)
  97:         .unwrap_or(0)
  98: }
  99:
