===== /crates/rustynetd/src/linux_runtime_acls.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Linux runtime ACL verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! Mirror of `windows_paths::collect_windows_runtime_acl_report` for
   6: //! Linux hosts. Walks the canonical Linux runtime roots used by the
   7: //! daemon's systemd unit + e2e bootstrap scripts, and confirms each
   8: //! root exists, is a real directory, has the reviewed owner / group,
   9: //! and matches the reviewed mode.
  10: //!
  11: //! The reviewed posture comes from two sources of truth:
  12: //!
  13: //! * `scripts/systemd/rustynetd.service` — sets `User=rustynetd`,
  14: //!   `Group=rustynetd`, `StateDirectoryMode=0700`, and `ReadWritePaths=`.
  15: //! * `scripts/e2e/live_lab_common.sh` — the bootstrap install commands:
  16: //!     ```text
  17: //!     install -d -m 0750 -o root      -g rustynetd /etc/rustynet
  18: //!     install -d -m 0700 -o rustynetd -g rustynetd /var/lib/rustynet
  19: //!     ```
  20: //!
  21: //! Off-Linux the report's per-root status is `Missing` with an explicit
  22: //! "requires a Linux runtime host" reason so the orchestrator surfaces
  23: //! a clear blocker rather than a fabricated answer.
  24: //!
  25: //! This is the Linux parity for the W1.1 Windows runtime-ACL verifier.
  26: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd linux-runtime-acls-check`. The
  27: //! orchestrator's `LinuxDaemonProbe` adapter dispatches the
  28: //! `RuntimeAcls` op to this subcommand.
  29: 
  30: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  31: 
  32: /// Reviewed Linux runtime roots. Each entry is
  33: /// `(path, label, expected_mode, expected_owner, expected_group)` where
  34: /// `expected_mode` is the directory mode bits (octal in source for
  35: /// readability; persisted as decimal-mode in JSON).
  36: ///
  37: /// `expected_owner` and `expected_group` are the textual usernames the
  38: /// systemd unit + bootstrap scripts use. The verifier resolves them to
  39: /// uid / gid at probe time so a host with a different uid mapping for
  40: /// `rustynetd` (eg. distros that pre-allocate different system uids)
  41: /// still passes when the *name* matches the reviewed posture.
  42: const LINUX_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ACL_ROOTS: &[(&str, &str, u32, &str, &str)] = &[
  43:     (
  44:         "/var/lib/rustynet",
  45:         "state root",
  46:         0o700,
  47:         "rustynetd",
  48:         "rustynetd",
  49:     ),
  50:     ("/etc/rustynet", "config root", 0o750, "root", "rustynetd"),
  51: ];
  52: 
  53: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  54: #[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
  55: pub enum LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus {
  56:     Ok,
  57:     Missing { reason: String },
  58:     Drifted { reason: String },
  59: }
  60: 
  61: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  62: pub struct LinuxRuntimeAclRootEntry {
  63:     pub label: String,
  64:     pub path: String,
  65:     #[serde(flatten)]
  66:     pub status: LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus,
  67: }
  68: 
  69: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  70: pub struct LinuxRuntimeAclReport {
  71:     pub schema_version: u32,
  72:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  73:     pub roots: Vec<LinuxRuntimeAclRootEntry>,
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// Diagnostic walk over the canonical Linux runtime roots. Collects
  77: /// per-root status instead of failing fast so a remote orchestrator
  78: /// can render a complete drift report in a single round-trip.
  79: pub fn collect_linux_runtime_acl_report() -> LinuxRuntimeAclReport {
  80:     let roots = LINUX_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ACL_ROOTS
  81:         .iter()
  82:         .map(|(path_str, label, mode, owner, group)| {
  83:             let status = inspect_runtime_root_status(path_str, label, *mode, owner, group);
  84:             LinuxRuntimeAclRootEntry {
  85:                 label: (*label).to_string(),
  86:                 path: (*path_str).to_string(),
  87:                 status,
  88:             }
  89:         })
  90:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  91:     let overall_ok = roots
  92:         .iter()
  93:         .all(|entry| matches!(entry.status, LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok));
  94:     LinuxRuntimeAclReport {
  95:         schema_version: 1,
  96:         overall_ok,
  97:         roots,
  98:     }
  99: }
 100: 
 101: /// Reviewed posture for one runtime root, resolved at probe time so
 102: /// the evaluator can stay platform-agnostic.
 103: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 104: pub struct LinuxRuntimeAclExpectation {
 105:     pub mode: u32,
 106:     pub owner_uid: u32,
 107:     pub group_gid: u32,
 108: }
 109: 
 110: /// Live metadata snapshot of one runtime root. Fields mirror the
 111: /// `std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt` view so the evaluator can stay
 112: /// `cfg`-free.
 113: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 114: pub struct LinuxRuntimeAclSnapshot {
 115:     pub mode: u32,
 116:     pub uid: u32,
 117:     pub gid: u32,
 118:     pub is_dir: bool,
 119:     pub is_symlink: bool,
 120: }
 121: 
 122: /// Pure evaluator: takes a fully-populated metadata snapshot and
 123: /// confirms it matches the reviewed posture. Splitting this out from
 124: /// the syscall-driven probe keeps unit tests deterministic — the
 125: /// fixture builds the snapshot in memory and the evaluator validates.
 126: pub fn evaluate_linux_runtime_acl_metadata(
 127:     label: &str,
 128:     expected: LinuxRuntimeAclExpectation,
 129:     actual: LinuxRuntimeAclSnapshot,
 130: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 131:     if actual.is_symlink {
 132:         return Err(format!("{label} must be a real directory, not a symlink"));
 133:     }
 134:     if !actual.is_dir {
 135:         return Err(format!("{label} must be a directory, not a file"));
 136:     }
 137:     let actual_perms = actual.mode & 0o7777;
 138:     if actual_perms != expected.mode {
 139:         return Err(format!(
 140:             "{label} mode is 0o{actual_perms:o}, expected 0o{:o}",
 141:             expected.mode
 142:         ));
 143:     }
 144:     if actual.uid != expected.owner_uid {
 145:         return Err(format!(
 146:             "{label} owner uid is {}, expected {}",
 147:             actual.uid, expected.owner_uid
 148:         ));
 149:     }
 150:     if actual.gid != expected.group_gid {
 151:         return Err(format!(
 152:             "{label} group gid is {}, expected {}",
 153:             actual.gid, expected.group_gid
 154:         ));
 155:     }
 156:     Ok(())
 157: }
 158: 
 159: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
 160: fn inspect_runtime_root_status(
 161:     path_str: &str,
 162:     label: &str,
 163:     expected_mode: u32,
 164:     expected_owner: &str,
 165:     expected_group: &str,
 166: ) -> LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus {
 167:     use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
 168:     let path = std::path::Path::new(path_str);
 169:     let metadata = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 170:         Ok(m) => m,
 171:         Err(err) => {
 172:             return LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Missing {
 173:                 reason: format!(
 174:                     "{label} must exist before rustynetd starts on Linux ({path_str}): {err}"
 175:                 ),
 176:             };
 177:         }
 178:     };
 179:     let is_symlink = metadata.file_type().is_symlink();
 180:     let is_dir = metadata.is_dir();
 181: 
 182:     let expected_owner_uid = match resolve_uid_for_username(expected_owner) {
 183:         Some(uid) => uid,
 184:         None => {
 185:             return LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted {
 186:                 reason: format!(
 187:                     "{label} reviewed owner {expected_owner:?} is not present on this host"
 188:                 ),
 189:             };
 190:         }
 191:     };
 192:     let expected_group_gid = match resolve_gid_for_groupname(expected_group) {
 193:         Some(gid) => gid,
 194:         None => {
 195:             return LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted {
 196:                 reason: format!(
 197:                     "{label} reviewed group {expected_group:?} is not present on this host"
 198:                 ),
 199:             };
 200:         }
 201:     };
 202: 
 203:     match evaluate_linux_runtime_acl_metadata(
 204:         label,
 205:         LinuxRuntimeAclExpectation {
 206:             mode: expected_mode,
 207:             owner_uid: expected_owner_uid,
 208:             group_gid: expected_group_gid,
 209:         },
 210:         LinuxRuntimeAclSnapshot {
 211:             mode: metadata.mode(),
 212:             uid: metadata.uid(),
 213:             gid: metadata.gid(),
 214:             is_dir,
 215:             is_symlink,
 216:         },
 217:     ) {
 218:         Ok(()) => LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok,
 219:         Err(reason) => LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted { reason },
 220:     }
 221: }
 222: 
 223: #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
 224: fn inspect_runtime_root_status(
 225:     path_str: &str,
 226:     label: &str,
 227:     _expected_mode: u32,
 228:     _expected_owner: &str,
 229:     _expected_group: &str,
 230: ) -> LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus {
 231:     LinuxRuntimeAclRootStatus::Missing {
 232:         reason: format!(
 233:             "{label} probe at {path_str} requires a Linux runtime host; \
 234:              linux-runtime-acls-check is not meaningful off-Linux"
 235:         ),
 236:     }
 237: }
 238: 
 239: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
 240: fn resolve_uid_for_username(username: &str) -> Option<u32> {
 241:     nix::unistd::User::from_name(username)
 242:         .ok()
 243:         .flatten()
 244:         .map(|user| user.uid.as_raw())
 245: }
 246: 
 247: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
 248: fn resolve_gid_for_groupname(groupname: &str) -> Option<u32> {
 249:     nix::unistd::Group::from_name(groupname)
 250:         .ok()
 251:         .flatten()
 252:         .map(|group| group.gid.as_raw())
 253: }
 254:

 403:     #[test]

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/linux_service_hardening.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Linux service-hardening verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! Linux parity for `windows_service_hardening`. Confirms the live
   6: //! systemd unit registration for `rustynetd.service` matches the
   7: //! reviewed hardening directives baked into
   8: //! `scripts/systemd/rustynetd.service`. Drift here means an operator
   9: //! (or distro packaging step) has weakened the unit relative to the
  10: //! reviewed posture.
  11: //!
  12: //! The collector dispatches `systemctl show rustynetd.service` and
  13: //! parses the `key=value` output. The pure evaluator takes a parsed
  14: //! property map and walks the reviewed-property table, returning
  15: //! every drift reason in a single pass.
  16: //!
  17: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd linux-service-hardening-check`.
  18: //! The orchestrator's `LinuxDaemonProbe` adapter dispatches the
  19: //! `ServiceHardening` op to this subcommand.
  20: //!
  21: //! Off-Linux the collector emits an unprobed report with an explicit
  22: //! "requires a Linux runtime host" reason.
  23: 
  24: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  25: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
  26: 
  27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  28: pub struct LinuxServiceHardeningReport {
  29:     pub schema_version: u32,
  30:     pub service_name: String,
  31:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  32:     /// True when the verifier ran a `systemctl show` probe; false when
  33:     /// running off-Linux or `systemctl` is unavailable.
  34:     pub probed: bool,
  35:     pub probe_reason: Option<String>,
  36:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  37:     /// The full parsed property map (sorted) so an operator can
  38:     /// see exactly what `systemctl show` reported. Useful for
  39:     /// post-mortem when drift_reasons is non-empty.
  40:     pub observed: BTreeMap<String, String>,
  41: }
  42: 
  43: /// Reviewed systemd-unit hardening directives. Each entry pins one
  44: /// `key` and the expected `value`. Pulled from the reviewed
  45: /// `scripts/systemd/rustynetd.service` unit file (Phase E hardening).
  46: const REVIEWED_HARDENING_DIRECTIVES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
  47:     ("User", "rustynetd"),
  48:     ("Group", "rustynetd"),
  49:     ("NoNewPrivileges", "yes"),
  50:     ("PrivateTmp", "yes"),
  51:     ("PrivateDevices", "yes"),
  52:     ("ProtectSystem", "strict"),
  53:     ("ProtectHome", "yes"),
  54:     ("ProtectControlGroups", "yes"),
  55:     ("ProtectKernelTunables", "yes"),
  56:     ("ProtectKernelModules", "yes"),
  57:     ("ProtectKernelLogs", "yes"),
  58:     ("MemoryDenyWriteExecute", "yes"),
  59:     ("LockPersonality", "yes"),
  60:     ("RestrictSUIDSGID", "yes"),
  61:     ("RestrictRealtime", "yes"),
  62:     ("SystemCallArchitectures", "native"),
  63:     // Empty CapabilityBoundingSet means "no caps inherited"; systemctl
  64:     // reports this as the empty string.
  65:     ("CapabilityBoundingSet", ""),
  66:     ("AmbientCapabilities", ""),
  67:     ("UMask", "0077"),
  68: ];
  69: 
  70: pub const REVIEWED_SERVICE_NAME: &str = "rustynetd.service";
  71: 
  72: /// Pure evaluator: walks the reviewed-property table against a
  73: /// parsed property map. Returns every drift reason in one pass.
  74: pub fn evaluate_linux_service_hardening(observed: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Vec<String> {
  75:     let mut reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  76:     if observed.is_empty() {
  77:         reasons
  78:             .push("systemctl show output contained no parseable key=value properties".to_string());
  79:         return reasons;
  80:     }
  81:     for (key, expected) in REVIEWED_HARDENING_DIRECTIVES {
  82:         match observed.get(*key) {
  83:             Some(actual) if actual == expected => {}
  84:             Some(actual) => {
  85:                 reasons.push(format!(
  86:                     "{key} drifted: expected {expected:?}, observed {actual:?}"
  87:                 ));
  88:             }
  89:             None => {
  90:                 reasons.push(format!(
  91:                     "{key} missing from systemctl show output (expected {expected:?})"
  92:                 ));
  93:             }
  94:         }
  95:     }
  96:     reasons
  97: }
  98: 
  99: /// Parse `systemctl show`'s `key=value` line-oriented output into a
 100: /// property map. systemd emits one property per line; multiline
 101: /// values are escaped with `\n`/`\\`. The reviewed directives we care
 102: /// about are scalar so naive split-on-`=` works; the parser returns
 103: /// the empty value for lines like `Foo=` (which `CapabilityBoundingSet`
 104: /// emits in the reviewed posture).
 105: pub fn parse_systemctl_show_output(body: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
 106:     let mut map: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
 107:     for line in body.lines() {
 108:         if let Some((key, value)) = line.split_once('=') {
 109:             map.insert(key.trim().to_string(), value.trim().to_string());
 110:         }
 111:     }
 112:     map
 113: }
 114: 
 115: pub fn build_linux_service_hardening_report(
 116:     probed: bool,
 117:     probe_reason: Option<String>,
 118:     observed: BTreeMap<String, String>,
 119: ) -> LinuxServiceHardeningReport {
 120:     let drift_reasons = if probed {
 121:         evaluate_linux_service_hardening(&observed)
 122:     } else {
 123:         vec![probe_reason.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {
 124:             "systemctl show was not run; service hardening posture unknown".to_string()
 125:         })]
 126:     };
 127:     let overall_ok = probed && drift_reasons.is_empty();
 128:     LinuxServiceHardeningReport {
 129:         schema_version: 1,
 130:         service_name: REVIEWED_SERVICE_NAME.to_string(),
 131:         overall_ok,
 132:         probed,
 133:         probe_reason,
 134:         drift_reasons,
 135:         observed,
 136:     }
 137: }
 138: 
 139: /// Collector: on Linux runs `systemctl show <service>` and parses the
 140: /// output. Off-Linux emits an unprobed report with the off-platform
 141: /// blocker reason.
 142: pub fn collect_linux_service_hardening_report() -> LinuxServiceHardeningReport {
 143:     run_systemctl_show_probe()
 144: }
 145: 
 146: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
 147: fn run_systemctl_show_probe() -> LinuxServiceHardeningReport {
 148:     use std::process::Command;
 149:     let output = match Command::new("systemctl")
 150:         .arg("show")
 151:         .arg(REVIEWED_SERVICE_NAME)
 152:         .output()
 153:     {
 154:         Ok(o) => o,
 155:         Err(err) => {
 156:             return build_linux_service_hardening_report(
 157:                 false,
 158:                 Some(format!(
 159:                     "systemctl show {REVIEWED_SERVICE_NAME} failed to spawn: {err}"
 160:                 )),
 161:                 BTreeMap::new(),
 162:             );
 163:         }
 164:     };
 165:     if !output.status.success() {
 166:         let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).into_owned();
 167:         return build_linux_service_hardening_report(
 168:             false,
 169:             Some(format!(
 170:                 "systemctl show {REVIEWED_SERVICE_NAME} exited non-zero: {} (stderr: {})",
 171:                 output
 172:                     .status
 173:                     .code()
 174:                     .map(|c| c.to_string())
 175:                     .unwrap_or_else(|| "signal".to_string()),
 176:                 stderr.trim()
 177:             )),
 178:             BTreeMap::new(),
 179:         );
 180:     }
 181:     let body = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).into_owned();
 182:     let observed = parse_systemctl_show_output(body.as_str());
 183:     build_linux_service_hardening_report(true, None, observed)
 184: }
 185: 
 186: #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
 187: fn run_systemctl_show_probe() -> LinuxServiceHardeningReport {
 188:     build_linux_service_hardening_report(
 189:         false,
 190:         Some(
 191:             "linux-service-hardening-check requires a Linux runtime host with systemctl"
 192:                 .to_string(),
 193:         ),
 194:         BTreeMap::new(),
 195:     )
 196: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/macos_authenticode.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! macOS authenticode-equivalent stub.
   4: //!
   5: //! Authenticode is a Windows-specific mechanism. macOS uses Gatekeeper
   6: //! (code signing + notarization) as the nearest equivalent, but Gatekeeper
   7: //! verification is performed at first-launch time by the OS, not by the
   8: //! running daemon at runtime. The macOS runtime verifier does not
   9: //! re-evaluate code signatures on already-running binaries.
  10: //!
  11: //! Rather than reject the `Authenticode` op on macOS, the daemon exposes
  12: //! a `macos-authenticode-check` subcommand that always emits a typed
  13: //! `applicable: false` report. This keeps the `MacosDaemonProbe::build_argv`
  14: //! shape uniform with Linux and Windows — every op resolves to argv — and
  15: //! gives the orchestrator a consistent JSON structure to consume.
  16: //!
  17: //! A future slice could wire `codesign --verify` here, at which point
  18: //! `applicable` would flip to `true`.
  19: 
  20: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  21: 
  22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  23: pub struct MacosAuthenticodeReport {
  24:     pub schema_version: u32,
  25:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  26:     /// Always `false` today: macOS Gatekeeper operates at launch time,
  27:     /// not as a runtime binary attestation mechanism.
  28:     pub applicable: bool,
  29:     pub reason: String,
  30: }
  31: 
  32: pub fn collect_macos_authenticode_report() -> MacosAuthenticodeReport {
  33:     MacosAuthenticodeReport {
  34:         schema_version: 1,
  35:         overall_ok: true,
  36:         applicable: false,
  37:         reason: "macOS does not enforce binary signatures at runtime via a mechanism \
  38:                  analogous to Windows Authenticode. Gatekeeper verification runs at \
  39:                  first-launch time. A runtime codesign --verify probe is not part of \
  40:                  the reviewed macOS posture today."
  41:             .to_string(),
  42:     }
  43: }
  44: 
  45: #[cfg(test)]
  46: mod tests {
  47:     use super::*;
  48: 
  49:     #[test]
  50:     fn report_marks_overall_ok_with_applicable_false() {
  51:         let report = collect_macos_authenticode_report();
  52:         assert!(
  53:             report.overall_ok,
  54:             "applicable=false must not fail overall_ok"
  55:         );
  56:         assert!(!report.applicable);
  57:         assert!(!report.reason.is_empty());
  58:     }
  59: 
  60:     #[test]
  61:     fn report_serde_round_trips() {
  62:         let report = collect_macos_authenticode_report();
  63:         let json = serde_json::to_string(&report).expect("serialize");
  64:         let parsed: MacosAuthenticodeReport = serde_json::from_str(&json).expect("deserialize");
  65:         assert_eq!(parsed, report);
  66:     }
  67: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/macos_dns_failclosed.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! macOS DNS fail-closed verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! macOS parity for `linux_dns_failclosed`. Reads `/etc/resolv.conf`
   6: //! (macOS populates this via mDNSResponder in most configurations) and
   7: //! confirms every nameserver is loopback-only. Off-loopback nameservers
   8: //! mean DNS queries that should stay inside the mesh can leak.
   9: //!
  10: //! The macOS resolver stack is more complex than Linux (mDNSResponder,
  11: //! scutil, /etc/resolv.conf). This verifier reads /etc/resolv.conf as
  12: //! the lowest-common-denominator that libc-using processes consult. A
  13: //! future slice can extend to `scutil --dns` for the full picture.
  14: //!
  15: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd macos-dns-failclosed-check`. The
  16: //! orchestrator's `MacosDaemonProbe` dispatches `DnsFailclosed` here.
  17: 
  18: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  19: use std::net::IpAddr;
  20: 
  21: pub const REVIEWED_RESOLV_CONF_PATH: &str = "/etc/resolv.conf";
  22: 
  23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  24: pub struct MacosDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
  25:     pub resolv_conf_path: String,
  26:     pub resolv_conf_present: bool,
  27:     pub nameservers: Vec<String>,
  28:     pub search_domains: Vec<String>,
  29:     pub loopback_resolver_advertised: bool,
  30: }
  31: 
  32: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  33: pub struct MacosDnsFailclosedReport {
  34:     pub schema_version: u32,
  35:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  36:     pub snapshot: MacosDnsFailclosedSnapshot,
  37:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  38: }
  39: 
  40: /// Pure evaluator: every nameserver must be loopback.
  41: pub fn evaluate_macos_dns_failclosed(nameservers: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
  42:     let mut reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  43:     for ns in nameservers {
  44:         let addr: Option<IpAddr> = ns.trim().parse().ok();
  45:         match addr {
  46:             Some(ip) if ip.is_loopback() => {}
  47:             Some(ip) => {
  48:                 reasons.push(format!(
  49:                     "nameserver {ip} is not loopback; DNS queries may leak outside the mesh"
  50:                 ));
  51:             }
  52:             None => {
  53:                 reasons.push(format!("nameserver entry {ns:?} is not a valid IP address"));
  54:             }
  55:         }
  56:     }
  57:     reasons
  58: }
  59: 
  60: pub fn parse_resolv_conf(body: &str) -> (Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
  61:     let mut nameservers: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  62:     let mut search_domains: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  63:     for line in body.lines() {
  64:         let line = line.trim();
  65:         if line.starts_with('#') || line.is_empty() {
  66:             continue;
  67:         }
  68:         if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("nameserver") {
  69:             let ns = rest.trim().to_string();
  70:             if !ns.is_empty() {
  71:                 nameservers.push(ns);
  72:             }
  73:         } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("search") {
  74:             for domain in rest.split_whitespace() {
  75:                 search_domains.push(domain.to_string());
  76:             }
  77:         } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("domain") {
  78:             for domain in rest.split_whitespace() {
  79:                 search_domains.push(domain.to_string());
  80:             }
  81:         }
  82:     }
  83:     (nameservers, search_domains)
  84: }
  85: 
  86: pub fn collect_macos_dns_failclosed_snapshot() -> MacosDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
  87:     let resolv_conf_path = REVIEWED_RESOLV_CONF_PATH.to_string();
  88:     match std::fs::read_to_string(REVIEWED_RESOLV_CONF_PATH) {
  89:         Ok(body) => {
  90:             let (nameservers, search_domains) = parse_resolv_conf(&body);
  91:             MacosDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
  92:                 resolv_conf_path,
  93:                 resolv_conf_present: true,
  94:                 nameservers,
  95:                 search_domains,
  96:                 loopback_resolver_advertised: true,
  97:             }
  98:         }
  99:         Err(_) => MacosDnsFailclosedSnapshot {
 100:             resolv_conf_path,
 101:             resolv_conf_present: false,
 102:             nameservers: Vec::new(),
 103:             search_domains: Vec::new(),
 104:             loopback_resolver_advertised: false,
 105:         },
 106:     }
 107: }
 108: 
 109: pub fn build_macos_dns_failclosed_report(
 110:     snapshot: MacosDnsFailclosedSnapshot,
 111: ) -> MacosDnsFailclosedReport {
 112:     let mut drift_reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
 113:     if !snapshot.resolv_conf_present {
 114:         drift_reasons.push(format!(
 115:             "{} is not present; DNS fail-closed posture cannot be verified",
 116:             snapshot.resolv_conf_path
 117:         ));
 118:     } else {
 119:         let ns_drift = evaluate_macos_dns_failclosed(&snapshot.nameservers);
 120:         drift_reasons.extend(ns_drift);
 121:     }
 122:     let overall_ok = drift_reasons.is_empty();
 123:     MacosDnsFailclosedReport {
 124:         schema_version: 1,
 125:         overall_ok,
 126:         snapshot,
 127:         drift_reasons,
 128:     }
 129: }
 130:

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/macos_key_custody.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! macOS key-custody verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! macOS parity for `linux_key_custody`. Validates that on-disk key
   6: //! material on a macOS runtime host matches the reviewed custody contract:
   7: //!
   8: //! * the encrypted WireGuard private key exists at
   9: //!   `/usr/local/var/rustynet/keys/wireguard.key.enc`, owned by
  10: //!   `rustynetd:rustynetd`, mode `0600`;
  11: //! * the WireGuard public key exists at
  12: //!   `/usr/local/var/rustynet/keys/wireguard.pub`, owned by
  13: //!   `rustynetd:rustynetd`, mode `0640` or `0600`;
  14: //! * the keys directory is a real directory owned by `rustynetd:rustynetd`,
  15: //!   mode `0700`;
  16: //! * the plaintext private key must be absent at rest.
  17: //!
  18: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd macos-key-custody-check`. The
  19: //! orchestrator's `MacosDaemonProbe` dispatches the `KeyCustody` op here.
  20: 
  21: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  22: 
  23: pub const MACOS_WG_KEYS_DIR: &str = "/usr/local/var/rustynet/keys";
  24: pub const MACOS_WG_ENCRYPTED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH: &str =
  25:     "/usr/local/var/rustynet/keys/wireguard.key.enc";
  26: pub const MACOS_WG_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH: &str = "/usr/local/var/rustynet/keys/wireguard.pub";
  27: /// Legacy plaintext private key — must NOT exist at rest after migration.
  28: pub const MACOS_WG_PLAINTEXT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH: &str = "/usr/local/var/rustynet/keys/wireguard.key";
  29: 
  30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  31: #[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
  32: pub enum MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus {
  33:     Ok {
  34:         mode: u32,
  35:         uid: u32,
  36:         gid: u32,
  37:     },
  38:     Missing {
  39:         reason: String,
  40:     },
  41:     Invalid {
  42:         reason: String,
  43:         mode: u32,
  44:         uid: u32,
  45:         gid: u32,
  46:     },
  47:     Forbidden {
  48:         reason: String,
  49:     },
  50:     AbsentAsExpected,
  51: }
  52: 
  53: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  54: pub struct MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
  55:     pub label: String,
  56:     pub path: String,
  57:     pub expected: String,
  58:     #[serde(flatten)]
  59:     pub status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus,
  60: }
  61: 
  62: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  63: pub struct MacosKeyCustodyReport {
  64:     pub schema_version: u32,
  65:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  66:     pub entries: Vec<MacosKeyCustodyEntry>,
  67: }
  68: 
  69: pub fn collect_macos_key_custody_report() -> MacosKeyCustodyReport {
  70:     let entries = build_entries();
  71:     let overall_ok = entries.iter().all(|e| {
  72:         matches!(
  73:             e.status,
  74:             MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok { .. } | MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected
  75:         )
  76:     });
  77:     MacosKeyCustodyReport {
  78:         schema_version: 1,
  79:         overall_ok,
  80:         entries,
  81:     }
  82: }
  83: 
  84: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
  85: fn build_entries() -> Vec<MacosKeyCustodyEntry> {
  86:     vec![
  87:         probe_required_dir(
  88:             MACOS_WG_KEYS_DIR,
  89:             "keys dir",
  90:             0o700,
  91:             "rustynetd",
  92:             "rustynetd",
  93:         ),
  94:         probe_required_file(
  95:             MACOS_WG_ENCRYPTED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH,
  96:             "encrypted private key",
  97:             &[0o600],
  98:             "rustynetd",
  99:             "rustynetd",
 100:         ),
 101:         probe_required_file(
 102:             MACOS_WG_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH,
 103:             "public key",
 104:             &[0o640, 0o600],
 105:             "rustynetd",
 106:             "rustynetd",
 107:         ),
 108:         probe_forbidden_file(
 109:             MACOS_WG_PLAINTEXT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH,
 110:             "plaintext private key (forbidden)",
 111:         ),
 112:     ]
 113: }
 114: 
 115: #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
 116: fn build_entries() -> Vec<MacosKeyCustodyEntry> {
 117:     let off_platform_reason = "requires a macOS runtime host; macos-key-custody-check \
 118:                                is not meaningful off-macOS";
 119:     vec![
 120:         MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 121:             label: "keys dir".to_string(),
 122:             path: MACOS_WG_KEYS_DIR.to_string(),
 123:             expected: "present".to_string(),
 124:             status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 125:                 reason: off_platform_reason.to_string(),
 126:             },
 127:         },
 128:         MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 129:             label: "encrypted private key".to_string(),
 130:             path: MACOS_WG_ENCRYPTED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH.to_string(),
 131:             expected: "present".to_string(),
 132:             status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 133:                 reason: off_platform_reason.to_string(),
 134:             },
 135:         },
 136:         MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 137:             label: "public key".to_string(),
 138:             path: MACOS_WG_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH.to_string(),
 139:             expected: "present".to_string(),
 140:             status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 141:                 reason: off_platform_reason.to_string(),
 142:             },
 143:         },
 144:         MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 145:             label: "plaintext private key (forbidden)".to_string(),
 146:             path: MACOS_WG_PLAINTEXT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH.to_string(),
 147:             expected: "absent".to_string(),
 148:             status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 149:                 reason: off_platform_reason.to_string(),
 150:             },
 151:         },
 152:     ]
 153: }

 155: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 156: fn resolve_uid(username: &str) -> Option<u32> {
 157:     nix::unistd::User::from_name(username)
 158:         .ok()
 159:         .flatten()
 160:         .map(|u| u.uid.as_raw())
 161: }
 162: 
 163: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 164: fn resolve_gid(groupname: &str) -> Option<u32> {
 165:     nix::unistd::Group::from_name(groupname)
 166:         .ok()
 167:         .flatten()
 168:         .map(|g| g.gid.as_raw())
 169: }
 170: 
 171: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 172: fn probe_required_dir(
 173:     path: &'static str,
 174:     label: &'static str,
 175:     mode: u32,
 176:     owner: &str,
 177:     group: &str,
 178: ) -> MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 179:     use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
 180:     let meta = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 181:         Ok(m) => m,
 182:         Err(err) => {
 183:             return MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 184:                 label: label.to_string(),
 185:                 path: path.to_string(),
 186:                 expected: "present".to_string(),
 187:                 status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 188:                     reason: format!("{label} not found at {path}: {err}"),
 189:                 },
 190:             };
 191:         }
 192:     };
 193:     let uid = meta.uid();
 194:     let gid = meta.gid();
 195:     let actual_mode = meta.mode() & 0o7777;
 196:     let expected_uid = resolve_uid(owner).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 197:     let expected_gid = resolve_gid(group).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 198:     if meta.file_type().is_symlink()
 199:         || !meta.is_dir()
 200:         || actual_mode != mode
 201:         || uid != expected_uid
 202:         || gid != expected_gid
 203:     {
 204:         return MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 205:             label: label.to_string(),
 206:             path: path.to_string(),
 207:             expected: "present".to_string(),
 208:             status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 209:                 reason: format!(
 210:                     "{label} mode/owner/type mismatch: mode=0o{actual_mode:o} uid={uid} gid={gid}"
 211:                 ),
 212:                 mode: actual_mode,
 213:                 uid,
 214:                 gid,
 215:             },
 216:         };
 217:     }
 218:     MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 219:         label: label.to_string(),
 220:         path: path.to_string(),
 221:         expected: "present".to_string(),
 222:         status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok {
 223:             mode: actual_mode,
 224:             uid,
 225:             gid,
 226:         },
 227:     }
 228: }
 229: 
 230: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 231: fn probe_required_file(
 232:     path: &'static str,
 233:     label: &'static str,
 234:     allowed_modes: &[u32],
 235:     owner: &str,
 236:     group: &str,
 237: ) -> MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 238:     use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
 239:     let meta = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 240:         Ok(m) => m,
 241:         Err(err) => {
 242:             return MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 243:                 label: label.to_string(),
 244:                 path: path.to_string(),
 245:                 expected: "present".to_string(),
 246:                 status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 247:                     reason: format!("{label} not found at {path}: {err}"),
 248:                 },
 249:             };
 250:         }
 251:     };
 252:     let uid = meta.uid();
 253:     let gid = meta.gid();
 254:     let actual_mode = meta.mode() & 0o7777;
 255:     let expected_uid = resolve_uid(owner).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 256:     let expected_gid = resolve_gid(group).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 257:     let mode_ok = allowed_modes.contains(&actual_mode);
 258:     if meta.file_type().is_symlink()
 259:         || !meta.is_file()
 260:         || !mode_ok
 261:         || uid != expected_uid
 262:         || gid != expected_gid
 263:     {
 264:         return MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 265:             label: label.to_string(),
 266:             path: path.to_string(),
 267:             expected: "present".to_string(),
 268:             status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 269:                 reason: format!(
 270:                     "{label} mode/owner/type mismatch: mode=0o{actual_mode:o} uid={uid} gid={gid}"
 271:                 ),
 272:                 mode: actual_mode,
 273:                 uid,
 274:                 gid,
 275:             },
 276:         };
 277:     }
 278:     MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 279:         label: label.to_string(),
 280:         path: path.to_string(),
 281:         expected: "present".to_string(),
 282:         status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok {
 283:             mode: actual_mode,
 284:             uid,
 285:             gid,
 286:         },
 287:     }
 288: }
 289: 
 290: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 291: fn probe_forbidden_file(path: &'static str, label: &'static str) -> MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 292:     match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 293:         Err(_) => MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 294:             label: label.to_string(),
 295:             path: path.to_string(),
 296:             expected: "absent".to_string(),
 297:             status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected,
 298:         },
 299:         Ok(_) => MacosKeyCustodyEntry {
 300:             label: label.to_string(),
 301:             path: path.to_string(),
 302:             expected: "absent".to_string(),
 303:             status: MacosKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Forbidden {
 304:                 reason: format!(
 305:                     "plaintext private key at {path} must not exist at rest — \
 306:                      Phase E migrated runtime key custody to encrypted-at-rest"
 307:                 ),
 308:             },
 309:         },
 310:     }
 311: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/macos_mesh_status.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! macOS mesh-status verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! macOS parity for `linux_mesh_status`. Reads the daemon's persisted
   6: //! session snapshot at the canonical macOS state path
   7: //! (`/usr/local/var/rustynet/rustynetd.state`) and emits a typed JSON
   8: //! report the orchestrator can parse to confirm the macOS peer joined
   9: //! the mesh and observes the expected peers.
  10: //!
  11: //! Re-uses `windows_mesh_status::evaluate_windows_mesh_status` as the
  12: //! pure evaluator — the snapshot-load enum + drift-rules are
  13: //! platform-neutral. Only the default state path differs.
  14: //!
  15: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd macos-mesh-status-check`. The
  16: //! orchestrator's `MacosDaemonProbe` dispatches the `MeshStatus` op here.
  17: 
  18: use crate::resilience::{ResilienceError, load_session_snapshot};
  19: use crate::windows_mesh_status::{WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad, evaluate_windows_mesh_status};
  20: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  21: use std::path::PathBuf;
  22: use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
  23: 
  24: pub const DEFAULT_MACOS_STATE_PATH: &str = "/usr/local/var/rustynet/rustynetd.state";
  25: 
  26: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  27: pub struct MacosMeshStatusReport {
  28:     pub schema_version: u32,
  29:     pub state_path: String,
  30:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  31:     pub snapshot: WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad,
  32:     pub expected_peer_ids: Vec<String>,
  33:     pub max_age_seconds: Option<i64>,
  34:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  35: }
  36: 
  37: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
  38: pub struct MacosMeshStatusOptions {
  39:     pub state_path: Option<PathBuf>,
  40:     pub expected_peer_ids: Vec<String>,
  41:     pub max_age_seconds: Option<i64>,
  42: }
  43: 
  44: pub fn collect_macos_mesh_status_report(options: &MacosMeshStatusOptions) -> MacosMeshStatusReport {
  45:     let state_path: PathBuf = options
  46:         .state_path
  47:         .clone()
  48:         .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(DEFAULT_MACOS_STATE_PATH));
  49:     let state_path_str = state_path.display().to_string();
  50:     let now_unix = current_unix_seconds();
  51:     let snapshot = match load_session_snapshot(state_path.as_path()) {
  52:         Ok(snap) => {
  53:             let age = now_unix.saturating_sub(snap.timestamp_unix as i64);
  54:             WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Ok {
  55:                 timestamp_unix: snap.timestamp_unix,
  56:                 age_seconds: age,
  57:                 peer_ids: snap.peer_ids,
  58:                 selected_exit_node: snap.selected_exit_node,
  59:                 lan_access_enabled: snap.lan_access_enabled,
  60:             }
  61:         }
  62:         Err(ResilienceError::Io) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Missing {
  63:             reason: format!("runtime state path is unreadable on this host: {state_path_str}"),
  64:         },
  65:         Err(ResilienceError::IntegrityMismatch) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::IntegrityMismatch {
  66:             reason: format!("runtime state file failed integrity verification: {state_path_str}"),
  67:         },
  68:         Err(ResilienceError::InvalidFormat) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::InvalidFormat {
  69:             reason: format!(
  70:                 "runtime state file does not match the expected on-disk format: {state_path_str}"
  71:             ),
  72:         },
  73:     };
  74:     let drift_reasons = evaluate_windows_mesh_status(
  75:         &snapshot,
  76:         options.expected_peer_ids.as_slice(),
  77:         options.max_age_seconds,
  78:     );
  79:     let overall_ok = drift_reasons.is_empty();
  80:     MacosMeshStatusReport {
  81:         schema_version: 1,
  82:         state_path: state_path_str,
  83:         overall_ok,
  84:         snapshot,
  85:         expected_peer_ids: options.expected_peer_ids.clone(),
  86:         max_age_seconds: options.max_age_seconds,
  87:         drift_reasons,
  88:     }
  89: }
  90: 
  91: fn current_unix_seconds() -> i64 {
  92:     SystemTime::now()
  93:         .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
  94:         .map(|d| d.as_secs() as i64)
  95:         .unwrap_or(0)
  96: }
  97: 
  98: #[cfg(test)]
  99: mod tests {
 100:     use super::*;
 101: 
 102:     #[test]
 103:     fn missing_state_file_reports_drift() {
 104:         let options = MacosMeshStatusOptions {
 105:             state_path: Some(PathBuf::from("/nonexistent/macos/rustynetd.state")),
 106:             expected_peer_ids: vec![],
 107:             max_age_seconds: None,
 108:         };
 109:         let report = collect_macos_mesh_status_report(&options);
 110:         assert!(!report.overall_ok);
 111:         assert!(
 112:             matches!(report.snapshot, WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Missing { .. }),
 113:             "missing state file must yield Missing snapshot"
 114:         );
 115:     }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/macos_runtime_acls.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! macOS runtime ACL verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! macOS parity for `linux_runtime_acls`. Walks the canonical macOS
   6: //! runtime roots used by the daemon's launchd unit, and confirms each
   7: //! root exists, is a real directory, has the reviewed owner / group,
   8: //! and matches the reviewed mode.
   9: //!
  10: //! Reviewed posture from `scripts/launchd/com.rustynet.daemon.plist`
  11: //! + `scripts/bootstrap/macos/Install-RustyNetMacosService.sh`:
  12: //!   install -d -m 0700 -o rustynetd -g rustynetd /usr/local/var/rustynet
  13: //!   install -d -m 0750 -o root      -g rustynetd /usr/local/etc/rustynet
  14: //!
  15: //! Off-macOS the report's per-root status is `Missing` with an explicit
  16: //! "requires a macOS runtime host" reason.
  17: //!
  18: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd macos-runtime-acls-check`. The
  19: //! orchestrator's `MacosDaemonProbe` adapter dispatches the
  20: //! `RuntimeAcls` op to this subcommand.
  21: 
  22: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  23: 
  24: const MACOS_RUNTIME_ACL_ROOTS: &[(&str, &str, u32, &str, &str)] = &[
  25:     (
  26:         "/usr/local/var/rustynet",
  27:         "state root",
  28:         0o700,
  29:         "rustynetd",
  30:         "rustynetd",
  31:     ),
  32:     (
  33:         "/usr/local/etc/rustynet",
  34:         "config root",
  35:         0o750,
  36:         "root",
  37:         "rustynetd",
  38:     ),
  39: ];
  40: 
  41: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  42: #[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
  43: pub enum MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus {
  44:     Ok,
  45:     Missing { reason: String },
  46:     Drifted { reason: String },
  47: }
  48: 
  49: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  50: pub struct MacosRuntimeAclRootEntry {
  51:     pub label: String,
  52:     pub path: String,
  53:     #[serde(flatten)]
  54:     pub status: MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus,
  55: }
  56: 
  57: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  58: pub struct MacosRuntimeAclReport {
  59:     pub schema_version: u32,
  60:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  61:     pub roots: Vec<MacosRuntimeAclRootEntry>,
  62: }
  63: 
  64: /// Diagnostic walk over the canonical macOS runtime roots.
  65: pub fn collect_macos_runtime_acl_report() -> MacosRuntimeAclReport {
  66:     let roots = MACOS_RUNTIME_ACL_ROOTS
  67:         .iter()
  68:         .map(|(path_str, label, mode, owner, group)| {
  69:             let status = inspect_runtime_root_status(path_str, label, *mode, owner, group);
  70:             MacosRuntimeAclRootEntry {
  71:                 label: (*label).to_string(),
  72:                 path: (*path_str).to_string(),
  73:                 status,
  74:             }
  75:         })
  76:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  77:     let overall_ok = roots
  78:         .iter()
  79:         .all(|entry| matches!(entry.status, MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok));
  80:     MacosRuntimeAclReport {
  81:         schema_version: 1,
  82:         overall_ok,
  83:         roots,
  84:     }
  85: }
  86: 
  87: /// Reviewed posture expectation for one runtime root.
  88: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  89: pub struct MacosRuntimeAclExpectation {
  90:     pub mode: u32,
  91:     pub owner_uid: u32,
  92:     pub group_gid: u32,
  93: }
  94: 
  95: /// Live metadata snapshot for one runtime root.
  96: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  97: pub struct MacosRuntimeAclSnapshot {
  98:     pub mode: u32,
  99:     pub uid: u32,
 100:     pub gid: u32,
 101:     pub is_dir: bool,
 102:     pub is_symlink: bool,
 103: }
 104: 
 105: /// Pure evaluator: confirms snapshot matches reviewed posture.
 106: pub fn evaluate_macos_runtime_acl_metadata(
 107:     label: &str,
 108:     expected: MacosRuntimeAclExpectation,
 109:     actual: MacosRuntimeAclSnapshot,
 110: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 111:     if actual.is_symlink {
 112:         return Err(format!("{label} must be a real directory, not a symlink"));
 113:     }
 114:     if !actual.is_dir {
 115:         return Err(format!("{label} must be a directory, not a file"));
 116:     }
 117:     let actual_perms = actual.mode & 0o7777;
 118:     if actual_perms != expected.mode {
 119:         return Err(format!(
 120:             "{label} mode is 0o{actual_perms:o}, expected 0o{:o}",
 121:             expected.mode
 122:         ));
 123:     }
 124:     if actual.uid != expected.owner_uid {
 125:         return Err(format!(
 126:             "{label} owner uid is {}, expected {}",
 127:             actual.uid, expected.owner_uid
 128:         ));
 129:     }
 130:     if actual.gid != expected.group_gid {
 131:         return Err(format!(
 132:             "{label} group gid is {}, expected {}",
 133:             actual.gid, expected.group_gid
 134:         ));
 135:     }
 136:     Ok(())
 137: }
 138: 
 139: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 140: fn inspect_runtime_root_status(
 141:     path_str: &str,
 142:     label: &str,
 143:     expected_mode: u32,
 144:     expected_owner: &str,
 145:     expected_group: &str,
 146: ) -> MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus {
 147:     use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
 148:     let path = std::path::Path::new(path_str);
 149:     let metadata = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 150:         Ok(m) => m,
 151:         Err(err) => {
 152:             return MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus::Missing {
 153:                 reason: format!(
 154:                     "{label} must exist before rustynetd starts on macOS ({path_str}): {err}"
 155:                 ),
 156:             };
 157:         }
 158:     };
 159:     let is_symlink = metadata.file_type().is_symlink();
 160:     let is_dir = metadata.is_dir();
 161: 
 162:     let expected_owner_uid = match resolve_uid_for_username(expected_owner) {
 163:         Some(uid) => uid,
 164:         None => {
 165:             return MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted {
 166:                 reason: format!(
 167:                     "{label} reviewed owner {expected_owner:?} is not present on this host"
 168:                 ),
 169:             };
 170:         }
 171:     };
 172:     let expected_group_gid = match resolve_gid_for_groupname(expected_group) {
 173:         Some(gid) => gid,
 174:         None => {
 175:             return MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted {
 176:                 reason: format!(
 177:                     "{label} reviewed group {expected_group:?} is not present on this host"
 178:                 ),
 179:             };
 180:         }
 181:     };
 182: 
 183:     match evaluate_macos_runtime_acl_metadata(
 184:         label,
 185:         MacosRuntimeAclExpectation {
 186:             mode: expected_mode,
 187:             owner_uid: expected_owner_uid,
 188:             group_gid: expected_group_gid,
 189:         },
 190:         MacosRuntimeAclSnapshot {
 191:             mode: metadata.mode(),
 192:             uid: metadata.uid(),
 193:             gid: metadata.gid(),
 194:             is_dir,
 195:             is_symlink,
 196:         },
 197:     ) {
 198:         Ok(()) => MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok,
 199:         Err(reason) => MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted { reason },
 200:     }
 201: }
 202: 
 203: #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
 204: fn inspect_runtime_root_status(
 205:     path_str: &str,
 206:     label: &str,
 207:     _expected_mode: u32,
 208:     _expected_owner: &str,
 209:     _expected_group: &str,
 210: ) -> MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus {
 211:     MacosRuntimeAclRootStatus::Missing {
 212:         reason: format!(
 213:             "{label} probe at {path_str} requires a macOS runtime host; \
 214:              macos-runtime-acls-check is not meaningful off-macOS"
 215:         ),
 216:     }
 217: }
 218: 
 219: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 220: fn resolve_uid_for_username(username: &str) -> Option<u32> {
 221:     nix::unistd::User::from_name(username)
 222:         .ok()
 223:         .flatten()
 224:         .map(|user| user.uid.as_raw())
 225: }
 226: 
 227: #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 228: fn resolve_gid_for_groupname(groupname: &str) -> Option<u32> {
 229:     nix::unistd::Group::from_name(groupname)
 230:         .ok()
 231:         .flatten()
 232:         .map(|group| group.gid.as_raw())
 233: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/macos_service_hardening.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! macOS service-hardening verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! macOS parity for `linux_service_hardening`. Confirms the live
   6: //! launchd service registration for `com.rustynet.daemon` matches the
   7: //! reviewed hardening in `scripts/launchd/com.rustynet.daemon.plist`.
   8: //!
   9: //! The collector reads the on-disk plist at
  10: //! `/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.rustynet.daemon.plist` and checks that
  11: //! the reviewed keys are present with the reviewed values. Unlike
  12: //! `systemctl show`, `launchctl print` output is not key=value, so we
  13: //! parse the plist file directly.
  14: //!
  15: //! Reviewed hardening keys (from the reviewed plist):
  16: //!   UserName        = rustynetd
  17: //!   GroupName       = rustynetd
  18: //!   RunAtLoad       = true
  19: //!   KeepAlive       = true
  20: //!   ProcessType     = Background
  21: //!   AbandonProcessGroup = false
  22: //!
  23: //! Wired through the CLI as `rustynetd macos-service-hardening-check`.
  24: //! The orchestrator's `MacosDaemonProbe` dispatches `ServiceHardening` here.
  25: 
  26: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  27: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
  28: 
  29: pub const REVIEWED_LAUNCHDAEMON_PLIST: &str = "/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.rustynet.daemon.plist";
  30: pub const REVIEWED_SERVICE_LABEL: &str = "com.rustynet.daemon";
  31: 
  32: /// Reviewed plist key=value pairs.
  33: const REVIEWED_PLIST_DIRECTIVES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
  34:     ("UserName", "rustynetd"),
  35:     ("GroupName", "rustynetd"),
  36:     ("RunAtLoad", "true"),
  37:     ("KeepAlive", "true"),
  38:     ("ProcessType", "Background"),
  39:     ("AbandonProcessGroup", "false"),
  40: ];
  41: 
  42: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  43: pub struct MacosServiceHardeningReport {
  44:     pub schema_version: u32,
  45:     pub service_label: String,
  46:     pub plist_path: String,
  47:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  48:     pub probed: bool,
  49:     pub probe_reason: Option<String>,
  50:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  51:     pub observed: BTreeMap<String, String>,
  52: }
  53: 
  54: /// Pure evaluator: walks the reviewed-property table against a parsed
  55: /// property map. Returns every drift reason in one pass.
  56: pub fn evaluate_macos_service_hardening(observed: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Vec<String> {
  57:     let mut reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  58:     if observed.is_empty() {
  59:         reasons.push("plist contained no parseable key=value properties".to_string());
  60:         return reasons;
  61:     }
  62:     for (key, expected) in REVIEWED_PLIST_DIRECTIVES {
  63:         match observed.get(*key) {
  64:             Some(actual) if actual == expected => {}
  65:             Some(actual) => {
  66:                 reasons.push(format!(
  67:                     "{key} drifted: expected {expected:?}, observed {actual:?}"
  68:                 ));
  69:             }
  70:             None => {
  71:                 reasons.push(format!("{key} missing from plist (expected {expected:?})"));
  72:             }
  73:         }
  74:     }
  75:     reasons
  76: }
  77: 
  78: /// Parse a minimal subset of plist XML: extract scalar string and bool
  79: /// values for the reviewed keys. Only handles the simple flat key/value
  80: /// structure used by the reviewed plist (not nested dicts or arrays).
  81: pub fn parse_plist_scalars(xml: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
  82:     let mut map: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
  83:     let mut last_key: Option<String> = None;
  84:     for line in xml.lines() {
  85:         let line = line.trim();
  86:         if let Some(inner) = line
  87:             .strip_prefix("<key>")
  88:             .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix("</key>"))
  89:         {
  90:             last_key = Some(inner.to_string());
  91:         } else if let Some(key) = last_key.take() {
  92:             if let Some(inner) = line
  93:                 .strip_prefix("<string>")
  94:                 .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix("</string>"))
  95:             {
  96:                 map.insert(key, inner.to_string());
  97:             } else if line == "<true/>" {
  98:                 map.insert(key, "true".to_string());
  99:             } else if line == "<false/>" {
 100:                 map.insert(key, "false".to_string());
 101:             } else {
 102:                 // dict, array, or other complex type — skip value, leave key consumed
 103:             }
 104:         }
 105:     }
 106:     map
 107: }
 108: 
 109: pub fn build_macos_service_hardening_report(
 110:     probed: bool,
 111:     probe_reason: Option<String>,
 112:     observed: BTreeMap<String, String>,
 113: ) -> MacosServiceHardeningReport {
 114:     let drift_reasons =
 115:         if probed {
 116:             evaluate_macos_service_hardening(&observed)
 117:         } else {
 118:             vec![probe_reason.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {
 119:                 "plist was not read; service hardening posture unknown".to_string()
 120:             })]
 121:         };
 122:     let overall_ok = probed && drift_reasons.is_empty();
 123:     MacosServiceHardeningReport {
 124:         schema_version: 1,
 125:         service_label: REVIEWED_SERVICE_LABEL.to_string(),
 126:         plist_path: REVIEWED_LAUNCHDAEMON_PLIST.to_string(),
 127:         overall_ok,
 128:         probed,
 129:         probe_reason,
 130:         drift_reasons,
 131:         observed,
 132:     }
 133: }
 134: 
 135: pub fn collect_macos_service_hardening_report() -> MacosServiceHardeningReport {
 136:     match std::fs::read_to_string(REVIEWED_LAUNCHDAEMON_PLIST) {
 137:         Ok(xml) => {
 138:             let observed = parse_plist_scalars(&xml);
 139:             build_macos_service_hardening_report(true, None, observed)
 140:         }
 141:         Err(err) => build_macos_service_hardening_report(
 142:             false,
 143:             Some(format!(
 144:                 "could not read {REVIEWED_LAUNCHDAEMON_PLIST}: {err}"
 145:             )),
 146:             BTreeMap::new(),
 147:         ),
 148:     }
 149: }
 150: 
 151: #[cfg(test)]
 152: mod tests {
 153:     use super::*;
 154: 
 155:     fn reviewed_property_map() -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
 156:         REVIEWED_PLIST_DIRECTIVES
 157:             .iter()
 158:             .map(|(k, v)| ((*k).to_string(), (*v).to_string()))
 159:             .collect()
 160:     }
 161: 
 162:     const SAMPLE_PLIST: &str = r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
 163: <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
 164: <plist version="1.0">
 165: <dict>
 166:     <key>Label</key>
 167:     <string>com.rustynet.daemon</string>
 168:     <key>UserName</key>
 169:     <string>rustynetd</string>
 170:     <key>GroupName</key>
 171:     <string>rustynetd</string>
 172:     <key>RunAtLoad</key>
 173:     <true/>
 174:     <key>KeepAlive</key>
 175:     <true/>
 176:     <key>ProcessType</key>
 177:     <string>Background</string>
 178:     <key>AbandonProcessGroup</key>
 179:     <false/>
 180: </dict>
 181: </plist>"#;
 182: 
 183:     #[test]
 184:     fn parser_extracts_reviewed_keys() {
 185:         let map = parse_plist_scalars(SAMPLE_PLIST);
 186:         assert_eq!(map.get("UserName").map(String::as_str), Some("rustynetd"));
 187:         assert_eq!(map.get("GroupName").map(String::as_str), Some("rustynetd"));
 188:         assert_eq!(map.get("RunAtLoad").map(String::as_str), Some("true"));
 189:         assert_eq!(map.get("KeepAlive").map(String::as_str), Some("true"));
 190:         assert_eq!(
 191:             map.get("ProcessType").map(String::as_str),

   6: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
   7: pub struct MetricRow {
   8:     pub name: &'static str,
   9:     pub value: f64,
  10:     pub unit: &'static str,
  11:     pub threshold: &'static str,
  12:     pub status: &'static str,
  13:     pub reason: &'static str,
  14: }
  15: 
  16: fn metric_from_env(
  17:     name: &'static str,
  18:     env_key: &'static str,
  19:     unit: &'static str,
  20:     threshold: &'static str,
  21:     threshold_max: f64,
  22: ) -> MetricRow {
  23:     match std::env::var(env_key) {
  24:         Ok(raw) => match raw.parse::<f64>() {
  25:             Ok(value) if value.is_finite() && value >= 0.0 => MetricRow {
  26:                 name,
  27:                 value,
  28:                 unit,
  29:                 threshold,
  30:                 status: if value <= threshold_max {
  31:                     "pass"
  32:                 } else {
  33:                     "fail"
  34:                 },
  35:                 reason: "measured",
  36:             },
  37:             _ => MetricRow {
  38:                 name,
  39:                 value: 0.0,
  40:                 unit,
  41:                 threshold,
  42:                 status: "fail",
  43:                 reason: "measurement_invalid",
  44:             },
  45:         },
  46:         Err(_) => MetricRow {
  47:             name,
  48:             value: 0.0,
  49:             unit,
  50:             threshold,
  51:             status: "fail",
  52:             reason: "measurement_unavailable",
  53:         },
  54:     }
  55: }
  56: 
  57: pub fn phase1_baseline_metrics() -> [MetricRow; 5] {
  58:     [

  60:             "idle_cpu_percent",

  62:             "percent_of_one_core",
  63:             "<=2",
  64:             2.0,
  65:         ),
  66:         metric_from_env(
  67:             "idle_memory_mb",
  68:             "RUSTYNET_PHASE1_IDLE_MEMORY_MB",
  69:             "mb_rss",
  70:             "<=120",
  71:             120.0,
  72:         ),
  73:         metric_from_env(
  74:             "reconnect_seconds",
  75:             "RUSTYNET_PHASE1_RECONNECT_SECONDS",
  76:             "seconds",
  77:             "<=5",
  78:             5.0,
  79:         ),
  80:         metric_from_env(
  81:             "route_policy_apply_p95_seconds",
  82:             "RUSTYNET_PHASE1_ROUTE_POLICY_APPLY_P95_SECONDS",
  83:             "seconds",
  84:             "<=2",
  85:             2.0,

  89:             "RUSTYNET_PHASE1_THROUGHPUT_OVERHEAD_PERCENT",

  97: fn metrics_to_json(metrics: &[MetricRow]) -> String {
  98:     let mut out = String::from(
  99: /* ELIDED: original line had 10 backslash-quote sequences — removed to avoid DeepSeek parser failure */
 100:     );
 101: 
 102:     for (index, metric) in metrics.iter().enumerate() {
 103:         let comma = if index + 1 == metrics.len() { "" } else { "," };
 104:         out.push_str(&format!(
 105: /* ELIDED: original line had 22 backslash-quote sequences — removed to avoid DeepSeek parser failure */
 106:             metric.name, metric.value, metric.unit, metric.threshold, metric.status, metric.reason, comma
 107:         ));
 108:     }
 109: 
 110:     out.push_str("  ]\n}\n");
 111:     out
 112: }

 114: pub fn write_phase1_baseline_report(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<(), String> {
 115:     let path = path.as_ref();
 116:     if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
 117:         fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|err| format!("create_dir_all failed: {err}"))?;
 118:     }
 119: 
 120:     let metrics = phase1_baseline_metrics();
 121:     let json = metrics_to_json(&metrics);
 122:     fs::write(path, json).map_err(|err| format!("write baseline report failed: {err}"))?;
 123:     Ok(())
 124: }

  31: struct Phase10PeerRuntime<'a, B: TunnelBackend, S: DataplaneSystem> {
  32:     controller: &'a mut Phase10Controller<B, S>,

  36: impl<'a, B: TunnelBackend, S: DataplaneSystem> SimultaneousOpenRuntime
  37:     for Phase10PeerRuntime<'a, B, S>
  38: {
  39:     fn send_probe(&mut self, endpoint: SocketEndpoint, round: u8) -> Result<(), TraversalError> {
  40:         // When probing, we treat it as a Direct path attempt.
  41:         // If the candidate was a relay, it wouldn't be in the direct_candidates list
  42:         // passed to execute_simultaneous_open.
  43:         self.controller
  44:             .reconfigure_managed_peer(&self.node_id, endpoint, PathMode::Direct)
  45:             .map_err(|_| TraversalError::InvalidConfig("phase10 direct probe send failed"))?;
  46:         self.controller
  47:             .backend
  48:             .initiate_peer_handshake(&self.node_id, round > 0)
  49:             .map_err(|_| TraversalError::InvalidConfig("phase10 direct probe send failed"))
  50:     }
  51: 
  52:     fn latest_handshake_unix(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u64>, TraversalError> {
  53:         self.controller
  54:             .backend
  55:             .peer_latest_handshake_unix(&self.node_id)
  56:             .map_err(|_| TraversalError::InvalidConfig("phase10 handshake read failed"))
  57:     }
  58: }

  92: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
  93: pub struct ManagementCidr {
  94:     address: IpAddr,
  95:     prefix: u8,
  96: }
  97: 
  98: impl ManagementCidr {
  99:     fn nft_family(self) -> &'static str {
 100:         match self.address {
 101:             IpAddr::V4(_) => "ip",
 102:             IpAddr::V6(_) => "ip6",
 103:         }
 104:     }
 105: 
 106:     fn pf_family(self) -> &'static str {
 107:         match self.address {
 108:             IpAddr::V4(_) => "inet",
 109:             IpAddr::V6(_) => "inet6",
 110:         }
 111:     }
 112: 
 113:     fn is_ipv6(self) -> bool {
 114:         matches!(self.address, IpAddr::V6(_))
 115:     }
 116: }
 117: 
 118: impl std::fmt::Display for ManagementCidr {
 119:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 120:         write!(f, "{}/{}", self.address, self.prefix)
 121:     }
 122: }
 123: 
 124: impl std::str::FromStr for ManagementCidr {
 125:     type Err = String;
 126: 
 127:     fn from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
 128:         let (base, prefix_raw) = value
 129:             .split_once('/')
 130:             .ok_or_else(|| format!("invalid management cidr: {value}"))?;
 131:         let prefix = prefix_raw
 132:             .parse::<u8>()
 133:             .map_err(|_| format!("invalid management cidr prefix: {value}"))?;
 134:         let address = base
 135:             .parse::<IpAddr>()
 136:             .map_err(|_| format!("invalid management cidr address: {value}"))?;
 137:         let max_prefix = match address {
 138:             IpAddr::V4(_) => 32,
 139:             IpAddr::V6(_) => 128,
 140:         };
 141:         if prefix > max_prefix {
 142:             return Err(format!("invalid management cidr prefix: {value}"));
 143:         }
 144:         Ok(Self { address, prefix })
 145:     }
 146: }

 356: impl fmt::Display for Phase10Error {
 357:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
 358:         match self {
 359:             Phase10Error::InvalidTransition(msg) => write!(f, "invalid transition: {msg}"),

 361:             Phase10Error::Backend(err) => write!(f, "backend error: {err}"),
 362:             Phase10Error::System(err) => write!(f, "system error: {err}"),
 363:             Phase10Error::TraversalProbeFailed(err) => {
 364:                 write!(f, "traversal probe failed: {err}")
 365:             }
 366:             Phase10Error::PolicyDenied => f.write_str("policy denied"),
 367:             Phase10Error::ExitNotSelected => f.write_str("exit node not selected"),
 368:             Phase10Error::LanAccessDenied => f.write_str("lan access denied"),
 369:             Phase10Error::PeerNotManaged => f.write_str("peer is not managed by phase10"),
 370:             Phase10Error::RelayPathUnavailable => {
 371:                 f.write_str("relay path unavailable for managed peer")
 372:             }
 373:             Phase10Error::NotStarted => f.write_str("phase10 controller not started"),
 374:             Phase10Error::MembershipRevoked(id) => {
 375:                 write!(f, "peer {id} membership is revoked: provisioning denied")
 376:             }
 377:             Phase10Error::MembershipNotFound(id) => {
 378:                 write!(f, "peer {id} not found in membership: provisioning denied")
 379:             }
 380:         }
 381:     }
 382: }
 383: 
 384: impl std::error::Error for Phase10Error {}
 385: 
 386: impl From<BackendError> for Phase10Error {
 387:     fn from(value: BackendError) -> Self {
 388:         Phase10Error::Backend(value)
 389:     }
 390: }
 391: 
 392: impl From<SystemError> for Phase10Error {
 393:     fn from(value: SystemError) -> Self {
 394:         Phase10Error::System(value)
 395:     }
 396: }

 452: impl DryRunSystem {
 453:     pub fn fail_on(mut self, operation: &str) -> Self {
 454:         self.fail_operation = Some(operation.to_string());
 455:         self
 456:     }
 457: 
 458:     fn step(&mut self, operation: &str) -> Result<(), SystemError> {
 459:         self.operations.push(operation.to_string());
 460:         if self
 461:             .fail_operation
 462:             .as_ref()
 463:             .map(|candidate| candidate == operation)
 464:             .unwrap_or(false)
 465:         {
 466:             return Err(SystemError::RollbackFailed(operation.to_string()));
 467:         }
 468:         Ok(())
 469:     }
 470: }
