  44:     pub deny_remote_clients: bool,
  45: }
  46: 
  47: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
  48: pub struct WindowsNamedPipeClientFacts {
  49:     pub is_local_system: bool,
  50:     pub is_builtin_administrator: bool,
  51:     pub matches_service_identity: bool,
  52:     pub is_remote_client: bool,
  53: }
  54: 
  55: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
  56: #[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
  57: pub enum WindowsPrivilegedRequest {
  58:     Probe { protocol_version: u16 },
  59:     InspectRuntimePathAcl { path: String },
  60: }
  61: 
  62: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
  63: #[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
  64: pub enum WindowsPrivilegedResponse {
  65:     ProbeAck { protocol_version: u16 },
  66:     RuntimePathAcl { path: String, sddl: String },
  67: }
  68: 
  69: pub fn default_security_policy(role: WindowsLocalIpcRole) -> WindowsNamedPipeSecurityPolicy {
  70:     match role {
  71:         WindowsLocalIpcRole::DaemonControl => WindowsNamedPipeSecurityPolicy {
  72:             allow_local_system: true,
  73:             allow_builtin_administrators: true,
  74:             allow_service_identity: true,
  75:             deny_remote_clients: true,
  76:         },
  77:         WindowsLocalIpcRole::PrivilegedHelper => WindowsNamedPipeSecurityPolicy {
  78:             allow_local_system: true,
  79:             allow_builtin_administrators: true,
  80:             allow_service_identity: true,
  81:             deny_remote_clients: true,
  82:         },
  83:     }
  84: }
  85: 
  86: pub fn is_client_authorized(
  87:     policy: &WindowsNamedPipeSecurityPolicy,
  88:     facts: WindowsNamedPipeClientFacts,
  89: ) -> bool {
  90:     if policy.deny_remote_clients && facts.is_remote_client {
  91:         return false;
  92:     }
  93:     if policy.allow_service_identity && facts.matches_service_identity {
  94:         return true;
  95:     }
  96:     if policy.allow_local_system && facts.is_local_system {
  97:         return true;
  98:     }
  99:     if policy.allow_builtin_administrators && facts.is_builtin_administrator {
 100:         return true;
 101:     }
 102:     false
 103: }
 104: 
 105: pub fn validate_windows_pipe_path(path: &Path, role: WindowsLocalIpcRole) -> Result<(), String> {
 106:     let text = path.to_string_lossy();
 107:     if text.is_empty() {
 108:         return Err(format!("{} path must not be empty", role.label()));
 109:     }
 110:     if is_linux_runtime_root_text(text.as_ref()) {
 111:         return Err(format!(
 112:             "{} must not use Linux runtime roots on Windows: {}",
 113:             role.label(),
 114:             path.display()
 115:         ));
 116:     }
 117:     if text.starts_with(r"\\") && !text.starts_with(r"\\.\pipe\") {
 118:         return Err(format!(
 119:             "{} must not use a remote UNC path: {}",
 120:             role.label(),
 121:             path.display()
 122:         ));
 123:     }
 124:     if !text.starts_with(r"\\.\pipe\") {
 125:         return Err(format!(
 126:             "{} must use a local Windows named pipe path under \\\\.\\pipe\\: {}",
 127:             role.label(),
 128:             path.display()
 129:         ));
 130:     }
 131:     let suffix = &text[r"\\.\pipe\".len()..];
 132:     if !suffix.starts_with("RustyNet\\") {
 133:         return Err(format!(
 134:             "{} must stay under the RustyNet named-pipe namespace: {}",
 135:             role.label(),
 136:             path.display()
 137:         ));
 138:     }
 139:     if suffix.ends_with('\\') {
 140:         return Err(format!(
 141:             "{} must include a concrete pipe leaf name: {}",
 142:             role.label(),
 143:             path.display()
 144:         ));
 145:     }
 146:     if !suffix
 147:         .chars()
 148:         .all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(ch, '\\' | '-' | '_' | '.'))
 149:     {
 150:         return Err(format!(
 151:             "{} contains invalid characters; allowed characters are [A-Za-z0-9._-\\\\]: {}",
 152:             role.label(),
 153:             path.display()
 154:         ));
 155:     }
 156:     let expected_leaf = role.pipe_leaf().to_ascii_lowercase();
 157:     let expected_self_check_prefix = role.reviewed_self_check_leaf_prefix().to_ascii_lowercase();
 158:     let lowered_suffix = suffix.to_ascii_lowercase();
 159:     let is_reviewed_leaf = lowered_suffix == format!("rustynet\\{expected_leaf}")
 160:         || lowered_suffix == format!("rustynet\\{expected_self_check_prefix}");
 161:     let is_reviewed_self_check =
 162:         lowered_suffix.starts_with(&format!("rustynet\\{expected_self_check_prefix}"));
 163:     if !is_reviewed_leaf && !is_reviewed_self_check {
 164:         return Err(format!(
 165:             "{} must pin the reviewed pipe leaf '{}' or a reviewed self-check leaf: {}",
 166:             role.label(),
 167:             role.pipe_leaf(),
 168:             path.display()
 169:         ));
 170:     }
 171:     Ok(())
 172: }
 173: 
 174: pub fn build_named_pipe_security_sddl(
 175:     role: WindowsLocalIpcRole,
 176:     service_sid: Option<&str>,
 177: ) -> String {
 178:     let policy = default_security_policy(role);
 179:     let mut aces = Vec::new();
 180:     if policy.allow_local_system {
 181:         aces.push("(A;;GA;;;SY)".to_string());
 182:     }
 183:     if policy.allow_builtin_administrators {
 184:         aces.push("(A;;GA;;;BA)".to_string());
 185:     }
 186:     if policy.allow_service_identity
 187:         && let Some(sid) = service_sid
 188:     {
 189:         aces.push(format!("(A;;GA;;;{sid})"));
 190:     }
 191:     format!("O:SYG:SYD:P{}", aces.join(""))
 192: }
 193: 
 194: pub fn validate_windows_privileged_request(
 195:     request: &WindowsPrivilegedRequest,
 196: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 197:     match request {
 198:         WindowsPrivilegedRequest::Probe { protocol_version } => {
 199:             if *protocol_version != WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_IPC_PROTOCOL_VERSION {
 200:                 return Err(format!(
 201:                     "unsupported Windows privileged IPC protocol version {protocol_version}; expected {WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_IPC_PROTOCOL_VERSION}",
 202:                 ));
 203:             }
 204:         }
 205:         WindowsPrivilegedRequest::InspectRuntimePathAcl { path } => {
 206:             if path.trim().is_empty() {
 207:                 return Err("inspect-runtime-path-acl path must not be empty".to_string());
 208:             }
 209:             validate_windows_runtime_file_path(Path::new(path), "inspect-runtime-path-acl path")?;
 210:         }
 211:     }
 212:     Ok(())
 213: }
 214: 
 215: pub fn encode_windows_privileged_request(
 216:     request: &WindowsPrivilegedRequest,
 217: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
 218:     validate_windows_privileged_request(request)?;
 219:     let bytes =
 220:         serde_json::to_vec(request).map_err(|err| format!("request encode failed: {err}"))?;
 221:     if bytes.is_empty() || bytes.len() > MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES {
 222:         return Err(format!(
 223:             "request payload must be between 1 and {MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES} bytes"
 224:         ));
 225:     }
 226:     Ok(bytes)
 227: }
 228: 
 229: pub fn decode_windows_privileged_request(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<WindowsPrivilegedRequest, String> {
 230:     if bytes.is_empty() || bytes.len() > MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES {
 231:         return Err(format!(
 232:             "request payload must be between 1 and {MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES} bytes"
 233:         ));
 234:     }
 235:     let request: WindowsPrivilegedRequest =
 236:         serde_json::from_slice(bytes).map_err(|err| format!("request decode failed: {err}"))?;
 237:     validate_windows_privileged_request(&request)?;
 238:     Ok(request)
 239: }
 240: 
 241: pub fn encode_windows_privileged_response(
 242:     response: &WindowsPrivilegedResponse,
 243: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
 244:     let bytes =
 245:         serde_json::to_vec(response).map_err(|err| format!("response encode failed: {err}"))?;
 246:     if bytes.is_empty() || bytes.len() > MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES {
 247:         return Err(format!(
 248:             "response payload must be between 1 and {MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES} bytes"
 249:         ));
 250:     }
 251:     Ok(bytes)
 252: }
 253: 
 254: pub fn decode_windows_privileged_response(
 255:     bytes: &[u8],
 256: ) -> Result<WindowsPrivilegedResponse, String> {
 257:     if bytes.is_empty() || bytes.len() > MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES {
 258:         return Err(format!(
 259:             "response payload must be between 1 and {MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES} bytes"
 260:         ));
 261:     }
 262:     serde_json::from_slice(bytes).map_err(|err| format!("response decode failed: {err}"))
 263: }
 264: 
 265: pub fn serve_windows_privileged_request_once<F>(
 266:     pipe_path: &Path,
 267:     role: WindowsLocalIpcRole,
 268:     service_sid: Option<&str>,
 269:     handler: F,
 270: ) -> Result<(), String>
 271: where
 272:     F: FnOnce(WindowsPrivilegedRequest) -> Result<WindowsPrivilegedResponse, String>,
 273: {
 274:     validate_windows_pipe_path(pipe_path, role)?;
 275:     let sddl = build_named_pipe_security_sddl(role, service_sid);
 276:     serve_named_pipe_one_message(
 277:         pipe_path.to_string_lossy().as_ref(),
 278:         sddl.as_str(),
 279:         MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES,
 280:         |bytes| {
 281:             let request = decode_windows_privileged_request(&bytes)?;
 282:             let response = handler(request)?;
 283:             encode_windows_privileged_response(&response)
 284:         },
 285:     )
 286: }
 287: 
 288: pub fn call_windows_privileged_request(
 289:     pipe_path: &Path,
 290:     role: WindowsLocalIpcRole,
 291:     request: &WindowsPrivilegedRequest,
 292:     timeout: Duration,
 293: ) -> Result<WindowsPrivilegedResponse, String> {
 294:     validate_windows_pipe_path(pipe_path, role)?;
 295:     let request_bytes = encode_windows_privileged_request(request)?;
 296:     let response_bytes = call_named_pipe(
 297:         pipe_path.to_string_lossy().as_ref(),
 298:         request_bytes.as_slice(),
 299:         MAX_WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_MESSAGE_BYTES,
 300:         timeout,
 301:     )?;
 302:     decode_windows_privileged_response(&response_bytes)
 303: }
 304: 
 305: pub fn windows_ipc_probe(
 306:     pipe_path: &Path,
 307:     role: WindowsLocalIpcRole,
 308:     timeout: Duration,
 309: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 310:     let response = call_windows_privileged_request(
 311:         pipe_path,
 312:         role,
 313:         &WindowsPrivilegedRequest::Probe {
 314:             protocol_version: WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_IPC_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
 315:         },
 316:         timeout,
 317:     )?;
 318:     match response {
 319:         WindowsPrivilegedResponse::ProbeAck { protocol_version }
 320:             if protocol_version == WINDOWS_PRIVILEGED_IPC_PROTOCOL_VERSION =>
 321:         {
 322:             Ok(())
 323:         }
 324:         other => Err(format!(
 325:             "unexpected Windows privileged probe response over {}: {other:?}",
 326:             pipe_path.display()
 327:         )),
 328:     }
 329: }
 330: 
 331: /// Maximum bytes for a single daemon control pipe message.
 332: /// Matches `MAX_COMMAND_BYTES` in `ipc.rs` so that the full command wire format always fits.
 333: pub const MAX_WINDOWS_DAEMON_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES: usize = 4096;
 334: 
 335: /// Serve exactly one daemon control pipe connection.
 336: ///
 337: /// The handler receives the raw request bytes (newline-terminated command wire format, e.g.
 338: /// `b"status\n"`) and must return raw response bytes (newline-terminated response wire format,
 339: /// e.g. `b"ok|...\n"`).
 340: ///
 341: /// Path validation and SDDL construction are applied on every call so the server loop thread
 342: /// can call this in a tight loop without holding external state between iterations.
 343: pub fn serve_windows_daemon_control_request_once<F>(
 344:     pipe_path: &Path,
 345:     service_sid: Option<&str>,
 346:     handler: F,
 347: ) -> Result<(), String>
 348: where
 349:     F: FnOnce(Vec<u8>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String>,
 350: {
 351:     validate_windows_pipe_path(pipe_path, WindowsLocalIpcRole::DaemonControl)?;
 352:     let sddl = build_named_pipe_security_sddl(WindowsLocalIpcRole::DaemonControl, service_sid);
 353:     serve_named_pipe_one_message(
 354:         pipe_path.to_string_lossy().as_ref(),
 355:         sddl.as_str(),
 356:         MAX_WINDOWS_DAEMON_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES,
 357:         handler,
 358:     )
 359: }
 360: 
 361: /// Send a daemon control command over the named pipe and return the raw response wire string.
 362: ///
 363: /// `request_wire` is the IPC command in wire format (e.g. `"status"` or `"state refresh"`).
 364: /// A trailing newline is appended automatically if absent.
 365: /// The returned string is the response wire format (e.g. `"ok|..."` or `"err|..."`).
 366: ///
 367: /// This is the low-level client call used by the CLI on Windows.
 368: pub fn call_windows_daemon_control_raw(
 369:     pipe_path: &Path,
 370:     request_wire: &str,
 371:     timeout: Duration,
 372: ) -> Result<String, String> {
 373:     validate_windows_pipe_path(pipe_path, WindowsLocalIpcRole::DaemonControl)?;
 374:     let mut request_bytes = request_wire.as_bytes().to_vec();
 375:     if !request_bytes.ends_with(b"\n") {
 376:         request_bytes.push(b'\n');
 377:     }
 378:     if request_bytes.len() > MAX_WINDOWS_DAEMON_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES {
 379:         return Err(format!(
 380:             "daemon control request exceeds maximum size ({} > {MAX_WINDOWS_DAEMON_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES} bytes)",
 381:             request_bytes.len()
 382:         ));
 383:     }
 384:     let response_bytes = call_named_pipe(
 385:         pipe_path.to_string_lossy().as_ref(),
 386:         &request_bytes,
 387:         MAX_WINDOWS_DAEMON_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES,
 388:         timeout,
 389:     )?;
 390:     String::from_utf8(response_bytes)
 391:         .map_err(|err| format!("daemon control response is not valid UTF-8: {err}"))
 392: }
 393: 
 394: pub fn windows_ipc_blocker_reason(role: WindowsLocalIpcRole) -> String {
 395:     match role {
 396:         WindowsLocalIpcRole::DaemonControl => {
 397:             // Daemon control is now implemented via serve_windows_daemon_control_request_once /
 398:             // call_windows_daemon_control_raw. This path is retained only as a fallback message
 399:             // for callers that still reference the blocker API directly.
 400:             "daemon control pipe is implemented on Windows; use serve_windows_daemon_control_request_once and call_windows_daemon_control_raw instead of this legacy blocker path".to_string()
 401:         }
 402:         WindowsLocalIpcRole::PrivilegedHelper => "privileged helper shell-command execution remains blocked on Windows; use the reviewed named-pipe probe and ACL inspection request shapes only until a real Windows backend defines native privileged operations".to_string(),
 403:     }
 404: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/windows_key_custody.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Windows key-custody verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! Validates that the on-disk key material on a Windows runtime host matches
   6: //! the reviewed custody contract:
   7: //!
   8: //! * the WireGuard runtime passphrase is stored as a DPAPI-protected blob at
   9: //!   the reviewed `.dpapi` path and is ACL-locked;
  10: //! * the encrypted WireGuard private key file exists at the reviewed path
  11: //!   and is ACL-locked;
  12: //! * the plaintext WireGuard private key file is absent at rest (Phase E
  13: //!   migrated runtime key custody to encrypted-at-rest);
  14: //! * the WireGuard public key file exists at the reviewed path and is
  15: //!   ACL-locked.
  16: //!
  17: //! The pure `evaluate_windows_key_custody` aggregator returns every drift
  18: //! reason in a single pass; the daemon-side collector
  19: //! (`collect_windows_key_custody_snapshot`) walks the canonical paths and
  20: //! captures each entry's status. Together they back the
  21: //! `windows-key-custody-check` subcommand the orchestrator dispatches over
  22: //! the existing argv-only PowerShell-encoded SSH channel.
  23: 
  24: use crate::windows_paths::{
  25:     DEFAULT_WINDOWS_WG_ENCRYPTED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH, DEFAULT_WINDOWS_WG_KEY_PASSPHRASE_PATH,
  26:     DEFAULT_WINDOWS_WG_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH, DEFAULT_WINDOWS_WG_RUNTIME_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH,
  27:     evaluate_windows_local_secret_acl_sddl,
  28: };
  29: use rustynet_windows_native::inspect_file_sddl;
  30: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  31: use std::path::Path;
  32: 
  33: /// Per-entry presence + ACL status for a key-custody artifact.
  34: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  35: #[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
  36: pub enum WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus {
  37:     /// Required artifact present, valid, and ACL-locked.
  38:     Ok { acl_sddl: String },
  39:     /// Required artifact missing.
  40:     Missing { reason: String },
  41:     /// Required artifact present but ACL drifted, format wrong, or otherwise
  42:     /// failed validation.
  43:     Invalid { reason: String, acl_sddl: String },
  44:     /// Forbidden artifact present (e.g. plaintext key file at rest).
  45:     Forbidden { reason: String },
  46:     /// Forbidden artifact correctly absent.
  47:     AbsentAsExpected,
  48: }
  49: 
  50: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  51: pub struct WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
  52:     pub label: String,
  53:     pub path: String,
  54:     /// `present` | `absent` requirement. Drives how the status is interpreted.
  55:     pub requirement: String,
  56:     #[serde(flatten)]
  57:     pub status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus,
  58: }
  59: 
  60: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  61: pub struct WindowsKeyCustodyReport {
  62:     pub schema_version: u32,
  63:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  64:     pub entries: Vec<WindowsKeyCustodyEntry>,
  65:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  66: }
  67: 
  68: const REQUIREMENT_PRESENT: &str = "present";
  69: const REQUIREMENT_ABSENT: &str = "absent";
  70: 
  71: /// Pure evaluator over a custody report. Recomputes drift reasons from the
  72: /// per-entry statuses; returns `Ok(())` when every entry's status is
  73: /// consistent with its requirement, otherwise returns the aggregated drift
  74: /// reasons.
  75: pub fn evaluate_windows_key_custody(entries: &[WindowsKeyCustodyEntry]) -> Result<(), Vec<String>> {
  76:     let mut reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  77:     if entries.is_empty() {
  78:         reasons.push("key custody report contains no entries".to_string());
  79:         return Err(reasons);
  80:     }
  81:     for entry in entries {
  82:         match (entry.requirement.as_str(), &entry.status) {
  83:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok { .. }) => {}
  84:             (REQUIREMENT_ABSENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected) => {}
  85:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing { reason }) => {
  86:                 reasons.push(format!("{} missing: {reason}", entry.label));
  87:             }
  88:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid { reason, .. }) => {
  89:                 reasons.push(format!("{} invalid: {reason}", entry.label));
  90:             }
  91:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected) => {
  92:                 reasons.push(format!(
  93:                     "{} required but reported absent (collector bug or missing artifact)",
  94:                     entry.label
  95:                 ));
  96:             }
  97:             (REQUIREMENT_PRESENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Forbidden { reason }) => {
  98:                 reasons.push(format!(
  99:                     "{} marked forbidden but requirement is present: {reason}",
 100:                     entry.label
 101:                 ));
 102:             }
 103:             (REQUIREMENT_ABSENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Forbidden { reason }) => {
 104:                 reasons.push(format!(
 105:                     "{} present but must be absent: {reason}",
 106:                     entry.label
 107:                 ));
 108:             }
 109:             (REQUIREMENT_ABSENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok { .. }) => {
 110:                 reasons.push(format!(
 111:                     "{} reported Ok but requirement is absent; collector treated forbidden artifact as required",
 112:                     entry.label
 113:                 ));
 114:             }
 115:             (REQUIREMENT_ABSENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing { .. })
 116:             | (REQUIREMENT_ABSENT, WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid { .. }) => {
 117:                 reasons.push(format!(
 118:                     "{} requirement is absent but collector returned a present-style status",
 119:                     entry.label
 120:                 ));
 121:             }
 122:             (other, _) => {
 123:                 reasons.push(format!(
 124:                     "{} has unknown requirement {:?}",
 125:                     entry.label, other
 126:                 ));
 127:             }
 128:         }
 129:     }
 130:     if reasons.is_empty() {
 131:         Ok(())
 132:     } else {
 133:         Err(reasons)
 134:     }
 135: }
 136: 
 137: /// Build the live custody report by inspecting the canonical Windows key
 138: /// material paths. Cross-platform: on non-Windows hosts the SDDL inspector
 139: /// returns a clear blocker error so the report records `Missing`/`Invalid`
 140: /// entries rather than fabricating success.
 141: pub fn collect_windows_key_custody_snapshot() -> WindowsKeyCustodyReport {
 142:     let mut entries = vec![
 143:         inspect_required_secret_blob(
 144:             "wg key passphrase blob",
 145:             DEFAULT_WINDOWS_WG_KEY_PASSPHRASE_PATH,
 146:             ".dpapi",
 147:         ),
 148:         inspect_required_secret_blob(
 149:             "wg encrypted private key",
 150:             DEFAULT_WINDOWS_WG_ENCRYPTED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH,
 151:             ".enc",
 152:         ),
 153:         inspect_required_secret_blob("wg public key", DEFAULT_WINDOWS_WG_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH, ".pub"),
 154:         inspect_forbidden_artifact(
 155:             "wg plaintext runtime private key",
 156:             DEFAULT_WINDOWS_WG_RUNTIME_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH,
 157:         ),
 158:     ];
 159:     let drift_reasons = match evaluate_windows_key_custody(&entries) {
 160:         Ok(()) => Vec::new(),
 161:         Err(reasons) => reasons,
 162:     };
 163:     let overall_ok = drift_reasons.is_empty();
 164:     // Sort entries by label for deterministic JSON output across runs.
 165:     entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.label.cmp(&b.label));
 166:     WindowsKeyCustodyReport {
 167:         schema_version: 1,
 168:         overall_ok,
 169:         entries,
 170:         drift_reasons,
 171:     }
 172: }
 173: 
 174: fn inspect_required_secret_blob(
 175:     label: &str,
 176:     path_str: &str,
 177:     expected_extension: &str,
 178: ) -> WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 179:     let path = Path::new(path_str);
 180:     let metadata = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 181:         Ok(meta) => meta,
 182:         Err(err) => {
 183:             return WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 184:                 label: label.to_string(),
 185:                 path: path.display().to_string(),
 186:                 requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 187:                 status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Missing {
 188:                     reason: format!("{label} must exist on Windows runtime host: {err}"),
 189:                 },
 190:             };
 191:         }
 192:     };
 193:     if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() || !metadata.is_file() {
 194:         return WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 195:             label: label.to_string(),
 196:             path: path.display().to_string(),
 197:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 198:             status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 199:                 reason: format!("{label} must be a regular file, not a symlink or directory"),
 200:                 acl_sddl: String::new(),
 201:             },
 202:         };
 203:     }
 204:     if !path
 205:         .to_string_lossy()
 206:         .to_ascii_lowercase()
 207:         .ends_with(expected_extension)
 208:     {
 209:         return WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 210:             label: label.to_string(),
 211:             path: path.display().to_string(),
 212:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 213:             status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 214:                 reason: format!("{label} must use the reviewed extension {expected_extension}"),
 215:                 acl_sddl: String::new(),
 216:             },
 217:         };
 218:     }
 219:     let sddl = match inspect_file_sddl(path) {
 220:         Ok(sddl) => sddl,
 221:         Err(err) => {
 222:             return WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 223:                 label: label.to_string(),
 224:                 path: path.display().to_string(),
 225:                 requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 226:                 status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 227:                     reason: format!("{label} ACL inspection failed: {err}"),
 228:                     acl_sddl: String::new(),
 229:                 },
 230:             };
 231:         }
 232:     };
 233:     if let Err(err) = evaluate_windows_local_secret_acl_sddl(label, sddl.as_str(), false) {
 234:         return WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 235:             label: label.to_string(),
 236:             path: path.display().to_string(),
 237:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 238:             status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Invalid {
 239:                 reason: format!("{label} ACL drift: {err}"),
 240:                 acl_sddl: sddl,
 241:             },
 242:         };
 243:     }
 244:     WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 245:         label: label.to_string(),
 246:         path: path.display().to_string(),
 247:         requirement: REQUIREMENT_PRESENT.to_string(),
 248:         status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Ok { acl_sddl: sddl },
 249:     }
 250: }
 251: 
 252: fn inspect_forbidden_artifact(label: &str, path_str: &str) -> WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 253:     let path = Path::new(path_str);
 254:     match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 255:         Ok(_) => WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 256:             label: label.to_string(),
 257:             path: path.display().to_string(),
 258:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_ABSENT.to_string(),
 259:             status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Forbidden {
 260:                 reason: format!(
 261:                     "{label} must not exist at rest; encrypted-at-rest custody requires the plaintext form to be absent"
 262:                 ),
 263:             },
 264:         },
 265:         Err(err) if err.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 266:             label: label.to_string(),
 267:             path: path.display().to_string(),
 268:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_ABSENT.to_string(),
 269:             status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::AbsentAsExpected,
 270:         },
 271:         Err(err) => WindowsKeyCustodyEntry {
 272:             label: label.to_string(),
 273:             path: path.display().to_string(),
 274:             requirement: REQUIREMENT_ABSENT.to_string(),
 275:             status: WindowsKeyCustodyEntryStatus::Forbidden {
 276:                 reason: format!(
 277:                     "{label} stat returned an unexpected error; cannot prove absence: {err}"
 278:                 ),
 279:             },
 280:         },
 281:     }
 282: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/windows_mesh_status.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Windows mesh-status verifier (W4.2 daemon-side support).
   4: //!
   5: //! Reads the daemon's persisted session snapshot at the canonical Windows
   6: //! state path and emits a typed JSON report the orchestrator can parse to
   7: //! confirm the Windows guest joined the mesh and observes the expected
   8: //! peers. The orchestrator's `validate_windows_mesh_join` stage dispatches
   9: //! the `windows-mesh-status-check` subcommand here.
  10: //!
  11: //! This is a "what does the daemon currently see?" diagnostic. It does not
  12: //! cause any state mutation. A live runtime IPC server for the daemon's
  13: //! observed state is out of scope for this slice; reading the persisted
  14: //! snapshot is sufficient because the daemon writes it on every reconcile.
  15: 
  16: use crate::resilience::{ResilienceError, load_session_snapshot};
  17: use crate::windows_paths::DEFAULT_WINDOWS_STATE_PATH;
  18: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  19: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
  20: use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
  21: 
  22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  23: #[serde(tag = "load_status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
  24: pub enum WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad {
  25:     Ok {
  26:         timestamp_unix: u64,
  27:         age_seconds: i64,
  28:         peer_ids: Vec<String>,
  29:         selected_exit_node: Option<String>,
  30:         lan_access_enabled: bool,
  31:     },
  32:     Missing {
  33:         reason: String,
  34:     },
  35:     IntegrityMismatch {
  36:         reason: String,
  37:     },
  38:     InvalidFormat {
  39:         reason: String,
  40:     },
  41: }
  42: 
  43: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  44: pub struct WindowsMeshStatusReport {
  45:     pub schema_version: u32,
  46:     pub state_path: String,
  47:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  48:     pub snapshot: WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad,
  49:     pub expected_peer_ids: Vec<String>,
  50:     pub max_age_seconds: Option<i64>,
  51:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  52: }
  53: 
  54: /// Knobs the orchestrator can pass through the subcommand. All optional.
  55: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
  56: pub struct WindowsMeshStatusOptions {
  57:     pub state_path: Option<PathBuf>,
  58:     /// Peer IDs the orchestrator expects to find in the snapshot. When
  59:     /// provided, missing peers count as drift.
  60:     pub expected_peer_ids: Vec<String>,
  61:     /// If set, snapshots older than this many seconds count as drift. Useful
  62:     /// when the orchestrator wants to confirm the daemon reconciled
  63:     /// post-distribution. `None` disables the freshness check.
  64:     pub max_age_seconds: Option<i64>,
  65: }
  66: 
  67: /// Inspect the runtime snapshot at the configured (or default) state path
  68: /// and return a typed report. Mirrors the W1.2 / W2.4 / W2.1 reporting shape
  69: /// so the orchestrator can drive every Windows security-check subcommand
  70: /// through the same evaluator pattern.
  71: pub fn collect_windows_mesh_status_report(
  72:     options: &WindowsMeshStatusOptions,
  73: ) -> WindowsMeshStatusReport {
  74:     let state_path: PathBuf = options
  75:         .state_path
  76:         .clone()
  77:         .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(DEFAULT_WINDOWS_STATE_PATH));
  78:     let state_path_str = state_path.display().to_string();
  79:     let now_unix = current_unix_seconds();
  80:     let snapshot = match load_session_snapshot(state_path.as_path()) {
  81:         Ok(snap) => {
  82:             let age = now_unix.saturating_sub(snap.timestamp_unix as i64);
  83:             WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Ok {
  84:                 timestamp_unix: snap.timestamp_unix,
  85:                 age_seconds: age,
  86:                 peer_ids: snap.peer_ids,
  87:                 selected_exit_node: snap.selected_exit_node,
  88:                 lan_access_enabled: snap.lan_access_enabled,
  89:             }
  90:         }
  91:         Err(ResilienceError::Io) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Missing {
  92:             reason: format!("runtime state path is unreadable on this host: {state_path_str}"),
  93:         },
  94:         Err(ResilienceError::IntegrityMismatch) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::IntegrityMismatch {
  95:             reason: format!("runtime state file failed integrity verification: {state_path_str}"),
  96:         },
  97:         Err(ResilienceError::InvalidFormat) => WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::InvalidFormat {
  98:             reason: format!(
  99:                 "runtime state file does not match the expected on-disk format: {state_path_str}"
 100:             ),
 101:         },
 102:     };
 103:     let drift_reasons = evaluate_windows_mesh_status(
 104:         &snapshot,
 105:         options.expected_peer_ids.as_slice(),
 106:         options.max_age_seconds,
 107:     );
 108:     let overall_ok = drift_reasons.is_empty();
 109:     WindowsMeshStatusReport {
 110:         schema_version: 1,
 111:         state_path: state_path_str,
 112:         overall_ok,
 113:         snapshot,
 114:         expected_peer_ids: options.expected_peer_ids.clone(),
 115:         max_age_seconds: options.max_age_seconds,
 116:         drift_reasons,
 117:     }
 118: }
 119: 
 120: /// Pure evaluator over a snapshot-load result + expectations. Returns the
 121: /// list of drift reasons (empty = ok). Cross-platform unit-testable.
 122: pub fn evaluate_windows_mesh_status(
 123:     snapshot: &WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad,
 124:     expected_peer_ids: &[String],
 125:     max_age_seconds: Option<i64>,
 126: ) -> Vec<String> {
 127:     let mut reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
 128:     match snapshot {
 129:         WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Missing { reason } => {
 130:             reasons.push(format!("state snapshot missing: {reason}"));
 131:         }
 132:         WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::IntegrityMismatch { reason } => {
 133:             reasons.push(format!("state snapshot integrity mismatch: {reason}"));
 134:         }
 135:         WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::InvalidFormat { reason } => {
 136:             reasons.push(format!("state snapshot invalid format: {reason}"));
 137:         }
 138:         WindowsMeshSnapshotLoad::Ok {
 139:             age_seconds,
 140:             peer_ids,
 141:             ..
 142:         } => {
 143:             if let Some(max_age) = max_age_seconds {
 144:                 if *age_seconds > max_age {
 145:                     reasons.push(format!(
 146:                         "state snapshot is stale: age={age_seconds}s exceeds max_age={max_age}s"
 147:                     ));
 148:                 }
 149:                 if *age_seconds < 0 {
 150:                     reasons.push(format!(
 151:                         "state snapshot has future timestamp: age={age_seconds}s (clock skew or tampered file)"
 152:                     ));
 153:                 }
 154:             }
 155:             for expected in expected_peer_ids {
 156:                 if !peer_ids.iter().any(|p| p == expected) {
 157:                     reasons.push(format!(
 158:                         "expected peer {expected} not present in snapshot peer_ids"
 159:                     ));
 160:                 }
 161:             }
 162:         }
 163:     }
 164:     reasons
 165: }
 166: 
 167: fn current_unix_seconds() -> i64 {
 168:     SystemTime::now()
 169:         .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
 170:         .map(|d| d.as_secs() as i64)
 171:         .unwrap_or(0)
 172: }
 173:

 175: fn ensure_state_path_under_reviewed_root(path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
 176:     crate::windows_paths::validate_windows_runtime_file_path(path, "mesh status state path")
 177: }

 108:     let sddl = inspect_file_sddl(path)
 109:         .map_err(|err| format!("{label} ACL inspection failed ({}): {err}", path.display()))?;
 110:     let is_dir = std::fs::symlink_metadata(path)
 111:         .map_err(|err| format!("{label} metadata read failed ({}): {err}", path.display()))?
 112:         .is_dir();
 113:     evaluate_windows_runtime_acl_sddl(label, sddl.as_str(), is_dir)
 114:         .map_err(|err| format!("{err}: {}", path.display()))
 115: }

 127: /// Validate the canonical Windows runtime root directories at daemon startup.
 128: ///
 129: /// All reviewed roots under `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet` must (a) exist, (b) be
 130: /// directories, (c) carry a protected DACL with no broader-than-reviewed
 131: /// principals, (d) grant LocalSystem and Builtin Administrators, and (e) be
 132: /// owned by LocalSystem, Builtin Administrators, or a service SID.
 133: ///
 134: /// The daemon refuses to start when any root drifts. This is a fail-closed
 135: /// gate; missing roots are treated as drift and rejected. The Windows service
 136: /// installer is responsible for provisioning these roots before the daemon
 137: /// runs.
 138: pub fn validate_windows_runtime_startup_acls() -> Result<(), String> {
 139:     for (path_str, label) in WINDOWS_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ACL_ROOTS {
 140:         let path = Path::new(path_str);
 141:         let metadata = std::fs::symlink_metadata(path).map_err(|err| {
 142:             format!(
 143:                 "{label} must exist before rustynetd starts on Windows ({}): {err}",
 144:                 path.display()
 145:             )
 146:         })?;
 147:         if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() || !metadata.is_dir() {
 148:             return Err(format!(
 149:                 "{label} must be a real directory, not a symlink or file ({})",
 150:                 path.display()
 151:             ));
 152:         }
 153:         validate_windows_runtime_acl(path, label)?;
 154:     }
 155:     Ok(())
 156: }
 157: 
 158: /// Per-root verification result for the Windows runtime ACL diagnostic
 159: /// command. Captures success or the exact failure reason for each reviewed
 160: /// root, so the orchestrator can pinpoint drift without re-parsing free-form
 161: /// daemon errors.
 162: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
 163: #[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
 164: pub enum WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus {
 165:     /// Root exists, is a directory, and ACL evaluation passed.
 166:     Ok,
 167:     /// Root path could not be inspected (typically: missing or non-directory).
 168:     Missing { reason: String },
 169:     /// Root exists but ACL evaluation failed (drifted ACL, wrong owner, etc.).
 170:     Drifted { reason: String },
 171: }
 172: 
 173: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
 174: pub struct WindowsRuntimeAclRootEntry {
 175:     pub label: String,
 176:     pub path: String,
 177:     #[serde(flatten)]
 178:     pub status: WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus,
 179: }
 180: 
 181: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
 182: pub struct WindowsRuntimeAclReport {
 183:     pub schema_version: u32,
 184:     pub overall_ok: bool,
 185:     pub roots: Vec<WindowsRuntimeAclRootEntry>,
 186: }
 187: 
 188: /// Diagnostic walk over the canonical Windows runtime roots. Unlike
 189: /// `validate_windows_runtime_startup_acls`, this collects per-root status
 190: /// instead of failing fast, so a remote orchestrator can render a complete
 191: /// drift report in a single round-trip.
 192: ///
 193: /// The function still returns `overall_ok = false` if any root failed; the
 194: /// caller decides whether to treat that as fatal. The startup gate keeps the
 195: /// fail-fast behavior to refuse daemon launch on the first drift.
 196: pub fn collect_windows_runtime_acl_report() -> WindowsRuntimeAclReport {
 197:     let roots = WINDOWS_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ACL_ROOTS
 198:         .iter()
 199:         .map(|(path_str, label)| {
 200:             let path = Path::new(path_str);
 201:             let status = inspect_runtime_root_status(path, label);
 202:             WindowsRuntimeAclRootEntry {
 203:                 label: (*label).to_string(),
 204:                 path: path.display().to_string(),
 205:                 status,
 206:             }
 207:         })
 208:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 209:     let overall_ok = roots
 210:         .iter()
 211:         .all(|entry| matches!(entry.status, WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok));
 212:     WindowsRuntimeAclReport {
 213:         schema_version: 1,
 214:         overall_ok,
 215:         roots,
 216:     }
 217: }
 218: 
 219: fn inspect_runtime_root_status(path: &Path, label: &str) -> WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus {
 220:     let metadata = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
 221:         Ok(metadata) => metadata,
 222:         Err(err) => {
 223:             return WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Missing {
 224:                 reason: format!(
 225:                     "{label} must exist before rustynetd starts on Windows ({}): {err}",
 226:                     path.display()
 227:                 ),
 228:             };
 229:         }
 230:     };
 231:     if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() || !metadata.is_dir() {
 232:         return WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Missing {
 233:             reason: format!(
 234:                 "{label} must be a real directory, not a symlink or file ({})",
 235:                 path.display()
 236:             ),
 237:         };
 238:     }
 239:     match validate_windows_runtime_acl(path, label) {
 240:         Ok(()) => WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok,
 241:         Err(reason) => WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Drifted { reason },
 242:     }
 243: }
 244: 
 245: const WINDOWS_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ACL_ROOTS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
 246:     (DEFAULT_WINDOWS_STATE_ROOT, "state root"),
 247:     (DEFAULT_WINDOWS_CONFIG_ROOT, "config root"),
 248:     (DEFAULT_WINDOWS_LOG_ROOT, "log root"),
 249:     (DEFAULT_WINDOWS_TRUST_ROOT, "trust root"),
 250:     (DEFAULT_WINDOWS_MEMBERSHIP_ROOT, "membership root"),
 251:     (DEFAULT_WINDOWS_KEYS_ROOT, "keys root"),
 252:     (DEFAULT_WINDOWS_SECRET_ROOT, "secret root"),
 253:     (DEFAULT_WINDOWS_KEY_CUSTODY_ROOT, "key-custody root"),
 254: ];
 255: 
 256: pub(crate) fn evaluate_windows_runtime_acl_sddl(
 257:     label: &str,
 258:     sddl: &str,
 259:     is_dir: bool,
 260: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 261:     evaluate_windows_protected_dacl_sddl(label, sddl, is_dir)?;
 262:     if !sddl_contains_principal(sddl, "SY") {
 263:         return Err(format!("{label} ACL must grant LocalSystem access"));
 264:     }
 265:     if !sddl_contains_principal(sddl, "BA") {
 266:         return Err(format!(
 267:             "{label} ACL must grant Builtin Administrators access"
 268:         ));
 269:     }
 270:     let owner = extract_sddl_owner(sddl)
 271:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("{label} ACL must expose an owner entry in SDDL form"))?;
 272:     if !matches!(owner, "SY" | "BA") && !owner.starts_with("S-1-5-80-") {
 273:         return Err(format!(
 274:             "{label} ACL owner must be LocalSystem, Builtin Administrators, or a service SID; found {owner}"
 275:         ));
 276:     }
 277:     Ok(())
 278: }
 279: 
 280: pub(crate) fn evaluate_windows_local_secret_acl_sddl(
 281:     label: &str,
 282:     sddl: &str,
 283:     is_dir: bool,
 284: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 285:     evaluate_windows_protected_dacl_sddl(label, sddl, is_dir)?;
 286:     if extract_sddl_owner(sddl).is_none() {
 287:         return Err(format!(
 288:             "{label} ACL must expose an owner entry in SDDL form"
 289:         ));
 290:     }
 291:     Ok(())
 292: }
 293: 
 294: fn evaluate_windows_protected_dacl_sddl(
 295:     label: &str,
 296:     sddl: &str,
 297:     is_dir: bool,
 298: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 299:     if !sddl.contains("D:") {
 300:         return Err(format!("{label} must expose a Windows DACL in SDDL form"));
 301:     }
 302:     if is_dir && !sddl.contains("D:P") {
 303:         return Err(format!(
 304:             "{label} must use a protected DACL with inheritance disabled"
 305:         ));
 306:     }
 307:     for principal in FORBIDDEN_WELL_KNOWN_SDDL_PRINCIPALS {
 308:         if sddl_contains_principal(sddl, principal) {
 309:             return Err(format!(
 310:                 "{label} ACL grants a broader-than-reviewed Windows principal ({principal})"
 311:             ));
 312:         }
 313:     }
 314:     Ok(())
 315: }
 316: 
 317: pub fn is_linux_runtime_root_text(text: &str) -> bool {
 318:     LINUX_RUNTIME_ROOTS
 319:         .iter()
 320:         .any(|prefix| text == *prefix || text.starts_with(&format!("{prefix}/")))
 321: }
 322: 
 323: fn normalize_windows_path(path: &Path, label: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
 324:     let text = path.to_string_lossy();
 325:     let normalized = text.replace('/', "\\");
 326:     if normalized.is_empty() {
 327:         return Err(format!("{label} path must not be empty"));
 328:     }
 329:     if is_linux_runtime_root_text(text.as_ref()) {
 330:         return Err(format!(
 331:             "{label} must not use Linux runtime roots on Windows: {}",
 332:             path.display()
 333:         ));
 334:     }
 335:     if normalized.starts_with(r"\\.\pipe\") {
 336:         return Err(format!(
 337:             "{label} must use a filesystem path, not a Windows named pipe: {}",
 338:             path.display()
 339:         ));
 340:     }
 341:     if normalized.starts_with(r"\\") {
 342:         return Err(format!(
 343:             "{label} must not use a remote or UNC filesystem path on Windows: {}",
 344:             path.display()
 345:         ));
 346:     }
 347:     if !looks_like_windows_absolute_path(normalized.as_str()) {
 348:         return Err(format!(
 349:             "{label} must use an absolute Windows path: {}",
 350:             path.display()
 351:         ));
 352:     }
 353:     if normalized
 354:         .split('\\')
 355:         .skip(1)
 356:         .any(|segment| segment == ".." || segment == ".")
 357:     {
 358:         return Err(format!(
 359:             "{label} must not contain parent-directory traversal on Windows: {}",
 360:             path.display()
 361:         ));
 362:     }
 363:     Ok(normalized)
 364: }
 365: 
 366: fn looks_like_windows_absolute_path(text: &str) -> bool {
 367:     let candidate = text.strip_prefix(r"\\?\").unwrap_or(text);
 368:     let bytes = candidate.as_bytes();
 369:     bytes.len() >= 3 && bytes[0].is_ascii_alphabetic() && bytes[1] == b':' && bytes[2] == b'\\'
 370: }
 371: 
 372: fn is_reviewed_runtime_path(normalized: &str) -> bool {
 373:     let lowered = normalized.to_ascii_lowercase();
 374:     // Match the canonical state file (rustynetd.state under the state
 375:     // root) and the state root directory itself.  The bare state root
 376:     // is needed because run_windows_runtime_boundary_check validates
 377:     // it directly via this helper before walking into its subdirs;
 378:     // earlier the bare root was rejected even though every accepted
 379:     // subdir (config/log/trust/membership/keys/secret) lives under it.
 380:     lowered == DEFAULT_WINDOWS_STATE_PATH.to_ascii_lowercase()
 381:         || lowered == DEFAULT_WINDOWS_STATE_ROOT.to_ascii_lowercase()
 382:         || under_reviewed_root(lowered.as_str(), DEFAULT_WINDOWS_CONFIG_ROOT)
 383:         || under_reviewed_root(lowered.as_str(), DEFAULT_WINDOWS_LOG_ROOT)
 384:         || under_reviewed_root(lowered.as_str(), DEFAULT_WINDOWS_TRUST_ROOT)
 385:         || under_reviewed_root(lowered.as_str(), DEFAULT_WINDOWS_MEMBERSHIP_ROOT)
 386:         || under_reviewed_root(lowered.as_str(), DEFAULT_WINDOWS_KEYS_ROOT)
 387:         || under_reviewed_root(lowered.as_str(), DEFAULT_WINDOWS_SECRET_ROOT)
 388: }
 389: 
 390: fn under_reviewed_root(lowered: &str, root: &str) -> bool {
 391:     let root = root.to_ascii_lowercase();
 392:     lowered == root || lowered.starts_with(&format!("{root}\\"))
 393: }
 394: 
 395: fn extract_sddl_owner(sddl: &str) -> Option<&str> {
 396:     let owner_start = sddl.strip_prefix("O:")?;
 397:     let mut owner_len = owner_start.len();
 398:     for marker in ["G:", "D:", "S:"] {
 399:         if let Some(index) = owner_start.find(marker) {
 400:             owner_len = owner_len.min(index);
 401:         }
 402:     }
 403:     Some(&owner_start[..owner_len])
 404: }
 405: 
 406: fn sddl_contains_principal(sddl: &str, principal: &str) -> bool {
 407:     let marker = format!(";;;{principal})");
 408:     sddl.contains(&marker)
 409: }

 720:     #[test]
 721:     fn collect_windows_runtime_acl_report_marks_every_root_off_windows() {
 722:         let report = collect_windows_runtime_acl_report();
 723:         assert_eq!(report.schema_version, 1);
 724:         assert!(
 725:             !report.overall_ok,
 726:             "non-Windows host must not report overall_ok=true"
 727:         );
 728:         assert_eq!(
 729:             report.roots.len(),
 730:             WINDOWS_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ACL_ROOTS.len(),
 731:             "every reviewed root must appear in the diagnostic report"
 732:         );
 733:         for entry in &report.roots {
 734:             assert!(
 735:                 !matches!(entry.status, WindowsRuntimeAclRootStatus::Ok),
 736:                 "non-Windows host must not mark {} as Ok",
 737:                 entry.label
 738:             );
 739:         }
 740:     }
 741: 
 742:     #[test]
 743:     fn windows_runtime_acl_report_overall_ok_requires_all_roots_ok() {

 745:             schema_version: 1,
 746:             overall_ok: true,
 747:             roots: vec![],

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/windows_runtime_boundary.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: use crate::key_material::{
   4:     read_passphrase_file, remove_file_if_present, store_passphrase_in_os_secure_store,
   5: };
   6: use crate::windows_ipc::{
   7:     WindowsLocalIpcRole, WindowsPrivilegedRequest, WindowsPrivilegedResponse,
   8:     call_windows_privileged_request, serve_windows_privileged_request_once, windows_ipc_probe,
   9: };
  10: use crate::windows_paths::{
  11:     validate_windows_runtime_acl, validate_windows_runtime_file_path,
  12:     validate_windows_secret_blob_path,
  13: };
  14: use rustynet_windows_native::inspect_file_sddl;
  15: use serde::Serialize;
  16: use std::fs::OpenOptions;
  17: use std::io::Write;
  18: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
  19: use std::thread;
  20: use std::time::Duration;
  21: 
  22: const DEFAULT_SELF_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS: u64 = 5_000;
  23: const SELF_CHECK_PASSPHRASE: &str = "00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff\n";
  24: 
  25: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
  26: pub struct WindowsRuntimeBoundaryReport {
  27:     pub schema_version: u32,
  28:     pub pipe_path: String,
  29:     pub secret_blob_path: String,
  30:     pub state_root_acl_validated: bool,
  31:     pub secret_root_acl_validated: bool,
  32:     pub secret_round_trip_ok: bool,
  33:     pub ipc_probe_ok: bool,
  34:     pub inspected_acl_path: String,
  35:     pub inspected_acl_sddl: String,
  36: }
  37: 
  38: pub fn run_windows_runtime_boundary_check(
  39:     state_root: &Path,
  40: ) -> Result<WindowsRuntimeBoundaryReport, String> {
  41:     validate_windows_runtime_file_path(state_root, "state root")?;
  42:     validate_windows_runtime_acl(state_root, "state root")?;
  43: 
  44:     let secret_root = state_root.join("secrets");
  45:     validate_windows_runtime_file_path(secret_root.as_path(), "secret root")?;
  46:     validate_windows_runtime_acl(secret_root.as_path(), "secret root")?;
  47: 
  48:     let secret_blob_path = secret_root.join("boundary-check.passphrase.dpapi");
  49:     let pipe_path = PathBuf::from(format!(
  50:         r"\\.\pipe\RustyNet\rustynetd-privileged.check-{}",
  51:         std::process::id()
  52:     ));
  53:     validate_windows_secret_blob_path(
  54:         secret_blob_path.as_path(),
  55:         "boundary check passphrase blob",
  56:     )?;
  57: 
  58:     let mut secret_round_trip_ok = false;
  59:     let mut ipc_probe_ok = false;
  60:     let mut inspected_acl_sddl = String::new();
  61:     let cleanup_path = secret_blob_path.clone();
  62: 
  63:     let run_result = (|| -> Result<(), String> {
  64:         write_plaintext_seed_passphrase(secret_blob_path.as_path())?;
  65:         store_passphrase_in_os_secure_store(secret_blob_path.as_path(), None)?;
  66:         let passphrase = read_passphrase_file(secret_blob_path.as_path())?;
  67:         if passphrase.trim() != SELF_CHECK_PASSPHRASE.trim() {
  68:             return Err("Windows DPAPI passphrase round-trip returned unexpected data".to_string());
  69:         }
  70:         secret_round_trip_ok = true;
  71: 
  72:         let timeout = Duration::from_millis(DEFAULT_SELF_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS);
  73: 
  74:         // The named-pipe server in `serve_windows_privileged_request_once`
  75:         // handles exactly one message and then disconnects.  The boundary
  76:         // check makes two calls (probe + inspect-runtime-path-acl), so
  77:         // each call needs its own freshly-spawned server.  Otherwise the
  78:         // second call hits CallNamedPipeW with ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND
  79:         // because the first call already consumed the only message.
  80:         //
  81:         // For each request: spawn the server, call the request with a
  82:         // retry that absorbs the spawn -> CreateNamedPipeW latency
  83:         // (Windows error 2 means "pipe doesn't exist yet"), then join.
  84: 
  85:         // Step 1: probe
  86:         {
  87:             let pipe_path_for_server = pipe_path.clone();
  88:             let server = thread::spawn(move || {
  89:                 serve_windows_privileged_request_once(
  90:                     pipe_path_for_server.as_path(),
  91:                     WindowsLocalIpcRole::PrivilegedHelper,
  92:                     None,
  93:                     |request| match request {
  94:                         WindowsPrivilegedRequest::Probe { protocol_version } => {
  95:                             Ok(WindowsPrivilegedResponse::ProbeAck { protocol_version })
  96:                         }
  97:                         other => Err(format!(
  98:                             "unexpected request during boundary-check probe: {other:?}"
  99:                         )),
 100:                     },
 101:                 )
 102:             });
 103:             wait_for_pipe_then(timeout, pipe_path.as_path(), || {
 104:                 windows_ipc_probe(
 105:                     pipe_path.as_path(),
 106:                     WindowsLocalIpcRole::PrivilegedHelper,
 107:                     timeout,
 108:                 )
 109:             })?;
 110:             server.join().map_err(|_| {
 111:                 "Windows privileged self-check probe server thread panicked".to_string()
 112:             })??;
 113:             ipc_probe_ok = true;
 114:         }
 115: 
 116:         // Step 2: inspect-runtime-path-acl
 117:         let response = {
 118:             let pipe_path_for_server = pipe_path.clone();
 119:             let secret_blob_for_server = secret_blob_path.clone();
 120:             let server = thread::spawn(move || {
 121:                 serve_windows_privileged_request_once(
 122:                     pipe_path_for_server.as_path(),
 123:                     WindowsLocalIpcRole::PrivilegedHelper,
 124:                     None,
 125:                     |request| match request {
 126:                         WindowsPrivilegedRequest::InspectRuntimePathAcl { path } => {
 127:                             let request_path = PathBuf::from(&path);
 128:                             validate_windows_secret_blob_path(
 129:                                 request_path.as_path(),
 130:                                 "inspect-runtime-path-acl path",
 131:                             )?;
 132:                             if request_path != secret_blob_for_server {
 133:                                 return Err(format!(
 134:                                     "inspect-runtime-path-acl request must stay pinned to the reviewed self-check secret blob {}; got {}",
 135:                                     secret_blob_for_server.display(),
 136:                                     request_path.display()
 137:                                 ));
 138:                             }
 139:                             let sddl =
 140:                                 inspect_file_sddl(request_path.as_path()).map_err(|err| {
 141:                                     format!(
 142:                                         "inspect-runtime-path-acl failed for {}: {err}",
 143:                                         request_path.display()
 144:                                     )
 145:                                 })?;
 146:                             Ok(WindowsPrivilegedResponse::RuntimePathAcl { path, sddl })
 147:                         }
 148:                         other => Err(format!(
 149:                             "unexpected request during boundary-check inspect: {other:?}"
 150:                         )),
 151:                     },
 152:                 )
 153:             });
 154:             let response = wait_for_pipe_then(timeout, pipe_path.as_path(), || {
 155:                 call_windows_privileged_request(
 156:                     pipe_path.as_path(),
 157:                     WindowsLocalIpcRole::PrivilegedHelper,
 158:                     &WindowsPrivilegedRequest::InspectRuntimePathAcl {
 159:                         path: secret_blob_path.display().to_string(),
 160:                     },
 161:                     timeout,
 162:                 )
 163:             })?;
 164:             server.join().map_err(|_| {
 165:                 "Windows privileged self-check inspect server thread panicked".to_string()
 166:             })??;
 167:             response
 168:         };
 169:         match response {
 170:             WindowsPrivilegedResponse::RuntimePathAcl { path, sddl } => {
 171:                 if path != secret_blob_path.display().to_string() {
 172:                     return Err(format!(
 173:                         "inspect-runtime-path-acl response path mismatch: expected {}, got {path}",
 174:                         secret_blob_path.display()
 175:                     ));
 176:                 }
 177:                 inspected_acl_sddl = sddl;
 178:             }
 179:             other => {
 180:                 return Err(format!(
 181:                     "unexpected Windows privileged response during runtime-boundary check: {other:?}",
 182:                 ));
 183:             }
 184:         }
 185: 
 186:         Ok(())
 187:     })();
 188: 
 189:     let cleanup_result = remove_file_if_present(cleanup_path.as_path());
 190:     if let Err(err) = cleanup_result {
 191:         return Err(format!(
 192:             "Windows runtime-boundary check cleanup failed for {}: {err}",
 193:             cleanup_path.display()
 194:         ));
 195:     }
 196:     run_result?;
 197: 
 198:     Ok(WindowsRuntimeBoundaryReport {
 199:         schema_version: 1,
 200:         pipe_path: pipe_path.display().to_string(),
 201:         secret_blob_path: secret_blob_path.display().to_string(),
 202:         state_root_acl_validated: true,
 203:         secret_root_acl_validated: true,
 204:         secret_round_trip_ok,
 205:         ipc_probe_ok,
 206:         inspected_acl_path: secret_blob_path.display().to_string(),
 207:         inspected_acl_sddl,
 208:     })
 209: }
 210: 
 211: /// Run `op` against a freshly-spawned named-pipe server, retrying when the
 212: /// underlying call returns Windows error 2 (ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND).  Used by
 213: /// the boundary check to absorb the spawn -> first CreateNamedPipeW latency
 214: /// without depending on platform-specific filesystem probing.
 215: fn wait_for_pipe_then<T>(
 216:     timeout: Duration,
 217:     pipe_path: &Path,
 218:     mut op: impl FnMut() -> Result<T, String>,
 219: ) -> Result<T, String> {
 220:     let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + timeout.max(Duration::from_secs(1));
 221:     loop {
 222:         match op() {
 223:             Ok(value) => return Ok(value),
 224:             Err(err) if err.contains("Windows error 2") => {
 225:                 if std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
 226:                     return Err(format!(
 227:                         "Windows runtime-boundary check pipe was not ready within {:?}: {} ({err})",
 228:                         timeout,
 229:                         pipe_path.display()
 230:                     ));
 231:                 }
 232:                 thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
 233:             }
 234:             Err(err) => return Err(err),
 235:         }
 236:     }
 237: }
 238: 
 239: fn write_plaintext_seed_passphrase(path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
 240:     let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
 241:         format!(
 242:             "boundary-check passphrase path must include a parent directory: {}",
 243:             path.display()
 244:         )
 245:     })?;
 246:     if path.exists() {
 247:         let metadata = std::fs::symlink_metadata(path).map_err(|err| {
 248:             format!(
 249:                 "inspect boundary-check passphrase seed path failed ({}): {err}",
 250:                 path.display()
 251:             )
 252:         })?;
 253:         if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() || !metadata.is_file() {
 254:             return Err(format!(
 255:                 "boundary-check passphrase seed path must be a regular file when pre-existing: {}",
 256:                 path.display()
 257:             ));
 258:         }
 259:     }
 260:     let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
 261:         .write(true)
 262:         .create(true)
 263:         .truncate(true)
 264:         .open(path)
 265:         .map_err(|err| {
 266:             format!(
 267:                 "create boundary-check passphrase seed failed ({}): {err}",
 268:                 path.display()
 269:             )
 270:         })?;
 271:     file.write_all(SELF_CHECK_PASSPHRASE.as_bytes())
 272:         .map_err(|err| {
 273:             format!(
 274:                 "write boundary-check passphrase seed failed ({}): {err}",
 275:                 path.display()
 276:             )
 277:         })?;
 278:     file.flush().map_err(|err| {
 279:         format!(
 280:             "flush boundary-check passphrase seed failed ({}): {err}",
 281:             path.display()
 282:         )
 283:     })?;
 284:     validate_windows_runtime_acl(parent, "boundary-check secret root")
 285: }

  75:             )),
  76:         }

  90: pub fn select_host_entry(args: &[String]) -> Result<HostEntrySelection, String> {
  91:     let (remaining, service) = strip_windows_service_args(args)?;
  92:     if let Some(service) = service {
  93:         if !remaining.is_empty() {
  94:             return Err(
  95:                 "--windows-service does not accept daemon subcommands or inline daemon flags; use --env-file with RUSTYNETD_DAEMON_ARGS_JSON"
  96:                     .to_string(),
  97:             );
  98:         }
  99:         return Ok(HostEntrySelection::WindowsService(service));
 100:     }
 101:     Ok(HostEntrySelection::Standard(remaining))
 102: }
 103: 
 104: pub fn strip_windows_service_args(
 105:     args: &[String],
 106: ) -> Result<(Vec<String>, Option<WindowsServiceOptions>), String> {
 107:     let mut remaining = Vec::new();
 108:     let mut windows_service = false;
 109:     let mut service_name: Option<String> = None;
 110:     let mut env_file: Option<PathBuf> = None;
 111:     let mut index = 0usize;
 112: 
 113:     while let Some(arg) = args.get(index) {
 114:         match arg.as_str() {
 115:             "--windows-service" => {
 116:                 windows_service = true;
 117:                 index += 1;
 118:             }
 119:             "--service-name" => {
 120:                 let value = args
 121:                     .get(index + 1)
 122:                     .ok_or_else(|| "--service-name requires a value".to_string())?;
 123:                 service_name = Some(value.clone());
 124:                 index += 2;
 125:             }
 126:             "--env-file" => {
 127:                 let value = args
 128:                     .get(index + 1)
 129:                     .ok_or_else(|| "--env-file requires a value".to_string())?;
 130:                 env_file = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
 131:                 index += 2;
 132:             }
 133:             _ => {
 134:                 remaining.push(arg.clone());
 135:                 index += 1;
 136:             }
 137:         }
 138:     }
 139: 
 140:     if !windows_service {
 141:         if service_name.is_some() {
 142:             return Err("--service-name requires --windows-service".to_string());
 143:         }
 144:         if env_file.is_some() {
 145:             return Err("--env-file requires --windows-service".to_string());
 146:         }
 147:         return Ok((remaining, None));
 148:     }
 149: 
 150:     let env_file = env_file.ok_or_else(|| {
 151:         "--windows-service requires --env-file so the Windows SCM host loads reviewed config input"
 152:             .to_string()
 153:     })?;
 154: 
 155:     Ok((
 156:         remaining,
 157:         Some(WindowsServiceOptions {
 158:             service_name: service_name.unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_WINDOWS_SERVICE_NAME.to_string()),
 159:             env_file,
 160:         }),
 161:     ))
 162: }

 164: pub fn prepare_windows_service_host(
 165:     options: &WindowsServiceOptions,
 166: ) -> Result<PreparedWindowsServiceHost, String> {
 167:     validate_windows_runtime_file_path(&options.env_file, "windows service env-file")?;
 168: 
 169:     let runtime_input = load_windows_service_runtime_input(&options.env_file)?;
 170:     let backend_request = classify_windows_backend_request(&runtime_input.daemon_args)?;
 171: 
 172:     Ok(PreparedWindowsServiceHost {
 173:         service_name: options.service_name.clone(),
 174:         env_file: runtime_input.env_file,
 175:         daemon_args: runtime_input.daemon_args,
 176:         backend_request,
 177:     })
 178: }
 179: 
 180: pub fn load_windows_service_runtime_input(
 181:     env_file: &Path,
 182: ) -> Result<WindowsServiceRuntimeInput, String> {
 183:     let bytes = fs::read(env_file).map_err(|err| {
 184:         format!(
 185:             "failed to read Windows service env-file {}: {err}",
 186:             env_file.display()
 187:         )
 188:     })?;
 189:     if bytes.len() > MAX_WINDOWS_ENV_FILE_BYTES {
 190:         return Err(format!(
 191:             "Windows service env-file is too large ({} bytes > {MAX_WINDOWS_ENV_FILE_BYTES})",
 192:             bytes.len()
 193:         ));
 194:     }
 195:     let text = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes)
 196:         .map_err(|err| format!("Windows service env-file must be UTF-8: {err}"))?;
 197:     let variables = parse_windows_env_file(text)?;
 198:     let daemon_args_json = variables
 199:         .get(WINDOWS_SERVICE_DAEMON_ARGS_ENV)
 200:         .ok_or_else(|| {
 201:             format!(
 202:                 "Windows service env-file must define {WINDOWS_SERVICE_DAEMON_ARGS_ENV} as a JSON array of daemon flags"
 203:             )
 204:         })?;
 205:     let daemon_args: Vec<String> = serde_json::from_str(daemon_args_json).map_err(|err| {
 206:         format!("{WINDOWS_SERVICE_DAEMON_ARGS_ENV} must be a JSON array of strings: {err}")
 207:     })?;
 208:     if daemon_args.is_empty() {
 209:         return Err(format!(
 210:             "{WINDOWS_SERVICE_DAEMON_ARGS_ENV} must include at least one daemon flag"
 211:         ));
 212:     }
 213:     Ok(WindowsServiceRuntimeInput {
 214:         env_file: env_file.to_path_buf(),
 215:         variables,
 216:         daemon_args,
 217:     })
 218: }
 219: 
 220: pub fn classify_windows_backend_request(args: &[String]) -> Result<WindowsBackendRequest, String> {
 221:     let mut backend: Option<String> = None;
 222:     let mut index = 0usize;
 223:     while index < args.len() {
 224:         match args.get(index).map(String::as_str) {
 225:             Some("--backend") => {
 226:                 let value = args.get(index + 1).ok_or_else(|| {
 227:                     "--backend in RUSTYNETD_DAEMON_ARGS_JSON requires a value".to_string()
 228:                 })?;
 229:                 if backend.is_some() {
 230:                     return Err(
 231:                         "RUSTYNETD_DAEMON_ARGS_JSON must not specify --backend more than once"
 232:                             .to_string(),
 233:                     );
 234:                 }
 235:                 backend = Some(value.clone());
 236:                 index += 2;
 237:             }
 238:             Some(_) => {
 239:                 index += 1;
 240:             }
 241:             None => break,
 242:         }
 243:     }
 244: 
 245:     let Some(backend) = backend else {
 246:         return Ok(WindowsBackendRequest::Missing);
 247:     };
 248: 
 249:     if matches!(
 250:         backend.as_str(),
 251:         "linux-wireguard"
 252:             | "linux-wireguard-userspace-shared"
 253:             | "macos-wireguard"
 254:             | "macos-wireguard-userspace-shared"
 255:     ) {
 256:         return Ok(WindowsBackendRequest::NonWindows(backend));
 257:     }
 258: 
 259:     match parse_windows_backend_mode(backend.as_str()) {
 260:         Ok(WindowsBackendMode::Unsupported) => Ok(WindowsBackendRequest::ExplicitUnsupported(
 261:             WindowsBackendMode::Unsupported,
 262:         )),
 263:         Ok(mode) => Ok(WindowsBackendRequest::Reviewed(mode)),
 264:         Err(_) => Ok(WindowsBackendRequest::Unknown(backend)),
 265:     }
 266: }
 267: 
 268: fn parse_windows_env_file(text: &str) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, String> {
 269:     let mut variables = BTreeMap::new();
 270:     for (line_number, raw_line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
 271:         let line = raw_line.trim();
 272:         if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {
 273:             continue;
 274:         }
 275:         let (key, value) = line.split_once('=').ok_or_else(|| {
 276:             format!(
 277:                 "invalid Windows service env-file line {}: expected KEY=VALUE",
 278:                 line_number + 1
 279:             )
 280:         })?;
 281:         let key = key.trim();
 282:         if !is_valid_env_key(key) {
 283:             return Err(format!(
 284:                 "invalid Windows service env-file key '{}' on line {}",
 285:                 key,
 286:                 line_number + 1
 287:             ));
 288:         }
 289:         if variables.contains_key(key) {
 290:             return Err(format!(
 291:                 "duplicate Windows service env-file key '{}' on line {}",
 292:                 key,
 293:                 line_number + 1
 294:             ));
 295:         }
 296:         let value = strip_optional_quotes(value.trim())?;
 297:         variables.insert(key.to_string(), value);
 298:     }
 299:     Ok(variables)
 300: }
 301: 
 302: fn is_valid_env_key(key: &str) -> bool {
 303:     let mut chars = key.chars();
 304:     match chars.next() {
 305:         Some(first) if first == '_' || first.is_ascii_alphabetic() => {}
 306:         _ => return false,
 307:     }
 308:     chars.all(|ch| ch == '_' || ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric())
 309: }
 310: 
 311: fn strip_optional_quotes(value: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
 312:     if value.len() >= 2 {
 313:         let first = value.as_bytes()[0];
 314:         let last = value.as_bytes()[value.len() - 1];
 315:         if (first == b'"' && last == b'"') || (first == b'\'' && last == b'\'') {
 316:             return Ok(value[1..value.len() - 1].to_string());
 317:         }
 318:         if first == b'"' || first == b'\'' || last == b'"' || last == b'\'' {
 319:             return Err("mismatched quotes in Windows service env-file value".to_string());
 320:         }
 321:     }
 322:     Ok(value.to_string())
 323: }

 330:     "  windows_service_env=requires RUSTYNETD_DAEMON_ARGS_JSON=[\"--backend\",\"windows-unsupported\"|\"windows-wireguard-nt\",...] in the reviewed env-file; windows-unsupported remains the explicit fail-closed label, while windows-wireguard-nt is opt-in and still outside release-gated support until measured evidence exists"
 331: }

 343:     _prepared: PreparedWindowsServiceHost,
