 349: #[cfg(windows)]
 350: fn run_windows_service_host_impl(
 351:     prepared: PreparedWindowsServiceHost,
 352:     daemon_runner: WindowsDaemonArgsRunner,
 353: ) -> Result<(), String> {
 354:     windows_only::dispatch(prepared, daemon_runner)
 355: }
 356: 
 357: #[cfg(windows)]
 358: mod windows_only {
 359:     use super::{PreparedWindowsServiceHost, WindowsDaemonArgsRunner};
 360:     use std::ffi::OsString;
 361:     use std::sync::OnceLock;
 362:     use std::time::Duration;
 363:     use windows_service::define_windows_service;
 364:     use windows_service::service::{
 365:         ServiceControlAccept, ServiceExitCode, ServiceState, ServiceStatus, ServiceType,
 366:     };
 367:     use windows_service::service_control_handler::{self, ServiceControlHandlerResult};
 368:     use windows_service::service_dispatcher;
 369: 
 370:     struct WindowsServiceHostState {
 371:         prepared: PreparedWindowsServiceHost,
 372:         daemon_runner: WindowsDaemonArgsRunner,
 373:     }
 374: 
 375:     static WINDOWS_SERVICE_HOST: OnceLock<WindowsServiceHostState> = OnceLock::new();
 376: 
 377:     define_windows_service!(ffi_windows_service_main, windows_service_main);
 378: 
 379:     pub(super) fn dispatch(
 380:         prepared: PreparedWindowsServiceHost,
 381:         daemon_runner: WindowsDaemonArgsRunner,
 382:     ) -> Result<(), String> {
 383:         let service_name = prepared.service_name.clone();
 384:         WINDOWS_SERVICE_HOST
 385:             .set(WindowsServiceHostState {
 386:                 prepared,
 387:                 daemon_runner,
 388:             })
 389:             .map_err(|_| "windows service host already initialized in this process".to_string())?;
 390:         service_dispatcher::start(service_name.as_str(), ffi_windows_service_main)
 391:             .map_err(|err| format!("failed to dispatch Windows service host: {err}"))
 392:     }
 393: 
 394:     fn windows_service_main(_arguments: Vec<OsString>) {
 395:         if let Err(err) = run_service_main() {
 396:             eprintln!("rustynetd Windows service host failed: {err}");
 397:         }
 398:     }
 399: 
 400:     fn run_service_main() -> Result<(), String> {
 401:         let state = WINDOWS_SERVICE_HOST
 402:             .get()
 403:             .ok_or_else(|| "missing Windows service host configuration".to_string())?;
 404:         let prepared = &state.prepared;
 405:         super::reset_windows_service_stop_requested();
 406:         let status_handle = service_control_handler::register(
 407:             prepared.service_name.as_str(),
 408:             move |control_event| match control_event {
 409:                 windows_service::service::ServiceControl::Interrogate => {
 410:                     ServiceControlHandlerResult::NoError
 411:                 }
 412:                 windows_service::service::ServiceControl::Stop
 413:                 | windows_service::service::ServiceControl::Shutdown => {
 414:                     super::request_windows_service_stop();
 415:                     ServiceControlHandlerResult::NoError
 416:                 }
 417:                 _ => ServiceControlHandlerResult::NotImplemented,
 418:             },
 419:         )
 420:         .map_err(|err| format!("failed to register Windows service control handler: {err}"))?;
 421: 
 422:         status_handle
 423:             .set_service_status(ServiceStatus {
 424:                 service_type: ServiceType::OWN_PROCESS,
 425:                 current_state: ServiceState::StartPending,
 426:                 controls_accepted: ServiceControlAccept::empty(),
 427:                 exit_code: ServiceExitCode::Win32(0),
 428:                 checkpoint: 1,
 429:                 wait_hint: Duration::from_secs(10),
 430:                 process_id: None,
 431:             })
 432:             .map_err(|err| {
 433:                 format!("failed to report Windows service start-pending status: {err}")
 434:             })?;
 435: 
 436:         if let Some(blocker) = prepared.backend_request.blocker_reason() {
 437:             status_handle
 438:                 .set_service_status(ServiceStatus {
 439:                     service_type: ServiceType::OWN_PROCESS,
 440:                     current_state: ServiceState::Stopped,
 441:                     controls_accepted: ServiceControlAccept::empty(),
 442:                     exit_code: ServiceExitCode::Win32(1),
 443:                     checkpoint: 0,
 444:                     wait_hint: Duration::default(),
 445:                     process_id: None,
 446:                 })
 447:                 .map_err(|err| format!("failed to report Windows service stopped status: {err}"))?;
 448:             return Err(blocker);
 449:         }
 450: 
 451:         status_handle
 452:             .set_service_status(ServiceStatus {
 453:                 service_type: ServiceType::OWN_PROCESS,
 454:                 current_state: ServiceState::Running,
 455:                 controls_accepted: ServiceControlAccept::STOP | ServiceControlAccept::SHUTDOWN,
 456:                 exit_code: ServiceExitCode::Win32(0),
 457:                 checkpoint: 0,
 458:                 wait_hint: Duration::default(),
 459:                 process_id: None,
 460:             })
 461:             .map_err(|err| format!("failed to report Windows service running status: {err}"))?;
 462: 
 463:         let daemon_runner = state.daemon_runner;
 464:         let daemon_args = prepared.daemon_args.clone();
 465:         let daemon_thread = std::thread::spawn(move || daemon_runner(&daemon_args));
 466:         let mut stop_pending_reported = false;
 467:         while !daemon_thread.is_finished() {
 468:             if super::windows_service_stop_requested() && !stop_pending_reported {
 469:                 status_handle
 470:                     .set_service_status(ServiceStatus {
 471:                         service_type: ServiceType::OWN_PROCESS,
 472:                         current_state: ServiceState::StopPending,
 473:                         controls_accepted: ServiceControlAccept::empty(),
 474:                         exit_code: ServiceExitCode::Win32(0),
 475:                         checkpoint: 1,
 476:                         wait_hint: Duration::from_secs(20),
 477:                         process_id: None,
 478:                     })
 479:                     .map_err(|err| {
 480:                         format!("failed to report Windows service stop-pending status: {err}")
 481:                     })?;
 482:                 stop_pending_reported = true;
 483:             }
 484:             std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200));
 485:         }
 486: 
 487:         let result = daemon_thread
 488:             .join()
 489:             .map_err(|_| "rustynetd Windows service daemon thread panicked".to_string())?;
 490:         let exit_code = if result.is_ok() { 0 } else { 1 };
 491:         status_handle
 492:             .set_service_status(ServiceStatus {
 493:                 service_type: ServiceType::OWN_PROCESS,
 494:                 current_state: ServiceState::Stopped,
 495:                 controls_accepted: ServiceControlAccept::empty(),
 496:                 exit_code: ServiceExitCode::Win32(exit_code),
 497:                 checkpoint: 0,
 498:                 wait_hint: Duration::default(),
 499:                 process_id: None,
 500:             })
 501:             .map_err(|err| format!("failed to report Windows service stopped status: {err}"))?;
 502: 
 503:         result
 504:     }
 505: }

===== /crates/rustynetd/src/windows_service_hardening.rs =====

   1: #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
   2: 
   3: //! Windows Service hardening verifier.
   4: //!
   5: //! Checks that the live `RustyNet` Windows service registration matches the
   6: //! reviewed hardened profile (binary path under reviewed install root,
   7: //! argv-only `--windows-service --env-file` invocation, restricted service
   8: //! SID, non-interactive desktop, recovery action present, locked-down binary
   9: //! ACL). The orchestrator dispatches the `windows-service-hardening-check`
  10: //! subcommand on a remote Windows guest and parses the typed JSON report
  11: //! produced here.
  12: //!
  13: //! The pure `evaluate_windows_service_hardening` function takes a typed
  14: //! snapshot and returns a precise drift reason. The collector
  15: //! (`collect_windows_service_hardening_snapshot`) is platform-gated: real on
  16: //! Windows via the `windows-service` crate plus `inspect_file_sddl`, stub on
  17: //! non-Windows hosts that returns a clear blocker error.
  18: 
  19: use crate::windows_paths::evaluate_windows_runtime_acl_sddl;
  20: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  21: 
  22: pub const REVIEWED_WINDOWS_SERVICE_NAME: &str = "RustyNet";
  23: pub const REVIEWED_WINDOWS_INSTALL_ROOT: &str = r"C:\Program Files\RustyNet";
  24: pub const REVIEWED_WINDOWS_BINARY_FILE_NAME: &str = "rustynetd.exe";
  25: 
  26: /// Allowed service SID types for the reviewed hardened profile. SID type
  27: /// `None` is rejected because it removes the per-service SID isolation that
  28: /// the reviewed install relies on.
  29: const REVIEWED_SERVICE_SID_TYPES: &[&str] = &["unrestricted", "restricted"];
  30: 
  31: /// Allowed account names. Reviewed install runs as LocalSystem; service
  32: /// accounts in the `NT SERVICE\` namespace are also accepted because they
  33: /// represent dedicated virtual SIDs. Anything else (Administrator, custom
  34: /// users) is rejected.
  35: const REVIEWED_ACCOUNT_PREFIXES: &[&str] = &["nt service\\"];
  36: const REVIEWED_ACCOUNT_NAMES: &[&str] = &["localsystem"];
  37: 
  38: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  39: pub struct WindowsServiceHardeningSnapshot {
  40:     pub schema_version: u32,
  41:     pub service_name: String,
  42:     /// Raw `ImagePath` as stored in the SCM registration. Free-form for
  43:     /// diagnostic carry-through; normative checks consume `binary_image_argv`.
  44:     pub binary_image_path: String,
  45:     /// Argv parsed from `binary_image_path`, with the executable as
  46:     /// `argv[0]`. Empty if parsing failed.
  47:     pub binary_image_argv: Vec<String>,
  48:     pub start_name: String,
  49:     /// Service SID type label: `none`, `unrestricted`, or `restricted`.
  50:     pub service_sid_type: String,
  51:     /// Service start type label: `auto_start`, `demand_start`, etc.
  52:     pub start_type: String,
  53:     /// True if the service registration carries `SERVICE_INTERACTIVE_PROCESS`.
  54:     pub interactive_process: bool,
  55:     /// Number of failure actions configured. Zero means the service has no
  56:     /// recovery configuration, which the hardened profile rejects.
  57:     pub failure_action_count: u32,
  58:     /// SDDL of the binary file's DACL. Validated with the same
  59:     /// `evaluate_windows_runtime_acl_sddl` evaluator W1.1 uses.
  60:     pub binary_path_acl_sddl: String,
  61: }
  62: 
  63: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  64: pub struct WindowsServiceHardeningReport {
  65:     pub schema_version: u32,
  66:     pub overall_ok: bool,
  67:     pub snapshot: WindowsServiceHardeningSnapshot,
  68:     /// Empty when `overall_ok=true`; otherwise a list of every drift reason
  69:     /// the evaluator produced for this snapshot. The orchestrator surfaces
  70:     /// every reason in the live-lab failure record.
  71:     pub drift_reasons: Vec<String>,
  72: }
  73: 
  74: /// Pure evaluator over a snapshot. Returns `Ok(())` when the snapshot
  75: /// satisfies every reviewed-profile rule; otherwise returns a `Vec<String>`
  76: /// of every drift reason found.
  77: pub fn evaluate_windows_service_hardening(
  78:     snapshot: &WindowsServiceHardeningSnapshot,
  79: ) -> Result<(), Vec<String>> {
  80:     let mut reasons: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
  81: 
  82:     if snapshot.schema_version != 1 {
  83:         reasons.push(format!(
  84:             "service hardening snapshot has unsupported schema_version={}",
  85:             snapshot.schema_version
  86:         ));
  87:     }
  88: 
  89:     if snapshot.service_name != REVIEWED_WINDOWS_SERVICE_NAME {
  90:         reasons.push(format!(
  91:             "service name must be {REVIEWED_WINDOWS_SERVICE_NAME}; found {:?}",
  92:             snapshot.service_name
  93:         ));
  94:     }
  95: 
  96:     if snapshot.binary_image_argv.is_empty() {
  97:         reasons.push(format!(
  98:             "service binary image path failed to parse into argv: {:?}",
  99:             snapshot.binary_image_path
 100:         ));
 101:     } else {
 102:         let exe_path = &snapshot.binary_image_argv[0];
 103:         let lowered = exe_path.to_ascii_lowercase().replace('/', "\\");
 104:         let install_root_lower = REVIEWED_WINDOWS_INSTALL_ROOT.to_ascii_lowercase();
 105:         if !lowered.starts_with(&format!("{install_root_lower}\\")) {
 106:             reasons.push(format!(
 107:                 "service binary path must live under {REVIEWED_WINDOWS_INSTALL_ROOT}; found {exe_path}"
 108:             ));
 109:         }
 110:         if !lowered.ends_with(&format!(
 111:             "\\{}",
 112:             REVIEWED_WINDOWS_BINARY_FILE_NAME.to_ascii_lowercase()
 113:         )) {
 114:             reasons.push(format!(
 115:                 "service binary path must end with {REVIEWED_WINDOWS_BINARY_FILE_NAME}; found {exe_path}"
 116:             ));
 117:         }
 118: 
 119:         let argv_tail = &snapshot.binary_image_argv[1..];
 120:         if !argv_tail.iter().any(|arg| arg == "--windows-service") {
 121:             reasons.push(
 122:                 "service argv must include --windows-service so the SCM host path is taken"
 123:                     .to_string(),
 124:             );
 125:         }
 126:         if !argv_tail.iter().any(|arg| arg == "--env-file") {
 127:             reasons.push(
 128:                 "service argv must include --env-file so daemon args are read from the reviewed env-file (no inline daemon flags)"
 129:                     .to_string(),
 130:             );
 131:         }
 132:         for arg in argv_tail {
 133:             if arg.starts_with("--")
 134:                 && arg != "--windows-service"
 135:                 && arg != "--env-file"
 136:                 && arg != "--service-name"
 137:             {
 138:                 reasons.push(format!(
 139:                     "service argv must not include inline daemon flags; found {arg}"
 140:                 ));
 141:             }
 142:         }
 143:     }
 144: 
 145:     let start_name_lower = snapshot.start_name.to_ascii_lowercase();
 146:     let start_name_ok = REVIEWED_ACCOUNT_NAMES.contains(&start_name_lower.as_str())
 147:         || REVIEWED_ACCOUNT_PREFIXES
 148:             .iter()
 149:             .any(|prefix| start_name_lower.starts_with(prefix));
 150:     if !start_name_ok {
 151:         reasons.push(format!(
 152:             "service must run as LocalSystem or an NT SERVICE\\* virtual account; found {:?}",
 153:             snapshot.start_name
 154:         ));
 155:     }
 156: 
 157:     let sid_type_lower = snapshot.service_sid_type.to_ascii_lowercase();
 158:     if !REVIEWED_SERVICE_SID_TYPES.contains(&sid_type_lower.as_str()) {
 159:         reasons.push(format!(
 160:             "service SID type must be one of {:?}; found {:?}",
 161:             REVIEWED_SERVICE_SID_TYPES, snapshot.service_sid_type
 162:         ));
 163:     }
 164: 
 165:     if snapshot.interactive_process {
 166:         reasons.push(
 167:             "service must not carry SERVICE_INTERACTIVE_PROCESS; the hardened profile is non-interactive"
 168:                 .to_string(),
 169:         );
 170:     }
 171: 
 172:     if snapshot.failure_action_count == 0 {
 173:         reasons.push(
 174:             "service must have at least one configured failure action so the SCM can recover the daemon after crash"
 175:                 .to_string(),
 176:         );
 177:     }
 178: 
 179:     if snapshot.binary_path_acl_sddl.trim().is_empty() {
 180:         reasons.push("service binary ACL SDDL is empty; cannot verify lockdown".to_string());
 181:     } else if let Err(err) = evaluate_windows_runtime_acl_sddl(
 182:         "service binary",
 183:         snapshot.binary_path_acl_sddl.as_str(),
 184:         false,
 185:     ) {
 186:         reasons.push(format!("service binary ACL drift: {err}"));
 187:     }
 188: 
 189:     if reasons.is_empty() {
 190:         Ok(())
 191:     } else {
 192:         Err(reasons)
 193:     }
 194: }
 195: 
 196: /// Combine snapshot + evaluation into a single report suitable for emission
 197: /// over the orchestrator dispatch path.
 198: pub fn build_windows_service_hardening_report(
 199:     snapshot: WindowsServiceHardeningSnapshot,
 200: ) -> WindowsServiceHardeningReport {
 201:     let drift_reasons = match evaluate_windows_service_hardening(&snapshot) {
 202:         Ok(()) => Vec::new(),
 203:         Err(reasons) => reasons,
 204:     };
 205:     WindowsServiceHardeningReport {
 206:         schema_version: 1,
 207:         overall_ok: drift_reasons.is_empty(),
 208:         snapshot,
 209:         drift_reasons,
 210:     }
 211: }
 212: 
 213: /// Best-effort argv split for a Windows ImagePath string. Handles a single
 214: /// double-quoted executable path followed by space-separated args. Does not
 215: /// implement full Windows command-line escaping; that is acceptable because
 216: /// the reviewed install always emits a quoted exe followed by simple flag
 217: /// tokens.
 218: pub fn parse_windows_image_path_argv(image_path: &str) -> Vec<String> {
 219:     let trimmed = image_path.trim();
 220:     if trimmed.is_empty() {
 221:         return Vec::new();
 222:     }
 223:     let mut argv: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
 224:     let mut chars = trimmed.chars().peekable();
 225:     let mut current = String::new();
 226:     let mut in_quotes = false;
 227:     while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
 228:         match ch {
 229:             '"' => {
 230:                 in_quotes = !in_quotes;
 231:             }
 232:             ch if ch.is_whitespace() && !in_quotes => {
 233:                 if !current.is_empty() {
 234:                     argv.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
 235:                 }
 236:                 while matches!(chars.peek(), Some(next) if next.is_whitespace()) {
 237:                     chars.next();
 238:                 }
 239:             }
 240:             _ => current.push(ch),
 241:         }
 242:     }
 243:     if !current.is_empty() {
 244:         argv.push(current);
 245:     }
 246:     argv
 247: }
 248: 
 249: /// Collect the live snapshot. On Windows, queries the SCM via the
 250: /// `windows-service` crate and inspects the binary file ACL via
 251: /// `rustynet_windows_native::inspect_file_sddl`. On other platforms, returns
 252: /// a clear blocker error so the subcommand still fails-closed without
 253: /// pretending to verify.
 254: pub fn collect_windows_service_hardening_snapshot()
 255: -> Result<WindowsServiceHardeningSnapshot, String> {
 256:     #[cfg(not(windows))]
 257:     {
 258:         Err(
 259:             "windows-service-hardening-check is only available on Windows hosts; the snapshot collector requires Win32 SCM access"
 260:                 .to_string(),
 261:         )
 262:     }
 263:     #[cfg(windows)]
 264:     {
 265:         windows_collector::collect()
 266:     }
 267: }
 268: 
 269: #[cfg(windows)]
 270: mod windows_collector {
 271:     use super::{
 272:         REVIEWED_WINDOWS_SERVICE_NAME, WindowsServiceHardeningSnapshot,
 273:         parse_windows_image_path_argv,
 274:     };
 275:     use rustynet_windows_native::inspect_file_sddl;
 276:     use std::path::Path;
 277:     use windows_service::service::{ServiceAccess, ServiceSidType, ServiceStartType};
 278:     use windows_service::service_manager::{ServiceManager, ServiceManagerAccess};
 279: 
 280:     pub(super) fn collect() -> Result<WindowsServiceHardeningSnapshot, String> {
 281:         let manager = ServiceManager::local_computer(None::<&str>, ServiceManagerAccess::CONNECT)
 282:             .map_err(|err| format!("open SCM failed: {err}"))?;
 283:         let service = manager
 284:             .open_service(
 285:                 REVIEWED_WINDOWS_SERVICE_NAME,
 286:                 ServiceAccess::QUERY_CONFIG | ServiceAccess::QUERY_STATUS,
 287:             )
 288:             .map_err(|err| format!("open service {REVIEWED_WINDOWS_SERVICE_NAME} failed: {err}"))?;
 289:         let config = service
 290:             .query_config()
 291:             .map_err(|err| format!("query service config failed: {err}"))?;
 292:         let sid_type = service
 293:             .get_config_service_sid_info()
 294:             .map_err(|err| format!("query service SID info failed: {err}"))?;
 295:         let failure_actions = service
 296:             .get_failure_actions()
 297:             .map_err(|err| format!("query service failure actions failed: {err}"))?;
 298:         let interactive_process = config
 299:             .service_type
 300:             .contains(windows_service::service::ServiceType::INTERACTIVE_PROCESS);
 301:         let image_path = config.executable_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();
 302:         let argv = parse_windows_image_path_argv(image_path.as_str());
 303:         let start_name = config
 304:             .account_name
 305:             .as_ref()
 306:             .map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().to_string())
 307:             .unwrap_or_else(|| "LocalSystem".to_string());
 308:         let binary_path_acl_sddl = if let Some(exe) = argv.first() {
 309:             inspect_file_sddl(Path::new(exe.as_str()))
 310:                 .map_err(|err| format!("inspect service binary ACL failed for {exe}: {err}"))?
 311:         } else {
 312:             String::new()
 313:         };
 314:         Ok(WindowsServiceHardeningSnapshot {
 315:             schema_version: 1,
 316:             service_name: REVIEWED_WINDOWS_SERVICE_NAME.to_string(),
 317:             binary_image_path: image_path,
 318:             binary_image_argv: argv,
 319:             start_name,
 320:             service_sid_type: service_sid_type_label(sid_type).to_string(),
 321:             start_type: service_start_type_label(config.start_type).to_string(),
 322:             interactive_process,
 323:             failure_action_count: failure_actions
 324:                 .actions
 325:                 .as_ref()
 326:                 .map(|v| v.len() as u32)
 327:                 .unwrap_or(0),
 328:             binary_path_acl_sddl,
 329:         })
 330:     }
 331: 
 332:     fn service_sid_type_label(value: ServiceSidType) -> &'static str {
 333:         match value {
 334:             ServiceSidType::None => "none",
 335:             ServiceSidType::Unrestricted => "unrestricted",
 336:             ServiceSidType::Restricted => "restricted",
 337:         }
 338:     }
 339: 
 340:     fn service_start_type_label(value: ServiceStartType) -> &'static str {
 341:         match value {
 342:             ServiceStartType::AutoStart => "auto_start",
 343:             ServiceStartType::OnDemand => "demand_start",
 344:             ServiceStartType::Disabled => "disabled",
 345:             ServiceStartType::SystemStart => "system_start",
 346:             ServiceStartType::BootStart => "boot_start",
 347:         }
 348:     }
 349: }

  77: fn fetcher_all_four_types_skip_when_url_unset() {
  78:     let dir = tempdir().unwrap();
  79:     let cfg = make_test_config(dir.path());
  80: 
  81:     let fetcher = StateFetcher::new_from_daemon(&cfg);
  82: 
  83:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_trust().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
  84:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_traversal().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
  85:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_assignment().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
  86:     assert_eq!(

  88:         FetchDecision::Skipped
  89:     );
  90: }

  92: #[test]
  93: fn fetcher_all_four_types_skip_when_remote_urls_are_configured() {
  94:     let dir = tempdir().unwrap();
  95:     let mut cfg = make_test_config(dir.path());
  96:     cfg.trust_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1/trust".to_string());
  97:     cfg.traversal_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1/traversal".to_string());
  98:     cfg.assignment_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1/assignment".to_string());
  99:     cfg.dns_zone_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1/dns".to_string());
 100: 
 101:     let fetcher = StateFetcher::new_from_daemon(&cfg);
 102: 
 103:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_trust().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
 104:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_traversal().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
 105:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_assignment().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
 106:     assert_eq!(
 107:         fetcher.fetch_dns_zone(None).unwrap(),
 108:         FetchDecision::Skipped
 109:     );
 110:     assert!(!cfg.trust_evidence_path.exists());
 111:     assert!(!cfg.trust_watermark_path.exists());
 112:     assert!(!cfg.traversal_bundle_path.exists());
 113:     assert!(!cfg.traversal_watermark_path.exists());
 114:     assert!(!cfg.dns_zone_bundle_path.exists());
 115:     assert!(!cfg.dns_zone_watermark_path.exists());
 116:     assert!(!cfg.auto_tunnel_bundle_path.as_ref().unwrap().exists());
 117:     assert!(!cfg.auto_tunnel_watermark_path.as_ref().unwrap().exists());
 118: }

 120: #[test]
 121: fn fetcher_skip_does_not_overwrite_existing_local_artifacts() {
 122:     let dir = tempdir().unwrap();
 123:     let mut cfg = make_test_config(dir.path());
 124:     cfg.trust_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1/trust".to_string());
 125:     cfg.traversal_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1/traversal".to_string());
 126:     cfg.assignment_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1/assignment".to_string());
 127:     cfg.dns_zone_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1/dns".to_string());
 128: 
 129:     fs::write(&cfg.trust_evidence_path, "trust-sentinel").unwrap();
 130:     fs::write(&cfg.traversal_bundle_path, "traversal-sentinel").unwrap();
 131:     fs::write(&cfg.dns_zone_bundle_path, "dns-sentinel").unwrap();
 132:     fs::write(
 133:         cfg.auto_tunnel_bundle_path.as_ref().unwrap(),
 134:         "assignment-sentinel",
 135:     )
 136:     .unwrap();
 137: 
 138:     let fetcher = StateFetcher::new_from_daemon(&cfg);
 139: 
 140:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_trust().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
 141:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_traversal().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
 142:     assert_eq!(fetcher.fetch_assignment().unwrap(), FetchDecision::Skipped);
 143:     assert_eq!(
 144:         fetcher.fetch_dns_zone(None).unwrap(),
 145:         FetchDecision::Skipped
 146:     );
 147:     assert_eq!(
 148:         fs::read_to_string(&cfg.trust_evidence_path).unwrap(),
 149:         "trust-sentinel"
 150:     );
 151:     assert_eq!(
 152:         fs::read_to_string(&cfg.traversal_bundle_path).unwrap(),
 153:         "traversal-sentinel"
 154:     );
 155:     assert_eq!(
 156:         fs::read_to_string(&cfg.dns_zone_bundle_path).unwrap(),
 157:         "dns-sentinel"
 158:     );
 159:     assert_eq!(
 160:         fs::read_to_string(cfg.auto_tunnel_bundle_path.as_ref().unwrap()).unwrap(),
 161:         "assignment-sentinel"
 162:     );
 163:     assert!(!cfg.trust_watermark_path.exists());
 164:     assert!(!cfg.traversal_watermark_path.exists());
 165:     assert!(!cfg.dns_zone_watermark_path.exists());
 166:     assert!(!cfg.auto_tunnel_watermark_path.as_ref().unwrap().exists());
 167: }
